title: 44 Harsh Truths About The Game Of Life – Naval Ravikant
speaker: Chris Williamson & Naval Ravikant

sentences.en: happiness is being satisfied with what you have.
sentences.zh: 幸福就是对你所拥有的感到满意。

sentences.en: Success comes from dissatisfaction. Is success worth it then?
sentences.zh: 成功来自于不满足。那成功还值得吗？

sentences.en: Oof. I'm not sure that statement is true anymore.
sentences.zh: 呃。我不确定这种说法现在是否还成立。

sentences.en: Like I made that statement a long time ago.
sentences.zh: 就像我很久以前说过的那样。

sentences.en: And a lot of these things are just notes to myself and they're highly contextual.
sentences.zh: 而且其中很多话只是我给自己的笔记，它们具有高度的情境性。

sentences.en: They come in the moment, they leave in the moment.
sentences.zh: 它们因时而生，也随风而去。

sentences.en: Happiness, okay. So very complicated topic, but I always liked the Socrates story where he goes into the marketplace and they show him all these luxuries and fineries.
sentences.zh: 幸福，好吧。这是一个非常复杂的话题，但我一直很喜欢苏格拉底的故事：他走进集市，人们向他展示各种奢侈品和精美物件。

sentences.en: And he says, how many things there are in this world that I do not want, right?
sentences.zh: 他说，这世上有多少东西是我不想要的啊，对吧？

sentences.en: And that's a form of freedom. So not wanting something is as good as having it.
sentences.zh: 这也是一种自由。所以，不想要某样东西就等于拥有它。

sentences.en: In the old story with Alexander Dionysius, right?
sentences.zh: 就像亚历山大和狄奥尼修斯的那个老故事一样，对吧？

sentences.en: Alexander goes out and conquers the world and he meets Dionysius who's living in a barrel.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大外出征服世界，他遇到了住在木桶里的狄奥尼修斯。

sentences.en: And Dionysius says, get out of the way, you're blocking my son.
sentences.zh: 狄奥尼修斯说，让开，你挡住我的阳光了。

sentences.en: And Alexander says, oh, how I wish I could be like Dionysius in the next life.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大说，哦，我多么希望下辈子能成为狄奥尼修斯啊。

sentences.en: And Dionysius says, that's the difference.
sentences.zh: 狄奥尼修斯说，这就是区别。

sentences.en: I don't wish that I could, sorry, Diogenes, Diogenes. diogenes says i i don't wish to be alexander so two paths to happiness and uh one path is success you get what you want you satisfy your material needs or like diogenes you just don't want it in the first place and i'm not sure which one is more valid um and it also depends what you define success if the end goal is happiness then why not cut to the chase and just go straight for it.
sentences.zh: 我才不希望……抱歉，是第欧根尼，第欧根尼。第欧根尼说，我不想成为亚历山大。所以通往幸福有两条路，呃，一条路是成功，你得到了你想要的，满足了你的物质需求；或者像第欧根尼那样，你一开始就不想要。我不确定哪一条更有效，嗯，这还取决于你如何定义成功。如果终极目标是幸福，那为什么不直奔主题，直接去追求它呢？

sentences.en: Does being happy make you less successful?
sentences.zh: 快乐会让你变得不那么成功吗？

sentences.en: That is a conventional wisdom. That may even be the practical earned experience of your reality.
sentences.zh: 那是传统观念。这甚至可能是你现实中通过实践得出的经验。

sentences.en: You find that when you're happy, you don't want anything, so you don't get up and do anything.
sentences.zh: 你会发现，当你快乐时，你无欲无求，所以你不会起床去做任何事。

sentences.en: On the other hand, you still got to do something.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，你总得做点什么。

sentences.en: You're an animal. You're here. You're here to survive.
sentences.zh: 你是个动物。你活在这里。你来到这里是为了生存。

sentences.en: You're here to replicate. You're driven.
sentences.zh: 你来到这里是为了繁衍。你是有驱动力的。

sentences.en: You're motivated. You're going to do something.
sentences.zh: 你是有动力的。你总得做点什么。

sentences.en: You're not just going to sit there all day.
sentences.zh: 你不可能整天就坐在那里。

sentences.en: Unlikely. Some people do. Maybe it's in their nature.
sentences.zh: 不大可能。有些人会这样。也许这是他们的天性。

sentences.en: But I think most people still want to act.
sentences.zh: 但我认为大多数人仍然想采取行动。

sentences.en: They want to live in the arena. I found for myself as I've become happier is a big word, but you know, more peaceful, more calm, more present, more satisfied with what I have.
sentences.zh: 他们想活在竞技场里。我发现，随着我变得更快乐——“快乐”这个词有点大，但你知道的，更平和、更平静、更当下、对自己所拥有的更满意——

sentences.en: I still want to do things. I just want to do bigger things.
sentences.zh: 我依然想做事情。我只是想做更大的事情。

sentences.en: I want to do things that are more pure, more aligned with what I think needs to be done and what I can uniquely do.
sentences.zh: 我想做更纯粹的事情，做那些更符合我内代理应去做、且唯有我能独特完成的事情。

sentences.en: So in that sense, I think that being happier can actually make you more successful, but your definition of success will likely change along the way.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种意义上，我认为更快乐实际上能让你更成功，但你对成功的定义可能会在这个过程中发生改变。

sentences.en: Is that a realization you think you could have gotten to had you have not had some success in the first place?
sentences.zh: 你觉得，如果不是先取得了一些成功，你能悟出这个道理吗？

sentences.en: At least for me, I always wanted to take the path of material success first.
sentences.zh: 至少对我和来说，我总是想先走物质成功这条路。

sentences.en: I was not going to go be an ascetic and sit there and renounce everything.
sentences.zh: 我可不会去当苦行僧，坐在那儿斩断一切欲望。

sentences.en: That just seems too unrealistic and too painful.
sentences.zh: 那显得太不切实际，也太痛苦了。

sentences.en: In the story of Buddha, he starts out as a prince, and then he sees that it's all kind of meaningless because you're still going to get old and die, and then he goes into the woods looking for something more.
sentences.zh: 在佛陀的故事里，他一开始是个王子，然后他发现这一切都毫无意义，因为你终究会变老并死去，于是他走进森林去寻找更多东西。

sentences.en: I'll take the happy route that involves material success.
sentences.zh: 我会选择那条通往物质成功的快乐之路。

sentences.en: Thank you. I think it's quicker in some ways.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。我觉得某种程度上它更快。

sentences.en: One of your insights is it's far easier to achieve our material desires than it is to renounce them.
sentences.zh: 你的见解之一是：实现我们的物质欲望，远比放弃它们要容易得多。

sentences.en: It depends on the person, but I think you have to try that path.
sentences.zh: 这因人而异，但我认为你必须去尝试那条路。

sentences.en: If you want something, go get it.
sentences.zh: 如果你想要什么，就去争取吧。

sentences.en: I quipped that the reason to win the game is to be free of it. so you you play the games you win the games and then you get hopefully you get bored of the games you don't want to just keep looping on the same game over and over although a lot of these games are very enticing and have many levels and are relatively open-ended and then you become free of the game in a sense that you're no longer trying to win it you know you can win it and either you move to a different game or you play the game for the sheer joy of it yeah you another one of yours most of the gains in life come from suffering in the short term so you can get paid in the long term.
sentences.zh: 我曾打趣说，赢得这场游戏的理由，就是为了从中获得自由。所以你参与游戏，赢得游戏，然后希望你对游戏感到厌倦，你不想一直在同一个游戏里不断死循环，尽管其中很多游戏非常诱人、有很多关卡且相对开放，接着你从游戏中解放出来，某种意义上你不再试图去赢得它——你知道你能赢，要么你换个不同的游戏，要么你纯粹为了乐趣而玩这个游戏。对，没错。你的另一个观点是：生活中的大部分收获都来自于短期的痛苦，这样你才能在长期获得回报。

sentences.en: I think that's classic. Winning the marshmallow test on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是经典理论。每天都在通过“棉花糖实验”。

sentences.en: But there's an interesting challenge where I think people need to avoid becoming... a suffering addict, sort of using suffering as the proxy for progress as opposed to the outcome of the suffering, right?
sentences.zh: 但这里有一个有趣的挑战，我认为人们需要避免变成……一个“痛苦上瘾者”，某种程度上把痛苦当作衡量进步的代理指标，而不是把痛苦带来的结果当作指标，对吧？

sentences.en: It's like I was in pain, not eating the marshmallow.
sentences.zh: 就像我为了不吃棉花糖而感到痛苦。

sentences.en: I was in pain doing this work. I have attached well-being and satisfaction to pain, not to what the pain gets me on the other side of it.
sentences.zh: 我做这项工作时感到痛苦。我把幸福感和满足感绑定在了痛苦上，而不是绑定在痛苦换来的结果上。

sentences.en: If you define pain as physical pain, then it's a real thing.
sentences.zh: 如果你把痛苦定义为身体上的痛楚，那它是真实存在的。

sentences.en: It happens and you can't ignore it. But that's not what we mean by suffering.
sentences.zh: 它会发生，你无法忽视。但这不是我们所说的痛苦。

sentences.en: Suffering is mostly mental anguish and mental pain.
sentences.zh: 痛苦主要是精神上的折磨和心理上的痛苦。

sentences.en: And it just means you don't want to do the task at hand.
sentences.zh: 这只意味着你不想做手头的工作。

sentences.en: If you were fine doing the task at hand, then you wouldn't be suffering.
sentences.zh: 如果你能欣然接受手头的工作，你就不会感到痛苦了。

sentences.en: And then the question is, what's more effective to suffer along the way or just to interpret it in a way that it's not suffering?
sentences.zh: 那么问题来了：是一路痛苦下去更有效，还是换个角度去解读，让它不再是痛苦？

sentences.en: You hear from a lot of successful people, they look back and they say, oh, the journey was the fun part, right?
sentences.zh: 你听许多成功人士说，他们回首往事时会说，哦，这段旅程才是最有趣的，对吧？

sentences.en: That was actually the entertaining part and I should have enjoyed it more.
sentences.zh: 那其实是最具娱乐性的部分，我本该更享受它才对。

sentences.en: It's a common regret. There's a little thought exercise I like to do, which is you can go back into your own life and try to put yourself in the exact position you were in five years ago 10 years ago 15 years ago 20 years ago and you try to remember okay who was i with what was i doing what was i feeling what were my emotions what were my objectives and really really try to transport yourself back and see if there's any advice you'd give yourself anything you'd do differently now you don't have new information don't pretend you could have gone back and you know bought a stock or bought Bitcoin or whatever, but just knowing what you know now in terms of your temperament and a little bit of age-related experience, how would you have done things differently?
sentences.zh: 这是一个常见的遗憾。我喜欢做一个小小的思想实验，那就是你可以回到自己的生活中，试着让自己回到五年前、十年前、十五年前、二十年前你所在的精确位置，然后试着去回忆：好吧，我和谁在一起？我在做什么？我当时有什么感觉？我的情绪是什么？我的目标是什么？真正、真正地努力把自己传送回去，看看有没有什么建议是你想给当年的自己的，有没有什么事情是你现在会做得不同的。你没有新的信息，别假装你可以回去买股票、买比特币之类；仅仅凭你现在的了解——就你的性格和一点随着年龄增长带来的经验而言，你当时会怎么做？

sentences.en: And I think it's a worthwhile exercise to do, so don't let me rob you of the conclusion, but I'll tell you for me, I would have done everything the same except I would have done it with less anger, less emotion, less internal suffering because that was optional.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个很值得做的实验，所以别让我剥夺了你得出结论的权利，但我可以告诉你，对于我来说，我会把一切都做得一模一样，除了我会少一些愤怒、少一些情绪、少一些内心的痛苦，因为那些都是不必要的。

sentences.en: It wasn't necessary. And I would argue that someone who can do the job at least peacefully, but maybe happily, is going to be more effective than someone who has unnecessary emotional turmoil.
sentences.zh: 那并非必需。而且我认为，一个能至少平静地、甚至快乐地完成工作的人，会比那些带有不必要情绪纠葛的人更高效。

sentences.en: Well, you end up with a series of miserable successes, right?
sentences.zh: 结果你会得到一连串痛苦的成功，对吧？

sentences.en: The outcome may have been the same, but the entire experience of getting that.
sentences.zh: 结局可能是一样的，但获取它的整个体验……

sentences.en: And the journey is not only the reward, the journey is the only thing there is.
sentences.zh: 而且旅程不仅是奖赏，旅程就是全部所有。

sentences.en: Even success, it's human nature to bank it very, very quickly, right?
sentences.zh: 甚至连成功，人类的天性也是非常非常快地把它存进“心理账户”，对吧？

sentences.en: Because the normal loop that we run through is you sit around, you're bored, then you want something.
sentences.zh: 因为我们经历的正常循环是：你坐在那儿，感到无聊，然后你想要某个东西。

sentences.en: Then when you want something, you decide you're not going to be happy until you get that thing.
sentences.zh: 接着当你想要某样东西时，你决定在得到它之前绝不快乐。

sentences.en: Then you start your bout of suffering or anticipation while you strive to get that thing.
sentences.zh: 然后你就开始了痛苦或期待的过程，努力去争取那个东西。

sentences.en: If you get that thing, then you get used to it.
sentences.zh: 如果你得到了那个东西，你就会习惯它。

sentences.en: And then you get bored again. Then a few months later, you want something else.
sentences.zh: 然后你又开始感到无聊。接着几个月后，你又想要别的东西了。

sentences.en: And if you don't get it, then you're unhappy for a bit.
sentences.zh: 如果你没得到，你就会郁闷一阵子。

sentences.en: And then you get over it and then you want something else, right?
sentences.zh: 然后你走出来，接着又想要别的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: That's the normal cycle. so whether you're happy or unhappy at the end it tends not to last now i don't want to be glib and say that oh there's no point in making money or being successful there absolutely is money solves all your money problems so it is good to have money um that said there are those uh those stories i don't know if you've seen those studies i don't know how real these are a lot of these psych studies don't replicate but it's a fun fun little study that shows that uh people who break their back and people who win the lottery are back to their baseline happiness two years later Yep.
sentences.zh: 这就是正常的循环。所以无论你最后是快乐还是痛苦，这种感觉往往都持续不长。现在，我不想轻率地说“赚钱或成功毫无意义”——它们绝对有意义。金钱能解决你所有的金钱问题，所以拥有金钱是件好事。话虽如此，还有那些……那些故事，我不知道你有没有看过那些研究，我不知道这些研究有多真实，很多心理学研究都无法复现，但这是一个很有趣的小研究：它显示那些遭遇瘫痪的人和中彩票的人，在两年后都会回到他们基准的幸福水平。是的。

sentences.en: Again, I don't know if that's entirely true.
sentences.zh: 再次声明，我不知道这是否完全正确。

sentences.en: I think money can buy you happiness if you earned it, because then along the way, you have both pride and confidence in yourself and you have a sense of accomplishment and you set out to do something and you were right.
sentences.zh: 我认为如果你是通过努力赚来的，钱就能买到快乐，因为在这个过程中，你对自己既有自豪感又有自信，你有一种成就感，你着手去做一件事并且做对了。

sentences.en: So I'll bet that lingers. And then, as I said, money solves your money problem.
sentences.zh: 所以我敢打赌这种感觉会挥之不去。而且，正如我所说，金钱能解决你的金钱问题。

sentences.en: So I don't want to be too glib about it, but I would say in general, this loop that we run through of desire, dopamine, fulfillment, unfulfillment.
sentences.zh: 所以我不想对此轻描淡写，但我想说，总的来说，我们经历的这种欲望、多巴胺、满足、不满足的循环……

sentences.en: You have to enjoy the journey. The journey is all there is, right?
sentences.zh: 你必须享受旅程。旅程就是一切，对吧？

sentences.en: 99% of your time is spent on the journey.
sentences.zh: 你99%的时间都花在旅程上。

sentences.en: So what kind of a journey is it if you're not going to enjoy it?
sentences.zh: 如果你不打算享受它，这算什么旅程？

sentences.en: How do you shortcut that desire contract? you could focus, you could decide that I don't want most things.
sentences.zh: 你该如何走捷径跳过这个欲望的契约？你可以专注于此，你可以决定我绝大多数东西都不想要。

sentences.en: I think we have a lot of unnecessary desires that we just pick up everywhere.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们有很多不必要的欲望，它们都是我们到处沾染来的。

sentences.en: We have opinions on everything, judgments on everything.
sentences.zh: 我们对每件事都有意见，对每件事都有评判。

sentences.en: So I think just knowing that those are the source of unhappiness will make you be choosy about your desires.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，只要知道这些就是不快乐的根源，你就会对自己的欲望变得挑剔。

sentences.en: And frankly, if you want to be successful, you have to be choosy about your desires.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，如果你想成功，你就必须对自己的欲望有所选择。

sentences.en: You have to focus. You can't be great at everything.
sentences.zh: 你必须保持专注。你不可能对每件事都精通。

sentences.en: You can't be great at everything. You're just going to waste your energy and waste your time.
sentences.zh: 你不可能在每件事上都做到最好。你只是在浪费精力和时间。

sentences.en: Is fame a worthwhile goal?
sentences.zh: 名气是一个值得追求的目标吗？

sentences.en: It gets you invited to better parties. It gets you to better restaurants.
sentences.zh: 它能让你受邀参加更好的派对，去更好的餐厅。

sentences.en: Fame. So fame is this funny thing where a lot of people know you, but you don't know them.
sentences.zh: 名气。所以名气是一件很有意思的事，很多人认识你，但你并不认识他们。

sentences.en: And it does get you put on the pedestal.
sentences.zh: 它确实能把你高高捧起。

sentences.en: It can get you what you want at a distance.
sentences.zh: 它能让你在远处就得到你想要的东西。

sentences.en: So I wouldn't say it's worthless. Obviously, people want it for a reason.
sentences.zh: 所以我不会说它毫无价值。显然，人们渴望它是有原因的。

sentences.en: It's high status, so it attracts the opposite sex, especially for men.
sentences.zh: 它是高地位的象征，因此能吸引异性，尤其是对男性而言。

sentences.en: It attracts women. That said, it is high cost.
sentences.zh: 它能吸引女性。话虽如此，它的代价也很高。

sentences.en: It means you have no privacy. You do have weirdos and lunatics.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你毫无隐私可言。你确实会遇到各种怪人和疯子。

sentences.en: You do get hit up a lot for weird things.
sentences.zh: 你确实会经常被卷入一些奇怪的事情中。

sentences.en: And you're on a stage, so you're forced to perform.
sentences.zh: 而且你身处舞台之上，所以你被迫去表演。

sentences.en: So you're forced to be consistent with your past proclamations and actions, and you're going to have haters and all that nonsense.
sentences.zh: 因此，你被迫与自己过去的宣言和行为保持一致，你也会招来黑粉和诸如此类的无聊风波。

sentences.en: But the fact that we do it, the fact that we all seem to want it, means that it would be disingenuous to say, oh, no, no, I'm famous, but you don't want to be famous.
sentences.zh: 但我们之所以这么做，我们似乎都渴望这一点，这意味着如果说“哦，不，不，我很出名，但你并不想出名”，那就太虚伪了。

sentences.en: That said, I think fame, like anything else, is best produced as a, or pursued as a byproduct of something potentially more worthwhile.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我认为名气和任何其他事物一样，最好是作为某种潜在更有价值事物的副产品来产生或追求。

sentences.en: Wanting to be famous and craving to be famous and being famous for being famous.
sentences.zh: 渴望成名，对名气的渴望，以及为了出名而出名。

sentences.en: These are sort of traps. Fame for fame's sake.
sentences.zh: 这些都是某种陷阱。为了名气而名气。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly. So it's better that it's earned fame.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。所以，通过努力赢得的名声会更好。

sentences.en: So for example, earned respect in the tribe is you do things that are good for the tribe.
sentences.zh: 比如，在部落里赢得尊重，就是去做对部落有益的事。

sentences.en: Who are the most famous people in human history? uh there uh you know there there are people who sort of transcended the self the buddhas and the jesus's and the muhammad's of the world who else is famous uh the artists are famous you know art lasts for a long time the scientists are famous they discover a thing the conquerors are famous presumably because they conquered for their tribe there was someone that they were fighting for so generally the higher up you rise by doing things for greater and greater groups of people even though it may be considered tyrannical or negative, like, you know, Genghis Khan is famous, but to the Mongols, he was doing good, to the rest of them, not so much.
sentences.zh: 人类历史上最有名的人是谁？呃，你知道，有一些超越自我的人，比如这个世界的佛陀、耶稣和穆罕默德。还有谁有名呢？艺术家很有名，你知道艺术可以流传很久；科学家很有名，他们发现了一个事物；征服者很有名，大概是因为他们为自己的部落去征服，有他们为之战斗的人。所以，总体来说，你通过为越来越庞大的人群做事而不断晋升，尽管这可能被认为是暴政或负面的，就像成吉思汗很有名，但对蒙古人来说他在做好事，对其他人来说就没那么好了。

sentences.en: The higher level you're operating at, the more people you're taking care of, the more you sort of earn respect and fame.
sentences.zh: 你运作的层级越高，你照顾的人越多，你某种程度上赢得的尊重和名气就越大。

sentences.en: And I think those are good reasons to be famous.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些都是成名的好理由。

sentences.en: If fame is empty, if you're famous just because your name showed up in a lot of places, or your face showed up in a lot of places, then that's a hollow fame.
sentences.zh: 如果名气是空洞的，如果你出名只是因为你的名字频繁出现，或者你的脸频繁出现在很多地方，那么这就是虚幻的名气。

sentences.en: And I think deep down, you will know that.
sentences.zh: 我想你内心深处会知道这一点。

sentences.en: And so it'll be fragile and you'll always be afraid of losing it.
sentences.zh: 所以它是脆弱的，你总是害怕失去它。

sentences.en: And then you'll be forced to perform. So the kind of fame that pure actors and celebrities have, I wouldn't want.
sentences.zh: 然后你就会被迫表演。因此，纯粹的演员和名流拥有的那种名气，我是不想要的。

sentences.en: But the kind of fame that's earned because you did something useful, why dodge that?
sentences.zh: 但那种因为你做了有用的事而赢得的名气，为什么要回避呢？

sentences.en: No, you can't. There's a challenge, I think, especially if people make very loud public proclamations about things.
sentences.zh: 不，你不能。我认为这里存在一个挑战，尤其是当人们对某些事情发表非常高调的公开宣言时。

sentences.en: You mentioned there about you're almost a hostage to the things that you used to say that, um, being able to update your opinions and change your mind looks very similar to the internet as hypocrisy does.
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到，你几乎成了自己过去所说之话的人质，呃，能够更新自己的观点和改变心意，在互联网看来，这和虚伪非常相似。

sentences.en: You know, the difference between me saying something in the past and saying something different now is perhaps I've learned, perhaps I've updated my beliefs, but so few people do it in a legitimate way.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我过去说的话和现在说的话之间的区别，也许是我学习了，也许我更新了自己的信念，但很少有人以正当的方式做到这一点。

sentences.en: I think that the grifter shill, you see, this is the smoking gun that shows that he didn't really believe that thing all along. and uh yeah i i went to a retreat in la a couple of years ago and there was a guy that i used to follow that a big um business and productivity advice content creator really really successful and he just totally stepped back from everything went like monk mode and focused on his business i asked him why and he said uh you I started feeling like I had to live up to in private the things that I was saying in public.
sentences.zh: 我认为江湖骗子和托儿，你看，这就是确凿的证据，表明他其实一直都不相信那件事。而且，呃，是的，几年前我去洛杉矶参加了一个静修会，那里有一个我以前关注的家伙，他是一个很大的商业和生产力建议内容创作者，非常非常成功。他完全退出了这一切，进入了“僧侣模式”，专注于他的生意。我问他为什么，他说，呃，我开始觉得我必须在私下里去兑现我在公开场合所说的话。

sentences.en: Right. Yeah, it's a, what was it, who said it was a Mencken that foolish consistency is a hobgoblin of little minds, right?
sentences.zh: 对。没错，这是一个，那是谁说的来着，是门肯（Mencken）说过愚蠢的一致性是狭隘头脑的心魔，对吧？

sentences.en: But essentially, look, all life is, all learning is error correction, right?
sentences.zh: 但本质上，看，所有的生活，所有的学习都是纠错，对吧？

sentences.en: Every knowledge creation system works through correcting errors, making guesses and correcting errors.
sentences.zh: 每一个知识创造系统都是通过纠正错误来运作的，做出猜测并纠正错误。

sentences.en: So by definition, if you're learning, you're going to be wrong most of the time and you'll be updating your priors.
sentences.zh: 因此，根据定义，如果你在学习，你大部分时间都会出错，并且你会在不断更新你先前的假设。

sentences.en: And so, for example, I did this Joe Rogan podcast.
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，我上了乔·罗根（Joe Rogan）的这个播客。

sentences.en: I don't know, it's like eight or nine years ago.
sentences.zh: 不知道，大概是八九年前吧。

sentences.en: And people will call out like the one thing that didn't turn out to be correct.
sentences.zh: 人们会挑出那件最终证明不正确的事情来。

sentences.en: Right. And it's just like, and they just beat on it because it helps them in their mind, raise their status a little bit.
sentences.zh: 对。就像是，他们揪住不放，因为这有助于他们在精神上稍微提升一点地位。

sentences.en: Aha, I caught him in an error. Well, I think if you catch someone in a blatant lie where there's believe one thing and they say another, that's legit.
sentences.zh: 哈，我抓住他犯错了。嗯，我认为如果你抓住某人在公然说谎，他们心里信一套，嘴上说另一套，那这就是合法的。

sentences.en: That's a character flaw. They shouldn't be lying.
sentences.zh: 那是一个性格缺陷。他们不应该撒谎。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, if they just made a guess at something and they got it wrong, and by the way, mostly it's about the AI-AGI thing.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，如果他们只是对某事做了一个猜测，结果猜错了——顺便说一句，这通常是关于AI-AGI那件事的。

sentences.en: And I think I'm still right about that, but it's a different story.
sentences.zh: 我想我在这点上仍然是正确的，但那是另一回事了。

sentences.en: People who think we have achieved AGI just fail a Turing test from their side.
sentences.zh: 那些认为我们已经实现AGI的人，只是从他们自身角度未能通过图灵测试而已。

sentences.en: But it's funny how people latch on to single proclamations, but the reality is all of us are dynamical systems.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，人们如何紧抓着单一的宣言不放，但现实是，我们所有人都是动态系统。

sentences.en: We're always changing. We're always learning.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在改变。我们一直在学习。

sentences.en: We're always growing. And hopefully we're correcting errors.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在成长。希望我们一直在纠正错误。

sentences.en: What you don't want to be doing is lying in public because you're trying to look good.
sentences.zh: 你最不想做的事情就是在公开场合撒谎，因为你想显得自己很好。

sentences.en: And I think people can smell that.
sentences.zh: 我想人们能闻出那种气味。

sentences.en: What this world really lacks right now is authenticity.
sentences.zh: 这个世界现在真正缺乏的是真实性。

sentences.en: And because everybody wants something, they want to be seen as something, they want to be something that they're not.
sentences.zh: 因为每个人都想要点什么，他们想被看作某种人，他们想成为他们本不是的那种人。

sentences.en: And so you do catch a lot of people saying things that they don't really believe.
sentences.zh: 所以你确实会发现很多人在说他们并不真正相信的话。

sentences.en: And I think people are very sensitive to that.
sentences.zh: 我想人们对此非常敏感。

sentences.en: Bullshit radars have become hypersensitized to try and work out whether or not this person means the thing that they're saying.
sentences.zh: 人们的胡话雷达变得极其敏感，试图弄清楚这个人是否真心实意地在说他嘴里的话。

sentences.en: Yeah. I mean, a lot of people are wrong.
sentences.zh: 对。我的意思是，很多人都是错的。

sentences.en: Most of us are wrong most of the time, especially in any new endeavor.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人在大部分时间里都是错的，尤其是在任何新的尝试中。

sentences.en: Difference between being wrong and disingenuous, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，犯错和虚伪是有区别的。

sentences.en: Purposefully wrong. Correct. Exactly. So I think that's the big difference.
sentences.zh: 故意犯错。没错。完全正确。所以我觉得这就是最大的区别。

sentences.en: If someone is wrong, no big deal, as long as they have a genuine reason for saying what they're saying or believing what they're believing.
sentences.zh: 如果一个人错了，那没什么大不了的，只要他们说出那些话或相信那些话有正当的理由。

sentences.en: But if they are lying to elevate their status or their appearance or to live up to some expectation, that's the mistake.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们为了提升自己的地位或外表，或者为了迎合某种期望而撒谎，那就是错误。

sentences.en: And that's a mistake not just for the listener.
sentences.zh: 这不仅是对听众而言是个错误。

sentences.en: It's a mistake for themselves, because then you're going to get trapped in a hall of mirrors.
sentences.zh: 对他们自己来说也是个错误，因为那样你就会被困在镜厅里。

sentences.en: You yourself are going to be consistent with your past proclamation.
sentences.zh: 你自己将不得不去迎合你过去的宣言。

sentences.en: So if you're lying to others, you're going to be lying to yourself.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你对别人撒谎，你最终也会对自己撒谎。

sentences.en: You're puppeted by a person that you are not even.
sentences.zh: 你被一个根本不是你自己的虚假人格所操控。

sentences.en: That's right. Yeah. It's like, what was that line?
sentences.zh: 没错。是的。就像那句台词说的什么来着？

sentences.en: You're basically trying to impress people who don't care about you.
sentences.zh: 你基本上是在试图给那些根本不在乎你的人留下深刻印象。

sentences.en: They don't like the real you. And if they saw the real you, they wouldn't care.
sentences.zh: 他们不喜欢真正的你。如果他们看到了真正的你，他们根本不会在乎。

sentences.en: And the people who would like the real you don't get to see the real you, so they pass you by.
sentences.zh: 而那些会喜欢真正的你的人却看不到真正的你，所以他们与你擦肩而过。

sentences.en: Right. You only want the respect of the very, very few people that you respect. trying to demand respect from the masses as the fools are in.
sentences.zh: 对。你只想赢得那些你所尊敬的极少数人的尊重。试图从大众那里强求尊重则是傻子才做的事。

sentences.en: Status games, the allure of accruing, whether it's fame, actual fame, or just the competition comparison trap, it's always there.
sentences.zh: 地位游戏，无论是真正的名气带来的诱惑，还是仅仅是盲目攀比的陷阱，它总是无处不在。

sentences.en: There's a real draw of being swayed by social approval.
sentences.zh: 受社会认可所左右有着极大的吸引力。

sentences.en: How should people learn to get less distracted by status games in that way?
sentences.zh: 人们应该如何学会不那么被这类的地位游戏所分心呢？

sentences.en: I think it just helps to see that status games don't matter as much as they used to. in old society let's go back hunter-gatherer times there was no such thing as wealth you just had what you could carry there was no stored wealth so wealth games didn't really exist to wealth creation games all that existed was status games if you were high status then you got what little was available first but even back then you had to earn your status by taking care of the tribe now we have wealth creation where you can actually create a product or a service you can scale that product or service and can provide abundance for a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 我认为，只要看到地位游戏不像以前那么重要了，就会有所帮助。在过去的社会里，让我们回到猎人采集的时代，根本没有财富这回事，你只有你能随身携带的东西，没有储存的财富，所以财富游戏其实并不存在。所有存在的都是地位游戏。如果你地位高，你就能最先得到那点可怜的可用资源。但即使在那个时候，你也必须通过照顾部落来赢得你的地位。现在我们有了财富创造，你可以真正创造产品或服务，你可以将该产品或服务规模化，并为很多人提供丰裕的物质。

sentences.en: And that's not zero sum. That's a positive sum game.
sentences.zh: 那不是零和博弈。那是一个正和游戏。

sentences.en: I can be wealthy, you can be wealthy, we can create things together.
sentences.zh: 我可以富有，你也可以富有，我们可以一起创造东西。

sentences.en: And clearly, since we are all collectively far, far wealthier than we were in hunter-gatherer times. uh wealth creation is positive but status is limited there's limited status to go around it's a ranking ladder it's a hierarchy and so to rise in status somebody else has a lower in status now you can have multiple kinds of status so you can expand some kinds of status but it's not like wealth creation where it can go infinitely where we can all be you know living in the stars and moon bases or mars colonies or what have you so just realize the status games are inherently limited.
sentences.zh: 显然，既然我们集体比猎人采集时代要富裕得多得多，财富创造是正和的，但地位是有限的。可供争夺的地位是有限的，它是一个排名阶梯，是一个等级制度。因此，为了提升地位，势必有人的地位会下降。虽然你可以拥有多种地位，所以你可以扩展某些种类的地位，但这不像财富创造那样可以无限发展，我们可以全部生活在星空、月球基地或火星殖民地等等地方。所以，只要意识到地位游戏本质上是有限的。

sentences.en: They're always combative. They always require direct combat, whereas wealth creation games can be just you're creating products.
sentences.zh: 它们总是充满对抗性。它们总是需要直接对抗，而财富创造游戏则可以仅仅是你自己在创造产品。

sentences.en: You don't have to fight anybody else. Yes, in the marketplace, your product has to succeed, but that's not quite the same as invective against other people or being angry with other people or feeling pushed down or pushed up or having a beef with somebody.
sentences.zh: 你不需要和任何人打架。是的，在市场上，你的产品必须成功，但这与对别人恶语相向、对别人感到愤怒、感到被压制或被抬高，或者与某人结怨是完全不同的。

sentences.en: So I would argue that wealth creation games are both more pleasant.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，财富创造游戏更加令人愉快。

sentences.en: They're positive some, and they actually have concrete material returns.
sentences.zh: 它们是正和博弈，而且确实有实际的物质回报。

sentences.en: If you have more money, you can buy more.
sentences.zh: 如果你有更多钱，你就能买更多东西。

sentences.en: Show me where you can exchange your status at the bank.
sentences.zh: 你倒是去银行把你的社会地位兑换成钱看看。

sentences.en: Exactly. Yeah. It's vague and it's fuzzy.
sentences.zh: 没错。对，这既模糊又抽象。

sentences.en: Now you see people get rich, they have money, what do they want?
sentences.zh: 现在你看到人们变富了，有了钱，他们想要什么？

sentences.en: They want status. So they go to Hollywood, start starring in movies, they donate to nonprofits, they go to Cannes or Davos or what have you, and they start trying to trade the money for status.
sentences.zh: 他们想要地位。所以他们去好莱坞，开始主演电影，向非营利组织捐款，去戛纳、达沃斯之类的地方，然后开始试图把金钱换成地位。

sentences.en: So people always want what they don't have.
sentences.zh: 所以人们总是想要他们没有的东西。

sentences.en: And we are evolutionarily hardwired for status because, as I said, wealth creation didn't really exist until the agricultural revolution when you could store grain and then the industrial revolution took it to another level and now the information age is taking it to yet another level.
sentences.zh: 而且我们在进化上天生就追求地位，因为正如我所说，财富创造在农业革命之前并不真正存在，当时你可以储存谷物，然后工业革命将其提升到了另一个水平，现在信息时代又将其提升到了一个新的水平。

sentences.en: But there's never been an easier time to make money.
sentences.zh: 但从来没有哪个时代比现在更容易赚钱。

sentences.en: Yes, it's still hard, but there's never been an easier time to create wealth because there's so much leverage out there.
sentences.zh: 是的，这仍然很难，但从来没有哪个时代比现在更容易创造财富，因为有那么多的杠杆。

sentences.en: There's so much opportunity. You still have to go find it.
sentences.zh: 有这么多的机会。你仍然得去寻找它们。

sentences.en: It's not easy. It's not going to fall in your lap and you have to learn something and know something and do something interesting.
sentences.zh: 这并不容易。它不会从天上掉下来，你必须学习一些东西，了解一些东西，做出一些有趣的事情。

sentences.en: But nevertheless, it's possible to many more people.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，对更多人来说这已经成为可能。

sentences.en: A few hundred years ago, you were born a surf, you were going to die a surf.
sentences.zh: 几百年前，你生下来是农奴，你就会死于农奴。

sentences.en: There was almost no way out of that. That's changed.
sentences.zh: 几乎没有出路。这一切都变了。

sentences.en: And so I would argue that you're better off focusing on wealth games and status games.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，你最好把精力集中在财富游戏上，而不是地位游戏上。

sentences.en: If you're trying to build up, for example, your following on a social network and get famous and then get rich off of being famous, that's a much harder path than getting rich first.
sentences.zh: 如果你试图在社交网络上积累粉丝，成名，然后靠出名发财，那比先发财要走的路艰难得多。

sentences.en: And then go for your fame afterwards would be my advice. well a lot of people do that as you said it's funny how uh people who have achieved such a level of wealth you don't think why do you need the status given that most people use status to then try and cash in to achieve wealth if you've achieved money already if you're post money or uh asset heavy as it's known um why are you trying to go in the other direction what as you said because we've got we've got an illustrious history biologically of wanting status and wealth is kind of novel.
sentences.zh: 我的建议是，先发财，然后再去追求名气。嗯，正如你所说，很多人都这样做，很有趣的是，那些达到这种财富水平的人，你不会去想，既然大多数人利用地位来试图套现以获取财富，如果你已经拥有了金钱，如果你是超越金钱的，或者如人们所知的资产雄厚，嗯，你为什么还要往反方向走？正如你所说，因为我们在生物学上有着对地位的显赫历史渴望，而财富某种程度上是新颖的。

sentences.en: It's new. Wealth is something that you have to understand more intellectually.
sentences.zh: 这是新鲜事。财富是你必须在理智上更多去理解的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's a physical component, more food, more survival.
sentences.zh: 是的，它有一个物理组成部分，更多的食物，更多的生存。

sentences.en: But to truly understand the effects and the powers and the abilities and limitations and the advantages and disadvantages of wealth, you have to use your neocortex a lot more.
sentences.zh: 但要真正理解财富的影响、力量、能力、局限性以及优势和劣势，你必须更多地动用你的新皮层。

sentences.en: Does that mean the reason to play the game is to win the game and be done with it is harder to win and be done with for status than it is for wealth?
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着，玩这个游戏的理由是为了赢得游戏并彻底结束它，对于地位来说，比对于财富来说更难赢得并结束？

sentences.en: That's a good observation. I hadn't thought that through, but you're right.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的观察。我之前没有想过这一点，但你是对的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's right. I think people always want more status, but I think you can be satisfied at a certain level of wealth.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想这很对。我认为人们总是想要更高的地位，但我认为你可以在某个财富水平上感到满足。

sentences.en: Whereas, well, you always have this sort of sense, and this is what leaderboards are, right?
sentences.zh: 然而，财富，你总是有一种这样的感觉，这就是排行榜的意义所在，对吧？

sentences.en: This is the iTunes billboard chart. And it is zero sum.
sentences.zh: 这是iTunes告示牌排行榜。而且它是零和博弈。

sentences.en: And it is, I guess, the Forbes richest people on the planet.
sentences.zh: 我想，这也是福布斯全球富豪榜的意思。

sentences.en: Yeah, that one's harder to climb the ladder on.
sentences.zh: 是的，那个榜单想要往上爬更难。

sentences.en: But the fact that, for example, iTunes and YouTube can put you in competition against your contemporaries every single day and make you go up and down and show you likes and comments and ratings.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，比如说，iTunes和YouTube可以让你每天都与同龄人展开竞争，让你上下浮动，向你展示点赞、评论和评分。

sentences.en: This is how much you fell. This is how much you're up.
sentences.zh: 这是你下跌的幅度。这是你上升的幅度。

sentences.en: Exactly. They keep you running on that treadmill forever.
sentences.zh: 没错。他们让你永远在那台跑步机上奔跑。

sentences.en: Jimmy Carr has this cool idea where he says trajectory is more important than position.
sentences.zh: 吉米·卡尔有一个很酷的观点，他说轨迹比当前位置更重要。

sentences.en: So if you are number... 101 in the world, but last year you were number 200 versus you're number two in the world, but last year you were number one.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是世界排名第101位，但去年你是第200位；与你是世界排名第二，但去年你是第一相比。

sentences.en: There is this sense of the deceleration is very, very tangible.
sentences.zh: 这种减速感是非常非常切实的。

sentences.en: And it's like, again, it goes back to evolution, you know, something that is bleeding eventually dies unless you stop the bleeding.
sentences.zh: 而且就像，再次回到进化论，你知道的，流血的东西最终会死，除非你止血。

sentences.en: So you're hardwired not to lose what you have.
sentences.zh: 所以你的本能决定了你不会失去你拥有的东西。

sentences.en: And because we evolved in conditions where we're so close to just not surviving, you don't want to give anything up.
sentences.zh: 而且因为我们进化时的环境是如此接近于无法生存，你不想放弃任何东西。

sentences.en: It's hardwired into us to not give anything up.
sentences.zh: 不放弃任何东西已经深深烙印在我们的基因里。

sentences.en: So you grip tightly. That's right. The worst outcome in the world is not having self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 所以你抓得很紧。没错。世上最糟糕的结果就是没有自尊。

sentences.en: Why? Yeah, it's a tough one.
sentences.zh: 为什么？是的，这是一个棘手的问题。

sentences.en: I look at the people and I don't want to offend anybody, but I look at the people who don't like themselves and that's the toughest slot because they're always wrestling with themselves and it's hard enough to face the outside world.
sentences.zh: 我看着那些人，我不想冒犯任何人，但我看着那些不喜欢自己的人，那是极其艰难的处境，因为他们总是在和自己搏击，而面对外部世界已经够难了。

sentences.en: And no one's going to like you more than you like yourself. so if you're struggling with yourself then the outside world becomes an insurmountable challenge and it's hard to say why people have low self-esteem it might be genetic it might just be circumstantial a lot of times i think it's because they just weren't unconditionally loved as a child and that sort of seeps in at a deep core level but self-esteem issues can be the most limiting one interesting thought is that you know to some extent self-esteem is a reputation you have with yourself.
sentences.zh: 没有人会比你自己更喜欢你。所以如果你在跟自己作斗争，那么外部世界就会变成一个不可逾越的挑战，而且很难说为什么人们会有低自尊，它可能是基因决定的，也可能只是环境使然，很多时候我认为是因为他们在童年时没有得到无条件地爱，这种感觉深入到了核心层面，但自尊问题可能是最具限制性的问题，一个有趣的思考是，在某种程度上，你对自己的自尊就是你在自己心目中的声誉。

sentences.en: You're watching yourself at all times. You know what you're doing and you have your own moral code.
sentences.zh: 你时刻在注视着自己。你知道自己在做什么，并且有你自己的道德准则。

sentences.en: Everyone has a different moral code. But if you don't live up to your own moral code, the same code that you hold others to, it will damage your self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 每个人都有不同的道德准则。但如果你没有达到你自己的道德准则，也就是你用来要求别人的准则，它就会损害你的自尊。

sentences.en: So perhaps one way to build up your self-esteem is to live up to your own code, very rigorously have one and then live up to it.
sentences.zh: 所以建立自尊的一个方法可能是遵守你自己的准则，非常严格地制定一个准则然后去践行它。

sentences.en: Another way to raise your self-esteem might be to do things for others.
sentences.zh: 提升自尊的另一个方法可能是为别人做点事。

sentences.en: If I look back on my life and you know what are the moments that i'm actually proud of there's very far and few between and it's not that often it's not the things you would expect it's not the material success it's not having learned this thing or that it's when i made a sacrifice for somebody or something that i loved and that's when i'm actually ironically most proud now that's through an explicit mental exercise but i'll bet you at some level i'm recording that implicitly so that tells me that even if i am not being loved and the way to create love is to give love to to express love through sacrifice and through duty.
sentences.zh: 如果我回首我的人生，你知道我真正引以为傲的时刻是什么吗？它们少之又少，而且并不常见，不是你所期望的那些事情，不是物质上的成功，不是学会了这个或那个，而是当我为我爱的人或事做出牺牲的时候，而讽刺的是，那正是我最自豪的时候，现在，这是通过一次明确的心理练习得出的，但我敢打赌，在某种程度上，我在潜意识里默默记录着这一点，所以这告诉我，即使我没有被爱，而创造爱的方法就是去付出爱，通过牺牲和责任来表达爱。

sentences.en: And so I think doing things like that can build up your self-esteem really fast.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为做这些事情可以非常快地建立你的自尊。

sentences.en: It's interesting when you talk about sacrifice, because a lot of the time people say, why sacrifice so much for my job?
sentences.zh: 当你谈到牺牲时很有趣，因为很多时候人们会说，为什么要为我的工作牺牲这么多？

sentences.en: It's like, yeah, but that was you sacrificing something that you wanted less for something that you wanted more, as opposed to genuinely taking some sort of cost.
sentences.zh: 这就像是，是的，但那是你牺牲了你较少想要的东西来换取你更想要的东西，而不是真正承担某种代价。

sentences.en: And yeah, I wonder whether if self-esteem is you adhering to your internal, your actions and your values aligning, even when it's difficult, or perhaps even more so when it's difficult.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想知道，如果自尊是你坚持内在的表现，是你的行动和价值观相一致，即使在困难的时候，或者也许在困难的时候更是如此。

sentences.en: I wonder whether there is a price that people who are more introspective, high integrity pay, because you think, well, you've got this heavier set of overheads that you need to pay in some way.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，那些更内省、正直的人是否需要付出某种代价，因为你会想，嗯，你有一套更沉重的日常开销，你需要以某种方式支付。

sentences.en: Well, if being ethical were profitable, everybody would do it, right? so uh you at some level it does involve a sacrifice uh but that sacrifice can also be thought of as you're thinking for the long term rather than the short term um for example the virtues are the set of uh virtues is a set of beliefs that if everybody in society followed them as individuals it would lead to win-win outcomes for everybody so if i am honest and you are honest then we can do business more easily we can interact more easily because we can trust each other.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果讲道德是有利可图的，每个人都会这么做，对吧？所以，在某种程度上，它确实涉及牺牲；但这种牺牲也可以被认为是你为长远考虑，而不是为短期考虑，例如，美德是一套信念，如果社会上的每个人作为个体都遵循这些信念，它将为每个人带来双赢的结果。所以如果我很诚实，你也很诚实，那么我们就能更轻松地做生意，我们能更轻松地互动，因为我们可以信任彼此。

sentences.en: So even though there might be a few liars in the system, as long as there aren't too many liars and too many cheaters, a high trust society where everybody's honest is better off.
sentences.zh: 所以即使系统中可能会有几个骗子，只要骗子和作瑟没有那么多，一个每个人都诚实的高信任社会就会过得更好。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of the virtues work this way, right?
sentences.zh: 我想很多美德都是这样运作的，对吧？

sentences.en: If I don't go around sleeping with your wife and you don't sleep with mine, and you know, if I don't take all the food that's at the table first and so on, then we all get along better and we can play win-win games.
sentences.zh: 如果我不出去跟你妻子睡觉，你也不跟我妻子睡觉，你知道的，如果我没有把桌上的所有食物都抢先拿光等等，那么我们大家就能相处得更好，我们就能玩双赢的游戏。

sentences.en: In game theory, the most famous game is Prisoner's Dilemma, but that's all about everybody cheating and the Nash equilibrium, the stable equilibrium there is everybody cheats.
sentences.zh: 在博弈论中，最著名的游戏是囚徒困境，但那全关乎每个人都作弊，那里的纳什均衡、稳定均衡就是每个人都作弊。

sentences.en: And the only way you can play a win-win game is if you have long-term iterated moves.
sentences.zh: 而你能玩双赢游戏的唯一方法，就是你有长期的、迭代的行动。

sentences.en: But that's not actually the most common game played in society.
sentences.zh: 但这实际上并不是社会中最常见的游戏。

sentences.en: The most common game played is one called a stag's hunt, where if we cooperate, we can bring down a big stag and both have big dinners.
sentences.zh: 最常见的游戏被称为“牡鹿猎取”（Stag Hunt），如果我们合作，我们可以猎杀一头大鹿，两人都能享用丰盛的晚餐。

sentences.en: But if we don't cooperate, then we have to go hunt like rabbits and we each have small dinners. so most of uh and that game has two stable equilibriums and one could be where we're both hunting the rabbit and one could be where we're hunting the stag so the high trust society is a more most more virtuous society where i can trust you to come hunt the stag with me and show up on time and do the work and divide it up properly so you want to live in a system where everybody has their own set of virtues and follows them and then we all win but i would argue you don't need to do that for sacrifice.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们不合作，那我们就只能去抓兔子，每个人只能吃一顿小晚餐。所以大多数……而且那个游戏有两个稳定的均衡，一个可能是我们都在抓兔子，另一个可能是我们在猎鹿。所以高信任社会是一个更加有美德的社会，在那里我可以信任你来和我一起猎鹿，准时出现，完成工作并适当地分配它。所以你想生活在一个每个人都有一套美德并遵循它们的系统中，然后我们都能赢。但我认为，你不需要为了牺牲而做到这一点。

sentences.en: You don't need to do that for other people.
sentences.zh: 你不需要为了别人而这么做。

sentences.en: You can do it just purely for yourself. You will have higher self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 你完全可以只为了你自己这样做。你将拥有更高的自尊。

sentences.en: You will attract other high virtue people.
sentences.zh: 你会吸引其他具有高美德的人。

sentences.en: Would I go on a stag hunt with me? Correct.
sentences.zh: 我会跟自己去猎鹿吗？没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right. And if you're the kind of person, if you're the kind of person who long-term signals ethics and virtues, then you'll attract other people who are ethical and virtuous.
sentences.zh: 是的，就是这样。如果你是那种人，如果你是那种长期发出道德和美德信号的人，那么你就会吸引其他有道德、有美德的人。

sentences.en: Whereas if you are a shark, you will eventually find yourself swimming entirely amongst sharks.
sentences.zh: 而如果你是一条鲨鱼，你最终会发现自己完全在鲨鱼群中游弋。

sentences.en: And that's an unpleasant existence. But again, this goes back to the equivalent of the marshmallow test.
sentences.zh: 那将是一种令人痛苦的生存状态。但话说回来，这可以追溯到棉花糖测试的等价物。

sentences.en: And by the way, the marshmallow test does not replicate.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，棉花糖测试无法被重复验证。

sentences.en: It's fake science. I saw the Icaut replication crisis hard recently.
sentences.zh: 这是伪科学。我最近看到冰激凌重复危机（译者注：原文icaut应为replication crisis即心理学可重复性危机）非常严重。

sentences.en: But it is about trading off the short term for the long term.
sentences.zh: 但这确实关乎权衡短期与长期。

sentences.en: And so I think for a lot of these so-called virtues, there are long-term selfish reasons to be virtuous.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为对于许多这些所谓的“美德”来说，保持美德有着长期的自私原因。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Did you deal with self-doubt in the past?
sentences.zh: 你过去处理过自我怀疑吗？

sentences.en: Is that something that was a hurdle for you to overcome?
sentences.zh: 那是你需要克服的一个障碍吗？

sentences.en: Yes and no. I think I dealt with self-doubt in the sense that, oh, I don't know what I'm doing and I need to figure it out.
sentences.zh: 算也不是。我认为我处理自我怀疑的方式是，哦，我不知道自己在做什么，我需要弄清楚它。

sentences.en: But I didn't doubt myself in the way of somebody else knows better than me for me or that, you know, I'm an idiot or I'm not worthwhile or anything that I guess I had the benefit of I grew up with a lot of love, like the people around me love me unconditionally.
sentences.zh: 但我并没有这样怀疑过自己：觉得别人比我更懂我，或者觉得我是个笨蛋，或者我毫无价值，或者其他什么。我想我有一个优势，我在充满爱的环境中长大，周围的人无条件地爱我。

sentences.en: And so that just gave me a lot of confidence, not the kind of confidence that would say, I have the answer, but the kind of confidence that I will figure it out and I know what I want, or only I am a good arbiter of what I want.
sentences.zh: 这给了我很多信心，不是那种觉得“我知道答案”的信心，而是那种“我会弄清楚它，我知道我想要什么，或者只有我才是自己想要什么的优秀裁判”的信心。

sentences.en: Yeah, that level of self-belief, I suppose, allows you to determine what is it that matters to me, my self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 是的，这种程度的自信，我想，能让你确定什么对我重要，我的自尊。

sentences.en: Should I chase this thing or not? I can make a fair judgment on that as opposed to being so swayed.
sentences.zh: 我应该追求这个还是不应该？我可以对此做出公正的判断，而不是轻易被左右。

sentences.en: But it's such a good point about even if you think you're not consciously logging the stuff that you're doing, there is some that's in the back of your mind was it the daemon is that what the ancient greeks are something used to talk about yeah also in computer science like there's a concept of a daemon which is a uh a program that's always running in the background you can't see it okay um but yeah it probably comes from the ancient greek daemon uh but yeah what you know that you don't even know you know is far greater than what you know you know right you can't even articulate most of the things you know.
sentences.zh: 但这真是一个极好的观点，哪怕你觉得自己并没有在有意识地记录你所做的事情，但你的脑海深处确实留存着一些东西，这就是所谓的“守护灵”吗？古希腊人以前常常谈论的东西吗？对的，在计算机科学里也有“守护灵”（daemon）这个概念，也就是一个总是在后台运行、你看不见的程序，对吧，不过是的，它大概源自古希腊语中的 daemon 吧，但你知道的、甚至连自己都不知道你所知道的东西，要远远多于你知道自己知道的东西，对吧？你甚至无法表述你所知道的大多数事情。

sentences.en: There are feelings you have that have no words for them.
sentences.zh: 你有些感受，甚至连对应的词汇都没有。

sentences.en: There are thoughts you have that are felt within the body or subconsciously that you never articulate to yourself.
sentences.zh: 你有些想法是在身体里或潜意识中感受到的，但你从未对自己明确表达过。

sentences.en: You can't articulate the rules of grammar, yet you exercise them effortlessly when you speak.
sentences.zh: 你无法表述语法规则，但在说话时却能轻而易举地运用它们。

sentences.en: So I would argue that your implicit knowledge and your knowledge that is unknown to yourself is far greater than the knowledge you can articulate and that you can communicate.
sentences.zh: 所以我想说，你的隐性知识以及那些连你自己都不知道的知识，要远远大于你能表述和交流的知识。

sentences.en: And so at some level, you're always watching yourself.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，你总是在审视自己。

sentences.en: That's what your consciousness is, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是你的意识，对吧？

sentences.en: It's the thing that's watching everything, including your mind, including your body.
sentences.zh: 它就是那个观察一切的事物，包括你的心灵，包括你的身体。

sentences.en: So if you want to have high self-esteem, then earn your own self-respect.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想拥有高度的自尊，那就去赢得你自己的尊重。

sentences.en: I had this idea, the internal golden rule.
sentences.zh: 我曾有过这样一个想法，叫做“内在黄金法则”。

sentences.en: So the golden rule says treat others the way that you should be treated, you want to be treated.
sentences.zh: 黄金法则说的是，你希望别人怎么对你，你就该怎么对待别人。

sentences.en: The internal golden rule says, treat yourself like others should have treated you.
sentences.zh: 而内在黄金法则说的是，对待自己要像别人本来应该对待你那样。

sentences.en: And it was a riposte to maybe people that didn't grow up with unconditional love in that way.
sentences.zh: 这是对那些在成长过程中没有得到无条件爱的人的一种回应。

sentences.en: On the love thing, one of the interesting things about love is you can try to remember the feeling of being loved.
sentences.zh: 关于爱这件事，关于爱的一个有趣之处在于，你可以试着去回忆被爱的感觉。

sentences.en: So go back to when someone was in love with you or someone did love you.
sentences.zh: 回想一下当初某人深爱着你，或者某人确实爱过你的时候。

sentences.en: And like, really remember that feeling, like really sit with it and try to recreate it within yourself.
sentences.zh: 然后，真的去回味那种感觉，真正地去体会它，并试着在自己内心重现它。

sentences.en: And then go to the feeling of you loving someone and when you were in love.
sentences.zh: 接着，转换到你爱某人以及你深陷爱河时的感觉。

sentences.en: And I'm not even talking about romantic love necessarily, so be a little careful there.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不一定是指浪漫的爱情，所以在这点上要稍微注意一下。

sentences.en: I'm talking more about like love for... It can sometimes get complex if you're talking about past romantic love.
sentences.zh: 我更多指的是对……如果你谈论的是过去的浪漫爱情，有时情况会变得复杂。

sentences.en: Right. A sibling or a child or something like that, or a parent.
sentences.zh: 没错。比如兄弟姐妹、孩子之类的，或者是父母。

sentences.en: And think about when you felt love towards someone or something.
sentences.zh: 想想当你对某人或某事感到爱意时的情景。

sentences.en: And now, which is better?
sentences.zh: 那么现在，哪个更好呢？

sentences.en: And I would argue that the feeling of being in love is actually more exhilarating than the feeling of being loved.
sentences.zh: 我认为，陷入爱河的感觉其实比被爱的感觉更让人振奋。

sentences.en: Being loved is a little clawing. It's a little too sweet.
sentences.zh: 被爱有点黏人。它太甜腻了。

sentences.en: You kind of want to push the person away.
sentences.zh: 你会有种想把对方推开的冲动。

sentences.en: It's a little embarrassing. And you know that if that person is too much into it, that you feel constrained.
sentences.zh: 这有点让人尴尬。而且你知道，如果对方陷得太深，你会感到受束缚。

sentences.en: On the other hand, the feeling of being in love is very expansive.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，陷入爱河的感觉是非常广阔的。

sentences.en: It's very open. It actually makes you a better version of yourself.
sentences.zh: 它是非常开放的。它实际上能让你成为更好的自己。

sentences.en: It makes you want to be a better person.
sentences.zh: 它会让你想要成为一个更好的人。

sentences.en: And so you can create love anytime you want.
sentences.zh: 所以你随时都可以创造爱。

sentences.en: It's just that craving to receive it. That's the problem.
sentences.zh: 问题就在于那种索取的渴望。

sentences.en: The most expensive trait is pride. How come?
sentences.zh: 最昂贵的特质是骄傲。为什么这么说？

sentences.en: Oh, that was a recent one. I tweeted that just because I think that pride is the enemy of learning.
sentences.zh: 哦，那是最近的一条。我发推文是因为我觉得骄傲是学习的天敌。

sentences.en: So when I look at my friends and colleagues, the ones who are still stuck in the past and have grown the least are the ones who were the proudest because they sort of feel like they already had the answers.
sentences.zh: 所以当我看看我的朋友和同事时，那些依然停滞不过去、成长最少的人，往往就是最骄傲的人，因为他们觉得自己好像已经掌握了答案。

sentences.en: And so they don't want to correct themselves publicly.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不愿意在公开场合纠正自己。

sentences.en: And so this goes back to the fame conversation.
sentences.zh: 这就回到了关于名气的对话。

sentences.en: You get locked into something you said, it made you famous, you're known for that, and now you want to pivot or change.
sentences.zh: 你被自己说过的话所束缚，它让你成名了，你也因此为人所知，而现在你想要转型或改变。

sentences.en: So pride prevents you from saying I'm wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以骄傲阻止了你说“我错了”。

sentences.en: What's pride in this context here? It could be as simple as you're trading stocks and then you don't admit you were wrong, so you hang on to a lousy trade.
sentences.zh: 这里的“骄傲”在语境中指什么？它可能很简单，比如你在炒股，然后你死不承认自己错了，于是你死死抓着一笔糟糕的交易不放。

sentences.en: It could be that you made a decision to marry someone or move somewhere or enter a profession, it doesn't work out, and then you don't admit that you were wrong, so you get stuck in it.
sentences.zh: 也可能是你做出了和某人结婚、搬到某地或从事某项职业的决定，结果并不顺利，但你却不肯承认自己错了，于是就被困在了其中。

sentences.en: It's mostly about getting trapped in local maxima as opposed to going back down and climbing up the mountain again.
sentences.zh: 这主要意味着陷入了局部最优解，而不是退回山脚下重新爬山。

sentences.en: And that's why it's an expensive trade, because you continue to need to repay it in one form or another.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它是一笔昂贵的交易，因为你得不断地以这样或那样的方式去偿还它。

sentences.en: Yeah, you're just stuck at a suboptimal point.
sentences.zh: 对，你只是被困在了一个次优的点上。

sentences.en: It's going to cost you money. It's going to cost you success.
sentences.zh: 这会花掉你的钱。这会花掉你的成功。

sentences.en: And time. And time. The great artists always have this ability to start over, whether it's Paul Simon or Madonna or you two, and I'm dating myself a little bit.
sentences.zh: 还有时间。还有时间。伟大的艺术家总是拥有重新开始的能力，无论是保罗·西蒙（Paul Simon）、麦当娜（Madonna）还是U2乐队，我这么说有点暴露年龄了。

sentences.en: But even the great entrepreneurs, they're just always willing to start over.
sentences.zh: 但即使是伟大的企业家，他们也总是愿意重新开始。

sentences.en: I'm always struck by the Elon Musk story where he did PayPal as x.com originally, actually.
sentences.zh: 埃隆·马斯克（Elon Musk）的故事总是让我印象深刻，他最初把PayPal叫做 x.com。

sentences.en: It was his financial institution that got merged into PayPal.
sentences.zh: 其实那是他自己的金融机构，后来合并进了PayPal。

sentences.en: It's good that you've got the domain, you know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你拥有这个域名挺好的，你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly. I'll park that. I'll hold on to it.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。我先把这个存起来。我得留着它。

sentences.en: He's consistent. He's been using it for quite a while.
sentences.zh: 他很专一。他用这个名字已经挺久了。

sentences.en: And he said something like along the lines of, I made $200 million from the sale of PayPal.
sentences.zh: 他曾说过类似这样的话：我通过出售PayPal赚了2亿美元。

sentences.en: I put $100 million into SpaceX, $80 million in Tesla, 20 in the solar city, and I had to borrow money for rent, right?
sentences.zh: 我把1亿美元投给了SpaceX，8000万美元投给了特斯拉，2000万美元投给了SolarCity，结果我还得借钱付房租，对吧？

sentences.en: This guy is a perennial risk taker. He's always willing to start over.
sentences.zh: 这家伙是个不折不扣的风险承担者。他总是愿意重新开始。

sentences.en: He doesn't have any pride about being seen as successful as being seen as a failure.
sentences.zh: 他一点也不在乎别人把他看作成功人士还是失败者。

sentences.en: He's willing to put it all on the line. Back himself again each time.
sentences.zh: 他愿意孤注一掷。每次都坚定地支持自己。

sentences.en: Back himself again each time. But the key thing is he's always willing to start over, right?
sentences.zh: 每次都坚定地支持自己。但关键在于，他总是愿意重新开始，对吧？

sentences.en: Even now when he's sort of made his new startup is a USA, right?
sentences.zh: 即使是现在，当他可以说是开启了他的新创业项目——美国（USA），对吧？

sentences.en: He's basically trying to fix it like he would fix one of his startups.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是想去修复它，就像他会修复自己的某家创业公司一样。

sentences.en: And I think that is a willingness to look like a fool and that is a willingness to start over and a lot of people just don't have that they become successful they become rich or they become famous and that's it they're stuck they don't want to go back to zero and creating anything great requires zero to one and that means you go back to zero and that's really painful and hard to do talking about risk risk. something I've been thinking about a lot to do with you.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是一种甘愿显得像个傻子的意愿，这就是一种愿意重新开始的意愿，而很多人就是没有这一点，他们成功了，他们变富了，或者他们出名了，然后就到此为止了，他们被困住了，不想回到零点，而创造任何伟大的东西都需要从零到一，这意味着你得回到零点，这真的非常痛苦且难以做到，谈到风险，风险……这是我最近一直在思考的、和你密切相关的事。

sentences.en: Any moment when you're not having a good time, when you're not really happy, you're not doing anyone any favors.
sentences.zh: 任何你过得不开心、没有真正快乐的时刻，你其实都没有帮到任何人。

sentences.en: Lots of people have become unusually familiar with suffering silently in that sort of a way of not having a high bar for your expectation for quality of life.
sentences.zh: 很多人已经变得异常习惯于默默承受痛苦，用那种方式来降低对生活品质的期望标准。

sentences.en: Yeah, a lot of it is just you're memeing yourself into a bad outcome because you think that somehow suffering is glorious or that it makes you a better person or you know my old quip was if you're so smart why aren't you happy why can't you figure that one out um the reality is you can be smart and happy there are plenty of people in human history who are smart and happy and i think it just starts with saying yeah you know what i'm gonna be happy there was a guy that i met in thailand a long time ago and uh he used to work for tony robbins uh you know he had great attitude.
sentences.zh: 是的，很多时候你只是在用迷因（meme）心态把自己忽悠到一个糟糕的结果里，因为你觉得吃苦在某种程度上是光彩的，或者它能让你成为一个更好的人，你知道我的老笑话是：如果你那么聪明，为什么你还不快乐？为什么你想不通这一点？嗯，现实是你可以既聪明又快乐，人类历史上有很多聪明又快乐的人，我认为这一切都始于这样一句话：“是的，你知道吗，我要快乐。”很久以前我在泰国遇到过一个人，呃，他以前给托尼·罗宾斯（Tony Robbins）工作过，你知道的，他心态极好。

sentences.en: And we were sitting around and he said, I realized one day that someone out there had to be the happiest person in the world.
sentences.zh: 我们坐在一起时，他说：“我有一天突然意识到，外边总得有人是世界上最快乐的人吧。”

sentences.en: That person just has to exist. He said, why not me?
sentences.zh: 那个人必须存在。他说：“为什么不能是我？”

sentences.en: I'll take on that burden. I'll be that guy.
sentences.zh: “我来承担这个重担。我来当那个人。”

sentences.en: And I heard that and I was like, wow, that's pretty good.
sentences.zh: 我听到这话时心想：“哇，这太棒了。”

sentences.en: That's a good frame. He knew how to reframe things.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的思维框架。他懂得如何重塑事物。

sentences.en: And so I think a lot of happiness is just a choice in the sense that first you just identify yourself as actually, I'm going to be a person that's going to be happy.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为很多快乐其实只是一种选择，从某种意义上说，首先你得确认自己：“其实，我要做一个快乐的人。”

sentences.en: I'm going to figure it out. And you just figure it out along the way.
sentences.zh: “我会找到方法的。”然后你在前行的路上自然会找到解决办法。

sentences.en: You're not going to lose your other predilections.
sentences.zh: 你不会失去你其他的爱好。

sentences.en: You're not going to lose your ambition or desire for success.
sentences.zh: 你不会失去你的雄心壮志或对成功的渴望。

sentences.en: I think a lot of people have this fear that, oh, if I'm happy, then I won't want to be successful.
sentences.zh: 我觉得很多人都有这种恐惧，哦，如果我快乐了，那我就不想成功了。

sentences.en: No, you just want to do things that are more aligned with the happy version of you and you'll be successful at those things.
sentences.zh: 不，你只是想去做那些与快乐的你更契合的事情，而且你在这些事情上也会获得成功。

sentences.en: And believe me, the happy version of you is not going to look back at the unhappy version and say, oh man, that guy was going to be more successful.
sentences.zh: 相信我，快乐的你绝不会回过头去看那个不快乐的自己，然后说：“哦天哪，那家伙本来会更成功的。”

sentences.en: I wish that I was him. You're actually trying to be successful so you'll be happy.
sentences.zh: “我真希望我就是他。”其实你努力获得成功就是为了让自己快乐。

sentences.en: That's the whole point. You've gotten it backwards.
sentences.zh: 这才是重点。你们把因果关系搞颠倒了。

sentences.en: You unlocked one of my trap cards. One of my favorite insights is that we sacrifice the thing we want for the thing that's supposed to get it.
sentences.zh: 你触发了我的其中一张陷阱卡。我最喜欢的见解之一就是：我们为了得到某种东西而去牺牲原本想要的东西。

sentences.en: So we sacrifice happiness in order to be successful so that when we're finally sufficiently successful, we can actually be happy.
sentences.zh: 所以我们牺牲了快乐去换取成功，这样当我们在未来终于足够成功时，我们就能真正快乐了。

sentences.en: And if you have some sort of simultaneous equation, you just sort of stripped success off from both sides.
sentences.zh: 如果你有一个联立方程，你其实只是把“成功”这个因素从等式两边都消掉了。

sentences.en: At least in my own life, I have not found there to be a trade-off.
sentences.zh: 至少在我的生活中，我没发现两者之间存在权衡。

sentences.en: If anything, I have found that the happier I get, the more I am going to do the things that I'm good at and aligned with, and that will make me even happier.
sentences.zh: 如果说有什么的话，我发现我越快乐，就越会去做那些我擅长且与我志趣相投的事，而这会让我更快乐。

sentences.en: And so I actually end up more successful, not less.
sentences.zh: 所以我最终反而更成功了，而不是更不成功。

sentences.en: The aligned with thing is interesting. I'm going to try and put this across as delicately as I can.
sentences.zh: “志趣相投”这一点很有意思。我会尽量委婉地表达这一点。

sentences.en: I would say from the bit of time that we've spent together, you have a really interesting trait of holistic selfishness.
sentences.zh: 我想说，从我们相处的这段时间来看，你有一个非常有趣的特质，那就是“整体性的自私”。

sentences.en: You're sort of prepared to put yourself first.
sentences.zh: 你似乎总是准备好把自己放在第一位。

sentences.en: You seem largely unfazed by saying or doing things that might result in other people feeling a little bit awkward if it's truthful for you.
sentences.zh: 对于那些如果说出来会让人感到有点尴尬的话，你似乎完全不在意，只要那是你的真实想法。

sentences.en: It's like unapologetically self-prioritizing, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想，这就像是毫无歉意地优先考虑自己。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think everybody is. Maybe unapologetic is the part that's relatively rare, but I think everybody puts themselves first.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想每个人都是这样。也许“毫无歉意”这一点相对少见，但我认为每个人都会把自己放在第一位。

sentences.en: That's just human nature. You're here because you survive.
sentences.zh: 这是人性使然。你之所以存在，是因为你生存了下来。

sentences.en: You're a separate organism. That's interesting.
sentences.zh: 你是一个独立的有机体。这很有趣。

sentences.en: Maybe, but... I know we like to virtue signal and pretend we're doing it for each other.
sentences.zh: 也许吧，但……我知道我们喜欢进行道德标榜，假装我们是在为彼此着想。

sentences.en: How many times does somebody say, yeah, of course, I'd love to come to the wedding.
sentences.zh: 有多少次，有人说：“好啊，我当然很乐意去参加婚礼。”

sentences.en: And they're like, I don't want to be at the fucking wedding.
sentences.zh: 而他们心里想的是：“我才不想去参加那该死的婚礼。”

sentences.en: How many times does someone say, how are you doing today?
sentences.zh: 有多少次，有人问：“你今天过得怎么样？”

sentences.en: And they don't tell you. I don't go to weddings.
sentences.zh: 而他们并没有告诉你实话。我不去参加婚礼。

sentences.en: But this is my point. So I don't think you're necessarily right with that.
sentences.zh: 但这就是我的观点。所以我不认为你在这点上一定是对的。

sentences.en: I think that people do. I don't think they put themselves first.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们确实会那样做。我不认为他们把自己放在第一位。

sentences.en: I sometimes think that they compromise what it is that they want in order to appease socially what's in front of them.
sentences.zh: 我有时觉得，为了安抚眼前的社交需求，他们妥协了自己真正想要的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, I just view it as everyone's wasting their time on it.
sentences.zh: 是的，我只是觉得每个人都在为此浪费时间。

sentences.en: Don't do something you don't want to do. why are you wasting your time there's so little time on this earth life goes fast what are the 4 000 weeks that's your lifespan um and and yes we hear that but we don't remember it but uh i guess i'm keenly aware of how little time i have so i'm just not going to waste it How have you got more comfortable at being the unapologetic self-prioritizer?
sentences.zh: 不要做你不想做的事。为什么要浪费时间呢？在这个地球上时间太少了，生命过得很快，人的一生大约只有四千周。嗯，是的，我们听过这些，但我们没记住。不过，我想我非常清楚自己剩下的时间有多么少，所以我绝不会浪费它。你是如何变得更从容地去做一个毫无歉意的“自我优先者”的？

sentences.en: Yeah, I've gotten utterly more and more ruthless on it.
sentences.zh: 是的，我在这方面变得越来越冷酷了。

sentences.en: Mainly, it's that I see or hear people's freedom, and then that liberates me further.
sentences.zh: 主要是因为我看到或听到了人们的自由，这进一步解放了我。

sentences.en: So I read a blog post by P. Mark, aka Mark Andreessen, where he said, don't keep a schedule.
sentences.zh: 所以我读了一篇 P. Mark（也就是 Mark Andreessen）的博客文章，他说：不要制定日程表。

sentences.en: And I took that to heart. So I deleted my calendar, and I don't keep a schedule.
sentences.zh: 我把这话记在心里了。所以我删除了我的日历，我不再制定日程表。

sentences.en: I try to remember it all in my head. If I can't remember it, I'm not going to add it to my schedule.
sentences.zh: 我试着把一切都记在脑子里。如果我记不住，我就不会把它加到我的日程里。

sentences.en: I'm glad you got here on time. Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你准时到了这里。是的，没错。

sentences.en: I had to look things up at the last minute.
sentences.zh: 我不得不最后一刻才去查这些事。

sentences.en: But ironically, I don't even know if Mark himself follows that, but he made the correct point.
sentences.zh: 但讽刺的是，我甚至不知道 Mark 自己是否遵循这一点，但他提出了正确的观点。

sentences.en: I read a little story about Jack Dorsey doing all his business off his iPhone and iPad and not even going into a Mac.
sentences.zh: 我读过一个小故事，说 Jack Dorsey 所有的业务都是在 iPhone 和 iPad 上完成的，甚至不用 Mac。

sentences.en: And I said, okay, I want to do that. So I'm going to operate through text messaging and I put up my nasty email.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，我也想那样做。所以我打算通过短信来处理事务，并且我设置了我的“讨厌的”自动回复邮件。

sentences.en: Does that feel like more freedom? It does, yeah, because you're on the go.
sentences.zh: 那感觉更自由了吗？是的，确实，因为你可以随时随地处理事情。

sentences.en: So I have a nasty email autoresponder that says, I don't check email and don't text me either, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我有一个讨厌的自动回复邮件，上面写着：我不看邮件，也别给我发短信，好吗？

sentences.en: If you need to find me, you'll find me. Obviously, some of this is a luxury of success, but some of these habits I adopted long before, actually.
sentences.zh: 如果你需要找到我，你自然会找到我。显然，这其中一部分是成功的红利，但其中一些习惯我其实很早就养成了。

sentences.en: The hostile email autoresponder started a long time ago.
sentences.zh: 那个不友好的自动回复邮件是很久以前就开始的。

sentences.en: I used to own the domain. I let it go. Don'tdocoffee.com.
sentences.zh: 我曾经拥有过那个域名。后来我放弃了。Don'tdocoffee.com。

sentences.en: I don't do coffee.com. I used to reply from that email just so people would get the point.
sentences.zh: 我不喝咖啡网。我过去常从那个邮箱回复，只是为了让人们明白我的意思。

sentences.en: But I stopped being rude about it. Now I just ghost.
sentences.zh: 但我不再对此表现得粗鲁了。现在我只是直接“玩失踪”。

sentences.en: I just disappear. My wife knows not to ever book or schedule me for anything.
sentences.zh: 我只是消失。我妻子知道永远不要帮我预订或安排任何事情。

sentences.en: I'm not expected to go to couples' dinners.
sentences.zh: 没人指望我去参加情侣晚餐。

sentences.en: I'm not expected to go to birthdays. I'm not expected to go to weddings.
sentences.zh: 没人指望我去参加生日派对。没人指望我去参加婚礼。

sentences.en: If somebody tries to rope her into having me show up, she says he makes his own decisions.
sentences.zh: 如果有人试图拉她让我出席，她会说：他自己做决定。

sentences.en: You got to ask him directly. And vice versa.
sentences.zh: 你得直接问他。反之亦然。

sentences.en: Are you not killing serendipity in a way, Dad?
sentences.zh: 爸爸，你这样难道不是在扼杀偶然的惊喜吗？

sentences.en: No, no. I'm freeing up all my time. So my entire life is serendipity.
sentences.zh: 不，不。我是在腾出我所有的时间。所以我的整个人生都是偶然的惊喜。

sentences.en: I get to interact with whoever I want, whenever I want, wherever I want.
sentences.zh: 我可以随时、随地、与任何我想见的人互动。

sentences.en: So you'll hear the invite, but make the decision? because if you're if there's fewer things in coming you're assuming that you know what's i don't commit to anything in the future so i'll say okay if that thing is interesting i'll see if i can get in that day when i'm in the mood but there's nothing worse than something coming up that your past self committed you to your present self doesn't want to do god damn it past it of all yeah and then it destroys your entire calendar uh it destroys your day because there's like oh this one hour slot which is sitting like a turd on my calendar that i have to like schedule my whole day around i can't do anything at 20 minutes before the 20 minutes afterwards even for phone calls if someone wants to do a phone call say okay just text me when you're free i'll text you when i'm free and we'll just do it on the fly it's a much better way of living than this overly scheduled uh you know cal.com or i cal whatever the uh the overscheduled life is not worth living it's not i think it's a terrible way to live life that's not how we evolve it's not how we grew up it's not how we were as children hopefully unless you have a helicopter parent or a tiger mom your natural order is freedom i had a friend who uh said to me once you know uh i never want to have to be at a specific place at a specific time and i was like oh my god that's freedom when i heard that that changed my life right you still a alarm clock alarm clockless yes i'm alarm clock today i did set my alarm just so i wouldn't miss very important yeah if you still just so you know i set the alarm clock from 11 a.m in case i was stricken with a flu i wasn't gonna set my alarm clock for 8 a.m. or 9 a.m.
sentences.zh: 所以你会听到邀请，但会自己做决定？因为如果你……如果进来的事情变少了，你是在假设你知道什么是……我不对未来的任何事情做承诺，所以我会说，好吧，如果那件事很有趣，我会看看那天我是否有心情去参加。但没有什么比你过去的自己为你承诺了某事，而现在的你却不想做更糟糕的了。该死的过去的自己！是的，然后它会毁了你的整个日历。它会毁了你的一天，因为就像，“哦，这一个小时的空档就像一坨屎一样卡在我的日历上”，我必须围绕它来安排我的一整天。我甚至不能在它之前或之后的20分钟里做任何事。即使是打电话，如果有人想通话，我会说，好吧，当你空闲时给我发短信，我空闲时也会给你发短信，我们随时随地进行。这比那种过度安排的生活方式好得多，你知道的，cal.com 或者 iCal，无论那种过度安排的生活是什么，都不值得过。真的不值得。我认为那是一种糟糕的生活方式，那不是我们进化而来的方式，不是我们成长的方式，也不是我们小时候的样子。除非你有直升机父母或虎妈，否则你自然的秩序就是自由。我有个朋友曾经对我说：“你知道吗，我永远不想被迫在特定的时间出现在特定的地点。”我当时就想，天哪，那就是自由。当我听到那句话时，它改变了我的人生。对吧？你现在还是不用闹钟吗？不用闹钟，是的。今天我确实设了闹钟，只是为了不耽误非常重要的事情。是的，如果你还……只是为了让你知道，我把闹钟设在上午11点，以防我得了流感。我可不会把闹钟设在早上8点或9点。

sentences.en: And sure enough, I got up many hours before that.
sentences.zh: 果然，我在那之前好几个小时就起床了。

sentences.en: But it was sort of a backup emergency alarm.
sentences.zh: 但这算是一种备用的紧急闹钟。

sentences.en: In fact, sometimes when I have something that I need to do, I don't want to look at a calendar.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有时当我需要做某事时，我不想看日历。

sentences.en: So I'll just set an alarm for it. Just sink a little bit more into that.
sentences.zh: 所以我只会为它设一个闹钟。

sentences.en: Like kind of like that fuck you energy, that self-prioritizing energy, because I think people rationally love the idea of this.
sentences.zh: 再深入探讨一下这一点。就像那种“去你的”能量，那种自我优先的能量，因为我认为人们在理性上很喜欢这个想法。

sentences.en: I'm going to do what only I want to do, even if they've got the level of freedom.
sentences.zh: “我要做我只想做的事”，即使他们已经拥有了那种程度的自由。

sentences.en: It's not fuck you energy in the sense that I think everyone should live their life that way to the greatest extent possible.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说“去你的”能量，我的意思是，我认为每个人都应该在最大程度上那样生活。

sentences.en: Obviously, we have our requirements around work and obligations that are genuinely important to us, but don't fritter away your life on randomly scheduled things. and things that aren't important don't matter and events and weddings and you know tedious dinners with tedious people that you don't want to go to to the extent you can bring freedom into your life optimized for that you'll actually be more productive you won't just be happier more free you will be more productive because then you can focus on what is in front of you whatever the biggest problem of that day when i wake up in the morning the first four hours are when i have the most energy and that's when i want to solve all the hard problems and the next four hours are when I kind of want to do some more outdoorsy activities or I want to work out or maybe I can have some meetings, but I'll try to do those last second based on whatever the day's priorities demand.
sentences.zh: 显然，我们在工作和义务方面有对我们真正重要的要求，但不要把你的生命浪费在随机安排的事情上。那些不重要的事情根本不重要，比如活动、婚礼，还有那些你不想参加的、与无聊的人进行的无聊晚餐。在你能将自由带入生活的范围内，优化它，你实际上会更有效率。你不仅会更快乐、更自由，你还会更有效率，因为那时你可以专注于眼前的事情。无论我早上醒来时当天最大的问题是什么，前四个小时是我精力最充沛的时候，那是我想要解决所有难题的时候。接下来的四个小时，我可能想做一些户外活动，或者我想锻炼，或者也许我可以开一些会议，但我会尽量根据当天优先事项的需求在最后一刻决定。

sentences.en: The last four hours, I kind of want to wind down.
sentences.zh: 最后四个小时，我有点想放松一下。

sentences.en: I want to hang out with the kids and I want to play games or read a book or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我想和孩子们待在一起，我想玩游戏或读本书之类的。

sentences.en: So having that flexibility and freedom is really important.
sentences.zh: 所以拥有那种灵活性和自由是非常重要的。

sentences.en: So you can just put whatever is most needed into the slot at that moment. and instead if I have like a meeting at 2 p.m and then I have to like get a thing and some emails done and I put that off till 6 p.m and I'm rushing, I'm not gonna be productive.
sentences.zh: 这样你就可以在那个时刻把最需要做的事情放进那个空档里。相反，如果我下午2点有个会议，然后我必须去处理一件事和一些邮件，我把这些推迟到下午6点，然后我就会很匆忙，我不会有效率的。

sentences.en: I'm not gonna be... You're certainly not free.
sentences.zh: 我不会……你当然也不自由。

sentences.en: I'm definitely not free. But also another thing that I really believe is that inspiration is perishable.
sentences.zh: 我绝对不自由。但还有一件事我深信不疑，那就是灵感是易逝的。

sentences.en: Act on it immediately. So when you're inspired to do something, do that thing.
sentences.zh: 立即行动。所以当你受到启发去做某事时，就去做那件事。

sentences.en: If I'm inspired to write a blog post, I wanna do it at that moment.
sentences.zh: 如果我受到启发想写一篇博客文章，我想在那一刻就写。

sentences.en: If I'm inspired to send a tweet, I wanna do it at that moment.
sentences.zh: 如果我受到启发想发一条推文，我想在那一刻就发。

sentences.en: If I'm inspired to solve a problem, I wanna do it at that moment.
sentences.zh: 如果我受到启发想解决一个问题，我想在那一刻就解决。

sentences.en: If I'm inspired to read a book, I want to read it right then.
sentences.zh: 如果我受到启发想读一本书，我想就在那时读。

sentences.en: If I'm inspired to solve a problem, I'll solve it right there.
sentences.zh: 如果我受到启发想解决一个问题，我会就在那里解决它。

sentences.en: If I want to learn something, I do it at the moment of curiosity.
sentences.zh: 如果我想学习什么，我会在好奇心产生的瞬间去做。

sentences.en: The moment the curiosity arrives, I go learn that thing immediately.
sentences.zh: 好奇心到来的那一刻，我立刻去学习那个东西。

sentences.en: I download the book. I get on Google. I get on ChatGPT, whatever.
sentences.zh: 我下载书。我上谷歌。我用 ChatGPT，随便什么都行。

sentences.en: I will figure that thing out on the spot.
sentences.zh: 我会当场弄明白那件事。

sentences.en: And that's when the learning happens. It doesn't happen because I've scheduled time, because I've set an hour aside.
sentences.zh: 那就是学习发生的时候。它不是因为我安排了时间，因为我预留了一个小时而发生的。

sentences.en: Because when that time arrives, I might be in a different mood.
sentences.zh: 因为当那个时间到来时，我的心情可能已经变了。

sentences.en: I might just want to do something different.
sentences.zh: 我可能只想做点别的事情。

sentences.en: So I think that spontaneity is really important.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为自发性真的很重要。

sentences.en: You're going to learn best when you're having fun, when you generally are enjoying the process, not when you're forced to sit there and do it.
sentences.zh: 当你玩得开心时，当你真正享受这个过程时，你会学得最好，而不是当你被迫坐在那里去做的时候。

sentences.en: How much do you remember from school? You were forced to learn geography, history, mathematics on this schedule at this time, according to this person.
sentences.zh: 你还记得学校里的多少东西？你被迫在那个时间、按照那个人的日程表去学习地理、历史、数学。

sentences.en: Didn't happen. All the stuff that sticks with you is you learned it when you wanted to, when you genuinely had the desire.
sentences.zh: 根本没记住。所有留在你脑海里的东西，都是你在想学的时候，在你真正有欲望的时候学到的。

sentences.en: And that freedom, that ability to act on something the moment you want to is so liberating that most of us go through our lives with very, very little tastes of that.
sentences.zh: 而那种自由，那种在你想做某事的那一刻就去行动的能力，是如此令人解放，以至于我们大多数人一生中都很少尝到那种滋味。

sentences.en: If you live your entire life that way, that is a recipe for happiness.
sentences.zh: 如果你一生都那样生活，那就是通往幸福的秘诀。

sentences.en: It feels like efficiency.
sentences.zh: 这感觉像是效率。

sentences.en: It's efficient also. You have the inspiration.
sentences.zh: 它也很高效。你有了灵感。

sentences.en: That is going to be the most frictionless time to ever do that particular task.
sentences.zh: 那将是完成那项特定任务最顺畅、最无阻碍的时刻。

sentences.en: So, oh, I've had the inspiration to do that.
sentences.zh: 所以，哦，我有了做那件事的灵感。

sentences.en: I'll put that off until a time when I no longer really want to do it quite so much.
sentences.zh: 我把它推迟到一个我不再那么想做的时候。

sentences.en: And while I do want to do that thing, I'll do something else that I needed to do because it's on the schedule.
sentences.zh: 而在我确实想做那件事的时候，我却在做另一件我需要做的事，因为它在日程表上。

sentences.en: It does not work. Procrastination is because you don't want to do that thing right now.
sentences.zh: 这行不通。拖延是因为你现在不想做那件事。

sentences.en: You want to do something else. Go do that something else.
sentences.zh: 你想做别的事。那就去做别的事吧。

sentences.en: I reject this frame that efficiency and productivity and success are counter to happiness and freedom They actually go together How so?
sentences.zh: 我拒绝这种认为效率、生产力和成功与幸福和自由背道而驰的框架。它们实际上是相辅相成的。怎么说？

sentences.en: The happier you are, the more you can sustain doing something The more likely you're going to do something that will in turn make you even happier And you'll continue to do it and you'll outwork everybody else The more free you are, the better you can allocate your time And the less you're caught up in a web of obligations and commitments And the more you can focus on the task at hand This is related to another insight of yours the less you want something, the less you're thinking about it, the less you're obsessing over it, the more you're going to do it in a natural way.
sentences.zh: 你越快乐，你就越能持续地做某事。你越有可能做一些反过来让你更快乐的事情。你会继续做下去，你会比任何人都努力。你越自由，你就越能分配你的时间。你越少陷入义务和承诺的网中，你就越能专注于手头的任务。这与你的另一个见解有关：你越不想要某样东西，你对它的想法就越少，你对它的执念就越少，你就越会以自然的方式去做它。

sentences.en: The more you're going to do it for yourself, you're going to do it in a way that you're good at, and you're going to stick with it.
sentences.zh: 你越会为了自己去做它，你会以你擅长的方式去做它，并且你会坚持下去。

sentences.en: The people around you will see the quality of your work is higher.
sentences.zh: 你周围的人会看到你的工作质量更高。

sentences.en: But this seems like a difficult tension to navigate, because an obsessive attention to detail is a competitive advantage of your work as well.
sentences.zh: 但这似乎是一个难以驾驭的紧张关系，因为对细节的痴迷也是你工作的一种竞争优势。

sentences.en: So you have these two things sort of conflicting with each other. no one is going to beat you at being you if it so one of the things i like to say is like find what feels like play to you but looks like work to others So it looks like work to them, but to you, it feels like play.
sentences.zh: 所以你有这两样东西在某种程度上相互冲突。没有人能在做自己这件事上打败你。所以我喜欢说的一句话是：找到那些对你来说感觉像玩耍，但对别人来说看起来像工作的事情。所以对他们来说看起来像工作，但对你来说，感觉就像玩耍。

sentences.en: It's not work. So you're going to out-compete them because you're doing it effortlessly.
sentences.zh: 这不是工作。所以你会胜过他们，因为你在毫不费力地做它。

sentences.en: You're doing it for fun. They're doing it for work.
sentences.zh: 你在为了乐趣而做它。他们在为了工作而做它。

sentences.en: They're doing it for some byproduct. To you, it's art.
sentences.zh: 他们在为了某种副产品而做它。对你来说，这是艺术。

sentences.en: It's beauty. It's joy. It's flow. It's fulfilling.
sentences.zh: 这是美。这是快乐。这是心流。这是满足。

sentences.en: You must enjoy podcasting. If you didn't, you wouldn't be good at it.
sentences.zh: 你一定很享受做播客。如果你不享受，你就不会擅长它。

sentences.en: You would have lost it. You would have done 900 episodes either.
sentences.zh: 你早就放弃了。你也不会做900期节目。

sentences.en: Right. If you decided that the right way to get ahead in life was to go write books, nobody would have heard of you.
sentences.zh: 没错。如果你决定在生活中取得领先的正确方式是去写书，没人会听说过你。

sentences.en: Chris Williamson's book would be a complete flop.
sentences.zh: Chris Williamson 的书会彻底失败。

sentences.en: That's not who you are. You're a podcaster.
sentences.zh: 那不是你。你是个播客主持人。

sentences.en: You enjoy talking to people. You enjoy interviewing them.
sentences.zh: 你喜欢和人交谈。你喜欢采访他们。

sentences.en: The more you do things that are natural to you, the less competition you have.
sentences.zh: 你越做那些对你来说自然而然的事情，你的竞争就越少。

sentences.en: You escape competition through authenticity, by being your own self.
sentences.zh: 你通过真实性，通过做你自己，逃离了竞争。

sentences.en: If I had to summarize how to be successful in life in two words, I would just say productize yourself.
sentences.zh: 如果我必须用两个词来总结如何在生活中取得成功，我会说：产品化你自己。

sentences.en: That's it. just figure out what it is that you naturally do that the world might want that you can scale up and turn into a product and it'll be it'll eventually be effortless for you yes there's always work required but it won't even feel like work to you it'll feel like play to you and modern society gives us that opportunity you know if you were 2 000 years ago you're born on a farm your choices are very limited right you're going to do stuff on that farm now you can literally wake up and you can move to a different city.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。找出你自然而然会做的事情，世界可能需要它，你可以将其规模化并转化为产品，最终这对你来说将毫不费力。是的，总是需要工作，但这甚至不会让你觉得是在工作，它会让你觉得是在玩耍。现代社会给了我们这个机会，你知道，如果你是在2000年前，你出生在农场，你的选择非常有限，对吧？你只能在那个农场做事情。现在你可以真正地醒来，搬到另一个城市。

sentences.en: You can switch careers. You can switch jobs.
sentences.zh: 你可以转换职业。你可以换工作。

sentences.en: You can change the people that you're with.
sentences.zh: 你可以改变你身边的人。

sentences.en: You know, you can change so many things about who you are and who you're with and what you're doing that there is infinite opportunity out there for you, literally infinite.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可以改变关于你是谁、你和谁在一起、你在做什么的这么多事情，以至于那里有无限的机会，真的是无限的。

sentences.en: And so it's much better to treat this like a search function, to find the people who need you the most, to find the work that needs you the most, to find the place you're best suited to be at.
sentences.zh: 所以把这当作一个搜索功能要好得多，去找到最需要你的人，去找到最需要你的工作，去找到你最适合待的地方。

sentences.en: And it's worthwhile to spend time in that exploration before diving into exploitation.
sentences.zh: 在投入开发之前，花时间进行那种探索是值得的。

sentences.en: The biggest mistake in a world with so many choices is premature commitment.
sentences.zh: 在一个有这么多选择的世界里，最大的错误就是过早承诺。
