sentences.en: If you prematurely commit to being a lawyer or a doctor, and now you've got like, you know, five years invested into that, you might have just completely missed.
sentences.zh: 如果你过早地承诺成为一名律师或医生，现在你已经投入了五年时间，你可能完全错过了。

sentences.en: You might just end up in the wrong profession, the wrong place, the wrong people for 30 years of your life grinding away.
sentences.zh: 你可能最终会在错误的职业、错误的地方、与错误的人一起度过你生命中的30年，在那儿苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: And yes, the best time to figure that out was before, but the second best time is now.
sentences.zh: 是的，弄清楚这件事的最佳时间是之前，但第二个最佳时间就是现在。

sentences.en: So just change it. And also presumably kill things that aren't working very quickly. by default you should kill everything you know if you can't decide the answer is no and most things you just be saying no to the part of my keeping my calendar free is just by default saying no to everything do i want to create a calendar just to add your event right or to add your need or your desire one of the other things about you know like early on in life you're looking for opportunities so you're saying yes to everything and that is a phase that you go through.
sentences.zh: 所以直接改变它。而且大概还要很快地砍掉那些行不通的事情。默认情况下，你应该砍掉一切。你知道，如果你不能决定，答案就是“不”。大多数事情你都应该说“不”。我保持日历空闲的一部分原因就是默认对一切说“不”。我难道要为了添加你的活动，或者为了添加你的需求或欲望，而去创建一个日历吗？关于人生早期阶段，你是在寻找机会，所以你对一切都说“是”，那是你经历的一个阶段。

sentences.en: That is the exploration phase. Later, when you found the thing you want to work on, you're in the exploitation phase.
sentences.zh: 那是探索阶段。后来，当你找到了你想做的事情时，你就进入了开发阶段。

sentences.en: You have to say no to everything by default.
sentences.zh: 你必须默认对一切说“不”。

sentences.en: And if you don't say no to everything by default, if you have to even explicitly go out of your way to say no to something, that will take up time.
sentences.zh: 如果你不默认对一切说“不”，如果你甚至必须明确地费尽心思去拒绝某事，那会占用时间。

sentences.en: For example, you know, there are a lot of people out there who are into hustle culture.
sentences.zh: 例如，你知道，外面有很多热衷于“奋斗文化”的人。

sentences.en: And a big piece of hustle culture is like, well, you're not going to get something if you don't ask for it.
sentences.zh: 奋斗文化的一大块内容是：好吧，如果你不要求，你就得不到什么。

sentences.en: So they'll hustle people. They'll always be sending you requests, messages.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会去“奋斗”别人。他们总是会给你发送请求、消息。

sentences.en: Yeah, this is a famous person problem, but I have it.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个名人问题，但我也有这个问题。

sentences.en: And people are always asking me for things.
sentences.zh: 人们总是向我索要东西。

sentences.en: And I kind of squirm when I get these messages.
sentences.zh: 当我收到这些消息时，我有点坐立不安。

sentences.en: And I'm sure you get these two text messages, emails saying, hey, Chris, my friend so-and-so should really be on your podcast, or you should come to my event, you should write a forward for my book.
sentences.zh: 我相信你也会收到这些短信、邮件，说：嘿，Chris，我的某某朋友真的应该上你的播客，或者你应该来参加我的活动，你应该为我的书写序。

sentences.en: And you kind of squirm when you get this, right?
sentences.zh: 当你收到这个时，你会有点坐立不安，对吧？

sentences.en: You have to figure out how to say no. And one of the things I learned along the way is that if you wouldn't ask somebody else to do it, and then you get that request yourself, you can just dismiss it.
sentences.zh: 你必须弄清楚如何说“不”。我一路学到的一件事是，如果你不会要求别人去做某事，那么当你自己收到那个请求时，你可以直接无视它。

sentences.en: You don't have to respond. You don't even let it enter your brain.
sentences.zh: 你不需要回复。你甚至不需要让它进入你的大脑。

sentences.en: You have to be able to delete emails and text messages without flinching if you want to scale.
sentences.zh: 如果你想扩大规模，你必须能够毫不犹豫地删除邮件和短信。

sentences.en: And scaling is very important. Scaling your time is really important.
sentences.zh: 而规模化非常重要。规模化你的时间非常重要。

sentences.en: Every interruption will take you out of flow.
sentences.zh: 每一次中断都会让你脱离心流。

sentences.en: So the only way you can remain in flow is if you get either very good at ignoring these things by default or closing yourself off like a hermit, like our mutual friend Tim Ferriss does.
sentences.zh: 所以你保持心流的唯一方法是，要么你非常擅长默认忽略这些事情，要么像我们的共同朋友 Tim Ferriss 那样把自己封闭起来，像个隐士一样。

sentences.en: You just become emotionally capable of not registering these as something that causes turbulence inside of you.
sentences.zh: 你只是在情感上变得有能力不去把这些注册为引起你内心动荡的事情。

sentences.en: That not registering it emotionally thing, is that a...
sentences.zh: 那种在情感上不去注册它的事情，那是……

sentences.en: It's fundamental. That's so fundamental to so many things in life.
sentences.zh: 这是根本性的。这对生活中的许多事情来说太根本了。

sentences.en: Okay. Can we dig into that a little bit?
sentences.zh: 好的。我们可以深入探讨一下吗？

sentences.en: Because again, I've only seen you as you, right?
sentences.zh: 因为同样，我只见过作为你的你，对吧？

sentences.en: I didn't know you 20 years ago. I didn't know you as a child.
sentences.zh: 我20年前不认识你。我不知道你小时候是什么样。

sentences.en: So I've only seen you with this holistic selfishness, the integrated self-private. prioritization, whatever we, I don't know what we called it.
sentences.zh: 所以我只见过你这种整体性的自私，这种整合的自我优先，无论我们……我不知道我们叫它什么。

sentences.en: Selfish is fine. I'll take selfish. I'm selfish.
sentences.zh: 自私很好。我接受自私。我很自私。

sentences.en: I'm a very selfish person. Don't contact me.
sentences.zh: 我是一个非常自私的人。别联系我。

sentences.en: Yeah, that emotional reaction. Whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，那种情绪反应。无论它是什么。

sentences.en: I also get the sense too that maybe people have lived obligation life for so long that they actually kind of struggle to tap into what it is that they want.
sentences.zh: 我也感觉到，也许人们过这种“义务生活”太久了，以至于他们实际上很难触及他们真正想要的是什么。

sentences.en: They've hidden their wants and their desires and their needs, and they've deprioritized themselves so much for so long.
sentences.zh: 他们隐藏了自己的需求和欲望，他们为了别人把自己降级了太久太久。

sentences.en: They go, what do I want, actually? What is it?
sentences.zh: 他们会问：我到底想要什么？是什么？

sentences.en: Do I want to go to this thing or not? Because all I've done is be fucking puppeted, right?
sentences.zh: 我是想去参加这个活动还是不想？因为我所做的只是像个木偶一样，对吧？

sentences.en: I've been marionetted by other people's desires for so, so, so long.
sentences.zh: 我被别人的欲望像提线木偶一样操纵了太久太久。

sentences.en: I can't even tap into that anymore. And saying no feels like a war crime.
sentences.zh: 我甚至无法再触及那个了。而说“不”感觉就像战争罪行一样。

sentences.en: So I think it's really good to be able to view your own mind and your own thoughts objectively.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为能够客观地审视自己的思想和想法真的很好。

sentences.en: And that is the big benefit of meditation.
sentences.zh: 而这就是冥想的巨大好处。

sentences.en: It creates a small gap between your conscious observation, self, and your mind.
sentences.zh: 它在你的意识观察者、自我和你的思想之间创造了一个小小的间隙。

sentences.en: And And that lets you then look at your thoughts and evaluate them a little bit like you would a third party's statements.
sentences.zh: 这让你能够审视你的想法，并评估它们，有点像你评估第三方的陈述一样。

sentences.en: And if you just take your mind to be you and they're integrated in one and the same at all times and you're reacting from the mind, then you're not even going to question things that come into your mind.
sentences.zh: 如果你只是把你的思想当作你自己，并且它们在任何时候都整合为一体，而你又在从思想中做出反应，那么你甚至不会质疑进入你脑海的事情。

sentences.en: Anything that comes in that creates a reaction will immediately create a reaction.
sentences.zh: 任何进入并产生反应的东西都会立即产生反应。

sentences.en: But if you can observe your thoughts a little bit and not in some way, but you can even just do it through therapy.
sentences.zh: 但如果你能稍微观察一下你的想法，不是以某种方式，你甚至可以通过治疗来做到这一点。

sentences.en: You can do it through journaling. You can do it any way you would like.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过写日记来做到。你可以用任何你喜欢的方式来做到。

sentences.en: You can just take long walks. You don't have to meditate and do lotus position. all that is unnecessary.
sentences.zh: 你可以只是去散长步。你不必非得冥想和做莲花坐，所有这些都是不必要的。

sentences.en: But if you can observe your own thoughts and view them a little objectively, then you can start being a little more choosy, a little more critical.
sentences.zh: 但如果你能观察自己的想法，并稍微客观地看待它们，你就可以开始变得更挑剔、更具批判性。

sentences.en: And you can realize that there are no problems in the real world other than maybe things that inflict pain on your body.
sentences.zh: 你会意识到，除了那些会给身体带来痛苦的事情外，现实世界中根本没有所谓的“问题”。

sentences.en: Everything else has to become a problem in your mind first.
sentences.zh: 其他所有事情，都必须先在你的脑海中变成一个“问题”。

sentences.en: You have to view it and interpret it and create a narrative that it is a problem before it becomes a problem.
sentences.zh: 你必须先观察它、解读它，并编造一个叙事，认定它是个问题，它才会真的成为问题。

sentences.en: And then you realize that a lot of your emotional energy is spent on reacting to things that your mind is automatically saying are problems.
sentences.zh: 然后你会发现，你大部分的情绪能量都消耗在对那些大脑自动判定为“问题”的事情做出反应上。

sentences.en: And you don't need all those problems. Do you really need that many problems in your life?
sentences.zh: 你其实并不需要那么多问题。你的生活中真的需要那么多问题吗？

sentences.en: Again, I would say, try to focus on just one overarching problem and then go solve that problem.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我会建议你试着只专注于一个核心问题，然后去解决它。

sentences.en: It's like, if you want to be successful, define success very concretely, focus on that and everything else.
sentences.zh: 就像如果你想成功，就把成功定义得非常具体，专注于那个目标，剩下的事情就别管了。

sentences.en: When it enters your mind, it becomes a problem, whether it's a judgment about the girl walking down the street or the car that just cut in front you or whether it's like, you know, this, your accountant did this stupid thing.
sentences.zh: 当任何事情进入你的大脑，它就变成了一个问题，无论是对街上走过的女孩的评判，还是刚才别你车的车，又或者是你会计做的蠢事。

sentences.en: Like, yes, it's going to trigger you, but observe for a moment that like, it's triggering me.
sentences.zh: 没错，这些确实会触发你的情绪，但请观察片刻，意识到“这正在触发我的情绪”。

sentences.en: I've created a problem. Do I really want to have this problem right now?
sentences.zh: 我制造了一个问题。我现在真的想拥有这个问题吗？

sentences.en: Do I want to spend the energy on this problem or do I want that going somewhere else?
sentences.zh: 我是想把能量花在这个问题上，还是想把它用在别的地方？

sentences.en: And it doesn't have to be that overt. You don't have to, the mind mud wrestling with itself is also a problem because I'd love to do that.
sentences.zh: 而且这不必表现得那么明显。你不需要——大脑自己跟自己打架也是个问题，因为我其实很喜欢那样做。

sentences.en: I have, my problems have got problems and I have a real problem about fixing my problems.
sentences.zh: 我有，我的问题还有衍生问题，而且我在解决问题这件事上本身就有个大问题。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly. So you're going to be much happier and much more focused.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。所以你会变得更快乐、更专注。

sentences.en: Again, I think happiness and focus and success can kind of complement each other.
sentences.zh: 再次重申，我认为快乐、专注和成功是可以相辅相成的。

sentences.en: You're going to have much more energy. Just think about it as mental energy.
sentences.zh: 你会拥有更多的能量。就把这看作是心理能量吧。

sentences.en: You're going to have much more mental energy to focus on the actual problems you want to solve if you don't start unconsciously, subconsciously, reactively picking up problems everywhere. so before anything can be a problem that takes up your emotional energy you have to accept it as a problem you can be choosy about your problems and i'm not saying i'm perfect in that regard but i think i'm better than i used to be well lots of people are addicted to solving problems right so much so that sometimes times. people create problems when we don't have any simply so that we can solve them we have that going on and then even worse is we take on problems that we can't affect so uh you know another one of my little quips was uh you know a rational person uh can uh sort of uh a rational person should should cultivate indifference to things that are out of their control right or a rational person can find peace by cultivating indifference to things that are out of their control.
sentences.zh: 如果你不开始无意识地、潜意识地、被动地到处捡问题，你就会有更多的心理能量去专注于你真正想解决的问题。所以，在任何事情成为消耗你情绪能量的“问题”之前，你必须先接受它是个问题。你可以对自己的问题有所选择。我并不是说我在这一点上做得完美，但我认为我比过去好多了。嗯，很多人都对解决问题上瘾，对吧？甚至到了有时候我们没有问题也要制造问题的地步，仅仅是为了去解决它们。我们确实有这种情况，更糟糕的是，我们还去承担那些我们根本无法影响的问题。你知道，我的另一个小俏皮话是：一个理性的人，应该培养对那些无法控制之事的冷漠，或者说，一个理性的人可以通过对无法控制之事保持冷漠来获得内心的平静。

sentences.en: And I'm as guilty as anybody of doom surfing on X or social media and getting worked up about things that I can't do anything about, right?
sentences.zh: 我也和任何人一样，会陷入在 X 或社交媒体上刷负面新闻的怪圈，并为那些我无能为力的事情感到焦虑，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, do I want to be fighting those battles in my mind when I literally cannot do anything about it?
sentences.zh: 比如，当我在这些事情上真的无能为力时，我真的想在脑海里打这些仗吗？

sentences.en: So if you find yourself looping on a problem, like you're watching the news too much and you're getting caught up in a problem you can't do anything about, you have to step away from that.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你发现自己陷入了问题的死循环，比如你看新闻太多，被一些你无法改变的问题困住了，你就必须远离它。

sentences.en: And modern media is a delivery mechanism for mimetic viruses.
sentences.zh: 现代媒体是模因病毒的传播机制。

sentences.en: And what's happened now is, you know, 100 years ago, 500 years ago, if something wasn't happening in your immediate vicinity, you wouldn't hear about it.
sentences.zh: 现在的情况是，你知道，在 100 年前、500 年前，如果某件事不是发生在你的直接周边，你根本不会听说。

sentences.en: It wouldn't be a problem for you. But now every single one of the world's problems has turned into a mimetic virus, which is going into the battlefield of the news and is trying to infect your mind in real time.
sentences.zh: 那对你来说就不会是个问题。但现在，世界上每一个问题都变成了模因病毒，它们冲进新闻的战场，试图实时感染你的大脑。

sentences.en: Hyperspeed. Yeah. So that you become obsessed with the war in Ukraine, which is really far away, or you get obsessed with climate change or you get obsessed with AI doom or you get obsessed with whatever.
sentences.zh: 以极快的速度。是的。让你沉迷于远在天边的乌克兰战争，或者沉迷于气候变化，或者沉迷于 AI 末日论，或者沉迷于任何事情。

sentences.en: And there's nothing as riveting as the old religion, the world is ending.
sentences.zh: 没有什么比“世界末日”这种古老的宗教叙事更引人入胜了。

sentences.en: The world is ending. Pay attention, the world is ending.
sentences.zh: 世界末日了。快关注，世界末日了。

sentences.en: And if you don't- It's like Cassandra complex at global scale.
sentences.zh: 如果你不——这就像全球规模的卡珊德拉情结。

sentences.en: Cassandra complex at global scale. And I would argue that large percentages of the population are essentially just infected with these mimetic viruses that have taken over their brain and are causing them to do incredible gyration about things that probably aren't even true or are greatly exaggerated.
sentences.zh: 全球规模的卡珊德拉情结。我认为很大一部分人口本质上就是被这些模因病毒感染了，这些病毒接管了他们的大脑，导致他们对那些可能根本不是事实，或者被严重夸大的事情做出惊人的反应。

sentences.en: But even to the extent they are true, there are things that that person can do nothing about and they should put their own house in order first so you know another little line i have for myself is your family is broken but you're going to fix the world right people are running out there to try and fix the world when their own lives are a mess oh my god right and and i think it defies credibility if you can't fix your own life first i'm not going to take you seriously if you can't fix your own life like all these philosophers who you know seem like people you emulate and so smart or like these brilliant celebrities and they go off and commit suicide well you just kind of invalidated your whole way of life it's like that line of in no country for all men where the killer is waiting for the protagonist and protagonist shows up and the killer says well you know if your set of rules brought you here then what good are your rules didn't work i i am self i'm holistically selfish in in that i want to be objectively successful in everything i set out to want yeah uh you have one life don't settle for mediocrity don't settle for mediocrity and i think the only like people debate intelligence for example right we talk about iq tests and all that but i think the only true test of intelligence is if you get what you want out of life and there are two parts to that one is getting what you want so you know how to get it and the second is wanting the right things knowing what to want in the first place i could want to be a you know six foot eight basketball player and i'm not going to get that so it's wanting the wrong thing so that's wanting something that you can't get.
sentences.zh: 但即使它们是真的，那个人也对此无能为力，他们应该先整理好自己的生活。所以，你知道我对自己说的另一句小话是：你的家庭一团糟，但你却要去拯救世界？人们在自己的生活一团糟时，却跑出去试图拯救世界，天哪，对吧？我认为如果你不能先解决好自己的生活，这简直不可信。如果你连自己的生活都搞不定，我是不会认真对待你的。就像那些你崇拜的、看起来很聪明的哲学家，或者那些才华横溢的名人，结果他们自杀了，那你其实就否定了你整个人生方式。就像《老无所依》里的那句台词，杀手在等主角，主角出现后，杀手说：如果你的那套规则把你带到了这里，那你的规则有什么用？没用。我是整体上的自私，因为我想在我想要的一切事情上都取得客观的成功。是的，你只有一次生命，不要满足于平庸，不要满足于平庸。我认为衡量智力唯一的真正标准，就是你是否从生活中得到了你想要的。这有两部分：一是得到你想要的，所以你知道如何去得到它；二是想要正确的东西，首先要知道该想要什么。我可能想成为一个六英尺八英寸的篮球运动员，但我做不到，所以那是想要错误的东西，也就是想要一些你得不到的东西。

sentences.en: That's wanting something you can't get. There's also wanting something that you don't want.
sentences.zh: 那是想要一些你得不到的东西。还有一种是想要一些你其实并不想要的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, wanting something that's a booby prize.
sentences.zh: 是的，想要一些其实是“安慰奖”的东西。

sentences.en: There are plenty of booby prizes out there too, right?
sentences.zh: 外面有很多安慰奖，对吧？

sentences.en: I haven't heard that word in about 20 years.
sentences.zh: 我已经有 20 年没听过这个词了。

sentences.en: Yeah, prizes that are just not worth having or that create their own problems.
sentences.zh: 是的，那些根本不值得拥有，或者会制造出更多问题的奖品。

sentences.en: But if you're not careful, you can end up in a place in life not only that you don't want to be, but one that you didn't even mean to get to.
sentences.zh: 但如果你不小心，你最终可能会处于生活中一个你不仅不想去，甚至根本没打算去的地方。

sentences.en: That's if you're kind of proceeding unconsciously.
sentences.zh: 如果你是在无意识地前进，就会这样。

sentences.en: But how many people are? And usually I think people end up there because they are going on autopilot with sort of societal expectations or other people's expectations.
sentences.zh: 但有多少人是这样呢？通常我认为人们最终会那样，是因为他们是在自动驾驶模式下，遵循着社会期望或其他人的期望。

sentences.en: So, you know, or out of guilt or out of like mimetic desire, you know, Peter Thiel has this whole thing from Rene Girard about how... mimetic desires, our desires are picked up from other people.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，或者出于内疚，或者出于模因欲望。你知道，Peter Thiel 有一套来自 Rene Girard 的理论，关于模因欲望，即我们的欲望是从别人那里学来的。

sentences.en: And some of those are automatically baked into society, like, you know, go to law school, go to med school, go to whatever, go to business school.
sentences.zh: 其中一些是自动植入社会的，比如，去读法学院，去读医学院，去读什么什么，去读商学院。

sentences.en: Or they might be from watching what your friends are doing and, you know, the other monkeys are doing.
sentences.zh: 或者可能来自观察你的朋友在做什么，你知道，其他猴子在做什么。

sentences.en: Or it might just be, you know, what your parents' expectations are.
sentences.zh: 或者可能只是你父母的期望。

sentences.en: I might be out of guilt. You know, guilt is just society's voice speaking in your head, socially programmed, so you'll be a good little monkey and do things that are good for the tribe.
sentences.zh: 也可能是出于内疚。你知道，内疚只是社会的声音在你脑海中说话，是社会编程，让你成为一只乖巧的小猴子，做对部落有益的事情。

sentences.en: But I think the best outcomes come when you think it through for yourself and decide for yourself and i don't think people spend enough time deciding for example we run on these uh four-year cycles you know in silicon valley you go join a startup you vest your stock over four years that's the standard okay um uh in uh college you know you go for four years high school you go for four years um some things take longer you know you have children they hit puberty nine years later That's like a nine-year cycle until that relationship changes.
sentences.zh: 但我认为最好的结果来自于你自己深思熟虑并做出决定。我不认为人们花足够的时间去决定。例如，我们按这些四年周期运行，你知道在硅谷，你去加入一家初创公司，你的股票在四年内归属，这是标准。好吧，在大学里，你知道你去读四年，高中你去读四年，有些事情需要更长时间，你知道你有孩子，他们九年后进入青春期，那是一个九年的周期，直到那种关系发生变化。

sentences.en: But we're used to these fairly long cycles, multi-year cycles in which we are committed to things.
sentences.zh: 但我们习惯了这些相当长的周期，多年周期，我们致力于某些事情。

sentences.en: You go to law school, you know, four or five-year cycle.
sentences.zh: 你去读法学院，你知道，四五年周期。

sentences.en: You go be a lawyer, 40-year cycle. These are very long cycles.
sentences.zh: 你去当律师，40 年周期。这些都是非常长的周期。

sentences.en: The amount of time we spend deciding what to do and who to do it with, very short, very, very short, right?
sentences.zh: 我们花在决定做什么和与谁一起做的时间，非常短，非常非常短，对吧？

sentences.en: We spend, you know, three months deciding, one month deciding on a job where we're going to be for 10 years or five years.
sentences.zh: 我们花三个月，一个月决定一份工作，我们要在那待 10 年或 5 年。

sentences.en: And because a lot of discovery is path dependent, where the next thing you find on the path is dependent on where you were on the previous path, you sort of start going down this vector that is a very long distance.
sentences.zh: 而且因为很多发现是路径依赖的，你在路径上发现的下一件事取决于你在上一条路径上的位置，你开始沿着这个向量走很长的距离。

sentences.en: People decide frivolously which city to live in, and that's going to decide who their friends are, what their jobs are, their opportunity, their weather, their food supply, their air supply, quality of life.
sentences.zh: 人们轻率地决定住在哪个城市，而那将决定他们的朋友是谁，他们的工作是什么，他们的机会、天气、食物供应、空气供应、生活质量。

sentences.en: It's such an important decision, but people spend so little time thinking it through.
sentences.zh: 这是一个如此重要的决定，但人们花在思考上的时间却很少。

sentences.en: I would argue that if you're making a four-year decision, spend a year thinking it through, like really thinking it through.
sentences.zh: 我会说，如果你在做一个四年的决定，花一年时间去思考它，像真正深思熟虑那样。

sentences.en: 25% of the time. Yeah, exactly. There's the secretary theorem.
sentences.zh: 25% 的时间。是的，完全正确。这就是秘书问题。

sentences.en: I don't know if you know that one. After you've done this many people, pick the best one of the next however many.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你知不知道那个。在你面试了这么多人之后，选择接下来的多少人里的最好一个。

sentences.en: That's right. Yeah. The secretary theorem is this computer science professor is trying to figure out how much time he should spend interviewing secretaries and then how long to keep the secretary.
sentences.zh: 没错。是的。秘书问题是这位计算机科学教授试图弄清楚他应该花多少时间面试秘书，然后面试多久。

sentences.en: So let's say he's going to have a secretary for 10 years.
sentences.zh: 所以假设他要雇一个秘书 10 年。

sentences.en: Does he keep searching for one year, two years, three years, one month, two months?
sentences.zh: 他是应该继续寻找一年、两年、三年、一个月、两个月？

sentences.en: What is the optimal time? and it turns out that the optimal time is somewhere around a third about a third of the way through you take the best person you've worked with and try to find someone that good or better so that by the time you've gone about a third of the way through you have excuse me seen enough that you now have a sense of what the bar is and then anybody who meets or exceeds that bar is good enough and this applies to dating this applies to jobs and careers this applies generally but But the interesting thing about the secretary theorem is that it's actually not time-based.
sentences.zh: 什么是最佳时间？结果发现最佳时间大约是三分之一，在三分之一的路程处，你选择你共事过的最好的人，并尝试找到一个同样好或更好的人。所以当你走完大约三分之一的路程时，你已经，抱歉，看够了，现在你对标准有了感觉，然后任何达到或超过那个标准的人都足够好了。这适用于约会，适用于工作和职业，这普遍适用。但秘书问题的有趣之处在于它实际上不是基于时间的。

sentences.en: It's not based on one third of the time.
sentences.zh: 它不是基于三分之一的时间。

sentences.en: It's iteration-based. It's the number of candidates.
sentences.zh: 它是基于迭代的。是候选人的数量。

sentences.en: The number of shots you took on goal. That's right.
sentences.zh: 你尝试的次数。没错。

sentences.en: So you want to have lots and lots of iterations.
sentences.zh: 所以你想有很多很多的迭代。

sentences.en: You need to bail out quickly and you need to be decisive quickly.
sentences.zh: 你需要快速退出，你需要快速果断。

sentences.en: That's right. You need to take opportunities quickly and bail out quickly.
sentences.zh: 没错。你需要快速抓住机会，快速退出。

sentences.en: Correct. Like if you go back and you look through failed relationships, probably the biggest regret will be staying in the relationship after your year was over.
sentences.zh: 正确。就像如果你回头看失败的感情，最大的遗憾可能是在一年结束后还留在关系里。

sentences.en: Exactly. You should have left sooner. The moment you knew it wasn't going to work out, you should have moved on.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。你应该早点离开。当你意识到它行不通的那一刻，你就应该继续前进。

sentences.en: So in that sense, I think Malcolm Gladwell popularized this idea of 10,000 hours to mastery.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，我认为 Malcolm Gladwell 普及了“一万小时定律”来达到精通。

sentences.en: I would say it's actually 10,000 iterations to mastery.
sentences.zh: 我会说实际上是“一万次迭代”来达到精通。

sentences.en: It's not actually 10,000. It's some unknown number.
sentences.zh: 实际上不是一万次。是一个未知的数字。

sentences.en: But it's about the number of iterations that drives a learning curve.
sentences.zh: 但正是迭代的次数推动了学习曲线。

sentences.en: And iteration is not repetition. Repetition is a different thing.
sentences.zh: 迭代不是重复。重复是另一回事。

sentences.en: Repeating is doing the same thing over and over.
sentences.zh: 重复是反复做同一件事。

sentences.en: Iteration is modifying it with a learning and then doing another version of it.
sentences.zh: 迭代是带着学习去修改它，然后做另一个版本。

sentences.en: So that's error correction. So if you get 10,000 error corrections in anything, you will be an expert at it.
sentences.zh: 所以那是纠错。所以如果你在任何事情上得到一万次纠错，你就会成为专家。

sentences.en: Don't partner with cynics and pessimists.
sentences.zh: 不要与愤世嫉俗者和悲观主义者合伙。

sentences.en: You mentioned there about the people who've got a nightmare going on at home and are trying to fix the world.
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到了那些家里一团糟却试图拯救世界的人。

sentences.en: But a lot of the time that... cynicism and pessimism we find in ourselves.
sentences.zh: 但很多时候，那种……我们在自己身上发现的愤世嫉俗和悲观主义。

sentences.en: We see the world, whether we want to, whether it's because we've imbibed what the news or the negative people around us have said, or it's a bit more kind of endogenous than that.
sentences.zh: 我们看待世界的方式，无论我们是否愿意，无论是因为我们吸收了新闻或周围负面的人所说的话，还是它更内在一些。

sentences.en: It's just sort of in us. It's the way that we see the world.
sentences.zh: 它就在我们心中。这就是我们看待世界的方式。

sentences.en: How can people avoid cynicism and pessimism within themselves?
sentences.zh: 人们如何避免内心的愤世嫉俗和悲观主义？

sentences.en: Yeah. Cynicism and pessimism is a tough one.
sentences.zh: 是的。愤世嫉俗和悲观主义是个难题。

sentences.en: We're naturally hardwired for it. Again, I go back to evolution.
sentences.zh: 我们天生就为此而生。再次，我回到进化论。

sentences.en: I'm sorry to keep harping on evolution, but within biology, there's very few good explanatory theories and, you know, theory of evolution by natural selection is probably the best one.
sentences.zh: 很抱歉一直谈论进化论，但在生物学中，很少有好的解释理论，你知道，自然选择的进化论可能是最好的一个。

sentences.en: So if you can't explain something about life or psychology or human nature through evolution, then you probably don't have a good theory for it.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你不能通过进化来解释关于生活、心理学或人性的某些事情，那么你可能就没有一个好的理论。

sentences.en: And I would say that pessimism is another one that comes out of this, which is in the natural environment, you're hardwired to be pessimistic because let's say that I see something rustling in the woods.
sentences.zh: 我会说悲观主义是另一个源于此的东西，即在自然环境中，你天生就是悲观的，因为假设我看到树林里有东西在沙沙作响。

sentences.en: And if I move towards it and it turns out to be food and prey, then good, I get to eat one meal.
sentences.zh: 如果我向它走去，结果发现是食物和猎物，那很好，我吃了一顿饭。

sentences.en: But if it turns us be a predator, I get eaten.
sentences.zh: 但如果结果是捕食者，我就被吃了。

sentences.en: And that's the end of that. So we are hardwired to avoid ruin and just dying.
sentences.zh: 那一切就结束了。所以我们天生就是为了避免毁灭和死亡。

sentences.en: So we are naturally hardwired to be pessimists.
sentences.zh: 所以我们天生就是悲观主义者。

sentences.en: But modern society is very different. Despite whatever problems you may have with modern society, it is far, far safer than living in the jungle and just trying to survive.
sentences.zh: 但现代社会非常不同。尽管你对现代社会可能有什么不满，但它比生活在丛林中试图生存要安全得多。

sentences.en: And the opportunities and the upside are nonlinear.
sentences.zh: 而且机会和收益是非线性的。

sentences.en: For example, when you're investing, if you short a stock, the most money you can make is 2x.
sentences.zh: 例如，当你投资时，如果你做空一只股票，你最多能赚 2 倍。

sentences.en: You You just lose, you know, if the stock goes to zero, you double your money.
sentences.zh: 你只是输了，你知道，如果股票跌到零，你就赚了一倍的钱。

sentences.en: But if the stock is the next NVIDIA and it goes 100x or 1,000x, you make a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 但如果这只股票是下一个 NVIDIA，它涨了 100 倍或 1000 倍，你就赚了很多钱。

sentences.en: So upside because of leverage is nearly unlimited.
sentences.zh: 所以由于杠杆作用，上行空间几乎是无限的。

sentences.en: Also in modern society, because there's so many different people you can interact with, if you go on a date and it fails, there are infinite more people to go on a date with.
sentences.zh: 同样在现代社会，因为你可以与许多不同的人互动，如果你去约会失败了，还有无数人可以去约会。

sentences.en: In a tribal system, there might have been 20 people and you can't even get through all of them.
sentences.zh: 在部落系统中，可能只有 20 个人，你甚至无法全部接触一遍。

sentences.en: So modern society is far more forgiving of failure. and you just have to sort of neocortically realize and override that.
sentences.zh: 所以现代社会对失败的宽容度要高得多。你只需要在皮层层面意识到并覆盖掉那种本能。

sentences.en: You have to realize that you're much more running a search function to find the thing that'll work.
sentences.zh: 你必须意识到你更多是在运行一个搜索功能来找到可行的事情。

sentences.en: And then that one thing will pay off in massive compounding.
sentences.zh: 然后那一件事情会带来巨大的复利回报。

sentences.en: Once you find your mate for the rest of your life, you find your wife or your husband, then you can compound it in that relationship.
sentences.zh: 一旦你找到了余生的伴侣，找到了你的妻子或丈夫，你就可以在那段关系中积累复利。

sentences.en: It's okay if you had 50 failed dates in between.
sentences.zh: 如果你中间有 50 次失败的约会也没关系。

sentences.en: The same way, once you find the one business you're meant to plow into and it'll compound returns, it's okay if you had 50 small failed ventures or 50 small failed job interviews.
sentences.zh: 同样，一旦你找到了你注定要投入的那项事业，它会带来复利回报，即使你有 50 次小的失败创业或 50 次小的失败面试也没关系。

sentences.en: The number of failures doesn't matter. And so there's no point in being a pessimist.
sentences.zh: 失败的次数并不重要。所以没有必要成为悲观主义者。

sentences.en: You want to be an optimist, but I would say you want to be skeptical about specific things.
sentences.zh: 你想成为乐观主义者，但我会说你想对具体的事情保持怀疑。

sentences.en: Every specific opportunity is probably a fail, but you want to be optimistic in the general.
sentences.zh: 每一个具体的机会可能都是失败的，但你想在总体上保持乐观。

sentences.en: In the general, you want to be like something in here is going to work out.
sentences.zh: 在总体上，你想表现得像“这里面总会有事情会成功的”。

sentences.en: How do you navigate that tension? I mean, exactly as I said, I'm optimistic in the general that if something fails right now, then this is a little woo-woo, but it wasn't meant to be.
sentences.zh: 你如何驾驭这种张力？我的意思是，正如我所说，我在总体上是乐观的，如果现在某件事失败了，那么这有点玄学，但它注定不是那样的。

sentences.en: It was a learning experience. It was an iteration.
sentences.zh: 这是一次学习经历。这是一次迭代。

sentences.en: As long as I learned something from it, then it's a win.
sentences.zh: 只要我从中吸取了教训，那它就是一次胜利。

sentences.en: If I didn't learn from it, then it's a loss.
sentences.zh: 如果我没有从中吸取教训，那它就是一次损失。

sentences.en: But as long as you're learning and you keep iterating fast and cutting your losses quickly, then when you find the right thing, you have to be optimistic and compound into it. so you don't want to jump into the first thing you don't want to marry the first person you date necessarily unless you got very lucky but you you want to investigate and explore very very quickly until you find the match and then you have to be willing to go all in you have to be willing to move your chips at the center of the table so both those uh both those uh approaches are required so it's a barbell strategy it's sort of black or it's white and most people are sort of stuck in this gray bit and like half in but i'm kind of don't really know if i am and i also think like labels like pessimists optimists cynic introvert extrovert these are very self-limiting humans are very dynamic there are times when you feel like being introverted there are times when you feel like being extroverted there are contexts in which you'll be pessimistic there are contexts in which you'll be optimistic leave all the labels alone It's better just to look at the problem at hand, look at reality the way it is.
sentences.zh: 但只要你在学习，并且保持快速迭代和快速止损，那么当你找到正确的事情时，你必须保持乐观并投入其中。所以你不想跳进第一件事，你不一定非要嫁给第一个约会的人，除非你非常幸运，但你想非常非常快地调查和探索，直到找到匹配的对象，然后你必须愿意全力以赴，你必须愿意把筹码推到桌子中央。所以这两种方法都是必需的，这是一种杠铃策略，它是黑的或者是白的，而大多数人被困在这个灰色的地带，半推半就，但我不太确定我是否是这样。我也认为像悲观主义者、乐观主义者、愤世嫉俗者、内向者、外向者这样的标签是非常自我限制的。人类是非常动态的，有时你会觉得想内向，有时你会觉得想外向，在某些情况下你会悲观，在某些情况下你会乐观。把所有的标签都抛开吧，最好只是看看手头的问题，看看现实本来的样子。

sentences.en: Try to take yourself out of the equation in a sense.
sentences.zh: 试着在某种意义上把自己从等式中剔除。

sentences.en: Like obviously you're involved, but motivated reasoning is the worst kind of reasoning.
sentences.zh: 就像显然你参与其中，但动机性推理是最糟糕的推理。

sentences.en: You're not going to find truth through highly motivated reasoning.
sentences.zh: 你不会通过高度动机的推理找到真相。

sentences.en: You have to be objective. And objective means trying to take yourself out of it as much as possible, or at least your personality out of it as much as possible.
sentences.zh: 你必须客观。客观意味着尽量把自己从其中剔除，或者至少把你的个性从其中剔除。

sentences.en: And so to the extent you run with this thick identity and personality, it's going to cloud your judgment.
sentences.zh: 所以，在某种程度上，你带着这种厚重的身份和个性去运行，它会模糊你的判断。

sentences.en: It's going to try and lock you into the past.
sentences.zh: 它会试图把你锁在过去。

sentences.en: If you say, I'm a depressed, unhappy person, yeah, I'm going to be unhappy.
sentences.zh: 如果你说，我是一个抑郁、不快乐的人，是的，我会不快乐。

sentences.en: That's a way of locking yourself into your past.
sentences.zh: 那是一种把自己锁在过去的方式。

sentences.en: Even saying, I have trauma, I have PTSD.
sentences.zh: 即使说，我有创伤，我有 PTSD。

sentences.en: Yeah, you feel something. There are memories, there are flashes, there are occasional bad feelings.
sentences.zh: 是的，你感觉到了什么。有记忆，有闪回，偶尔有不好的感觉。

sentences.en: But don't define yourself by it because then you'll lock it into your identity and you're just going to loop on it.
sentences.zh: 但不要用它来定义自己，因为那样你会把它锁进你的身份里，你只会陷入循环。

sentences.en: It's better to stay flexible because reality is always changing and you have to be able to adapt to it.
sentences.zh: 最好保持灵活，因为现实总是在变化，你必须能够适应它。

sentences.en: Adaptation is also intelligence. Adaptation is survival. adaptation is kind of how you're here you're here because you're an adapter and your ancestors were adapters so to adapt you'll see things clearly and if you're seeing them through your own identity it's going to cloud your judgment moving on to sort of thinking about happiness obviously a topic of yours that's a it's honestly the one that i feel least qualified to talk about is it like a guy that's got long arms teaching you how to bench press or a dude that's really tall teaching you how to deadlift someone that feels like they came from behind the eight ball Yeah, you're asking a crazy person about their thoughts.
sentences.zh: 适应也是一种智力。适应就是生存。适应是你之所以在这里的原因，你在这里是因为你是一个适应者，你的祖先是适应者。所以要适应，你就要清楚地看到事物，如果你通过自己的身份来看待它们，它会模糊你的判断。继续谈谈关于幸福的思考，显然这是你的一个话题，老实说，这是我感觉最没资格谈论的话题。就像一个长手臂的人教你如何卧推，或者一个很高的人教你如何硬拉，一个感觉像是从劣势中走出来的人。是的，你在问一个疯子关于他们的想法。

sentences.en: So just thought it through. Is happiness still more about peace than it is about joy?
sentences.zh: 所以只是想清楚了。幸福更多是关于平静而不是关于快乐吗？

sentences.en: It's just one of those overloaded words that means different things to different people.
sentences.zh: 这只是那些对不同人意味着不同事物的重载词之一。

sentences.en: So I'm not even sure we're communicating the same language.
sentences.zh: 所以我甚至不确定我们在用同一种语言交流。

sentences.en: But what is happiness?
sentences.zh: 但什么是幸福？

sentences.en: I think it's just basically being okay with where you are.
sentences.zh: 我认为这基本上就是对你所处的位置感到满意。

sentences.en: Not wanting. Not wanting things to be different than the way they are.
sentences.zh: 不想要。不想要事情变得与现在不同。

sentences.en: Not having the sense that anything is missing in this moment. needing something to change your current positive situation being contingent on an adjustment on getting something from the outside world ironically i think most people if you were to ask them when they were happiest for a sustained period of time not for a brief moment because pleasure can override happiness and create kind of this illusion of happiness but if you ask people when they were happy for a sustained period of time they were probably doing some variation of nothing that's interesting because in the chase is this sort of lack this contingency that's right but then you get bored if you just sit around all the time you get bored so you want adventure you want surprise like there's the funny thought experiment of the bliss machine right which is suppose i could drill a hole in your head and put an electrode in and they did this with monkeys and i can put a wire in there and i can stimulate just the right part of your brain and I can put you in bliss and you'll just be in bliss.
sentences.zh: 没有那种在这一刻缺少什么的感觉。不需要任何东西来改变你当前的积极状况，这种状况取决于调整，取决于从外部世界获得什么。讽刺的是，我认为大多数人，如果你问他们什么时候最快乐，在一段持续的时间里，而不是短暂的瞬间，因为快乐可以覆盖幸福并创造一种幸福的错觉，但如果你问人们什么时候在一段持续的时间里感到快乐，他们可能在做某种形式的“什么都不做”。这很有趣，因为在追求中存在这种缺乏，这种偶然性，没错。但如果你一直坐着，你会感到无聊，所以你想要冒险，你想要惊喜，就像那个关于“极乐机器”的有趣思想实验，对吧？假设我可以在你的头上钻个洞，放一个电极进去，他们对猴子做过这个，我可以在那里放一根电线，我可以刺激你大脑中正确的部分，我可以让你处于极乐状态，你就会一直处于极乐状态。

sentences.en: Would you, would you want that? Might be nice.
sentences.zh: 你会，你会想要那个吗？可能不错。

sentences.en: For how long? Do it and I'll tell you. Right.
sentences.zh: 多久？你做了，我就告诉你。对。

sentences.en: So most people will say, well, I don't want that.
sentences.zh: 所以大多数人会说，嗯，我不想要那个。

sentences.en: I want meaning. I don't want just bliss.
sentences.zh: 我想要意义。我不想要仅仅是极乐。

sentences.en: I want meaning. And you're like, okay, well, I'll put an electrode in there and I'll give you meaning.
sentences.zh: 我想要意义。你会说，好吧，我会放一个电极进去，给你意义。

sentences.en: How about that? And if you kind of run this thought experiment long enough, I think most people realize actually what I want is I want surprise.
sentences.zh: 那个怎么样？如果你把这个思想实验运行得足够久，我认为大多数人会意识到，实际上我想要的是惊喜。

sentences.en: I want the world to surprise me and I want to wrestle with it in ways that are somewhat predictable, but somewhat not.
sentences.zh: 我想要世界给我惊喜，我想要以某种程度上可预测，但某种程度上不可预测的方式与它搏斗。

sentences.en: And you kind of end up back where you started.
sentences.zh: 然后你最终回到了你开始的地方。

sentences.en: So I don't know if necessarily, for some people, pure happiness is the ultimate goal.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道，对某些人来说，纯粹的幸福是否是最终目标。

sentences.en: They want to just be blissfully happy wherever they are, whenever they are.
sentences.zh: 他们只想无论身在何处，无论何时，都感到极乐般的快乐。

sentences.en: But I think other people, most people would say, well, I'm here in this world.
sentences.zh: 但我认为其他人，大多数人会说，嗯，我在这里，在这个世界上。

sentences.en: I'm here in this life. I don't understand it or why, but I want to be...
sentences.zh: 我在这里，在这个生命中。我不明白它或为什么，但我想要……

sentences.en: I want to be engaged. I want to be surprised.
sentences.zh: 我想要参与。我想要惊喜。

sentences.en: I want to do things. I want to accomplish things.
sentences.zh: 我想要做事情。我想要完成事情。

sentences.en: I want to want things and then get them, right?
sentences.zh: 我想要想要东西，然后得到它们，对吧？

sentences.en: That's kind of the whole game that we're all playing here.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们都在这里玩的整个游戏。

sentences.en: Surprises are really interesting. The sort of unpredictability, I think, total bro science here, but I'm pretty sure that that's kind of how dopamine works, that things are a bit better than you expected.
sentences.zh: 惊喜真的很有趣。那种不可预测性，我认为，完全是“兄弟科学”，但我很确定这就是多巴胺的工作方式，事情比你预期的要好一点。

sentences.en: That within that, it means that if you, for the perennial insecure overachievers that cloy for control, that really want to be able to, the schedule is perfectly done and we know the itinerary, we know where we're going to be at this time.
sentences.zh: 在这其中，这意味着如果你，对于那些渴望控制、真的想要能够，时间表完美完成，我们知道行程，我们知道我们在什么时候会在哪里，的永恒不安全感的过度成就者。

sentences.en: You're in some ways, I guess, reducing down the capacity for surprise because everything has become very contrived, prescribed, done in advance, laid out.
sentences.zh: 你在某种程度上，我想，减少了惊喜的能力，因为一切都变得非常做作、规定、提前完成、安排好了。

sentences.en: Your ability to be surprised actually diminishes.
sentences.zh: 你被惊喜的能力实际上减少了。

sentences.en: Yeah. If nothing worked out the way you expected, if it was all serendipity, and you didn't want that, you would just be a ball of anxiety.
sentences.zh: 是的。如果没有任何事情按照你预期的那样发展，如果一切都是机缘巧合，而你不想要那样，你只会是一个焦虑的球。

sentences.en: On the other hand, if everything worked out as you expected and wanted, you'd be so bored, you might as well be dead.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，如果一切都按照你预期和想要的那样发展，你会感到非常无聊，你可能就像死了一样。

sentences.en: So there's some, you know, the river of life kind of flows between these two banks and enjoy it.
sentences.zh: 所以有一些，你知道，生命之河在两岸之间流动，享受它。

sentences.en: You say thinking about yourself is the source of all unhappiness, but presumably you need to work on yourself and your weaknesses as well.
sentences.zh: 你说思考自己是所有不快乐的源头，但大概你也需要努力改善自己和你的弱点。

sentences.en: So some degree of reflection is important.
sentences.zh: 所以一定程度的反思很重要。

sentences.en: And if thinking about yourself as a source of unhappiness, is this a price that you need to pay?
sentences.zh: 如果思考自己作为不快乐的源头，这是你需要付出的代价吗？

sentences.en: I need to sort of reflect inward. I'm going to have to diminish this level of happiness for a little while, and then I can use this new level.
sentences.zh: 我需要某种程度上向内反思。我将不得不暂时降低这种幸福水平，然后我可以使用这个新的水平。

sentences.en: I've got my brown belt on and I can go out into the world as a brown belt.
sentences.zh: 我已经系上了棕带，可以以棕带的身份走向世界了。

sentences.en: What I'm specifically referring to that is if you're thinking about your personality and your ego and the character of you, and you're obsessing over that, that's where a lot of depression and unhappiness sort of lingers and and gets cultivated uh so uh thinking about woe is me this happened to me that happened to me i have this personality i have this issue i deserve this i didn't get that that's you're just strengthening a little beast in there that is insatiable and that's where i think a lot of unhappiness comes from what's the beast it's the ego but that word is so overused that i kind of I hate to use the word, but it's a recurrent collection of thoughts that are very self-obsessed and will never be satisfied.
sentences.zh: 我特别指的是，如果你一直在思考你的个性、你的自我以及你的性格，并对此念念不忘，那么很多抑郁和不快乐往往就是从这里滋生并被培养出来的。比如总是想着“我真可怜”、“这事发生在我身上”、“那事也发生在我身上”、“我有这种个性”、“我有这个问题”、“我理应得到这个”、“我没得到那个”，你其实是在喂养内心那个贪得无厌的小怪兽，我认为很多不快乐都源于此。什么是怪兽？就是“自我”（ego），但这个词被用得太滥了，我不太想用，但它就是一连串非常自恋、永远无法满足的重复性思维。

sentences.en: And very concretized as well. So they're not malleable, not particularly flexible.
sentences.zh: 而且非常固化。它们并不具有延展性，也不怎么灵活。

sentences.en: Well, you're just adding to them by thinking about them all the time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你一直在想它们，只会让它们变得更严重。

sentences.en: You're creating narratives and stories and identities.
sentences.zh: 你是在编造叙事、故事和身份认同。

sentences.en: But that's different from solving personal problems.
sentences.zh: 但这与解决个人问题是两码事。

sentences.en: So if you encounter something, you learn from something, you're reflecting upon the learning, then you can reflect upon it, absorb it, and then just move on. but sitting there saying i'm chris i'm nabal i deserve this this happened to me that person wronged me this is who i am this shouldn't have happened i need to go get revenge on this or i need to fix that or change this i mean that i think is where a lot of mental illness is you know comes from so it depends if you are thinking about something to solve a problem and get it off your chest and get it off your mind if it leaves your mind clearer at the end of it then i think it was worthwhile.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你遇到了什么事，从中学到了东西，你在反思这次学习，那么你可以反思它、吸收它，然后继续前进。但如果坐在那里说“我是Chris，我是Naval，我理应得到这个，这事发生在我身上，那个人亏待了我，我就是这样的人，这本不该发生，我得去报复，或者我得去修复那个、改变这个”，我认为很多心理疾病就是这么来的。所以这取决于你思考某事是为了解决问题、把它从心头放下，还是为了别的。如果思考结束后你的头脑更清醒了，那我觉得是值得的。

sentences.en: If it leaves your mind busier at the end of it, then you're probably going in the wrong direction.
sentences.zh: 如果思考结束后你的头脑反而更乱了，那你可能走错方向了。

sentences.en: Is this a justification for detachment, cultivated ignorance, distraction?
sentences.zh: 这是为超脱、刻意无知或逃避现实找借口吗？

sentences.en: Detachment is not a goal. Detachment is a byproduct.
sentences.zh: 超脱不是目标。超脱是副产品。

sentences.en: It's just a byproduct of just realizing what matters and what doesn't.
sentences.zh: 它只是意识到什么重要、什么不重要后的副产品。

sentences.en: And just for one moment on the self thing, I think everybody craves thinking about something more than themselves if you want to be you know happy to some extent you have to forget about your personal problems and one way to do that is take on other problems bigger problems uh and that could be a mission that could be that could be spirituality that could be kids um it could be caring about the planet although I think people take that a little far you know and then they get kind of oppressive and And... and tyrannical in support of abstract concepts.
sentences.zh: 关于“自我”这件事，我想多说一点：每个人都渴望思考超越自身的东西。如果你想在某种程度上获得快乐，你必须忘记你的个人问题。实现这一点的方法之一就是承担其他问题，更宏大的问题。那可能是一个使命，可能是灵性追求，可能是孩子，也可能是关心地球——尽管我觉得人们有时会走得太远，以至于为了支持抽象概念而变得压迫和专制。

sentences.en: So these can be taken too far, just like religion, for example.
sentences.zh: 所以这些东西也可能过犹不及，就像宗教一样。

sentences.en: Anything in excess. Anything in excess, right?
sentences.zh: 凡事过犹不及，对吧？

sentences.en: But generally, the less you think about yourself, the more you can think about a mission or about God or about a child or something like that.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，你越少想自己，就越能多想使命、上帝、孩子或其他类似的事情。

sentences.en: So I remember Vinny Haimath, the founder of Loom, said, I am rich and I have no idea what to do with my life.
sentences.zh: 我记得Loom的创始人Vinny Haimath说过：“我很富有，但我完全不知道该拿我的人生怎么办。”

sentences.en: And you replied, God, kids, our mission, pick at least one.
sentences.zh: 你回答说：“上帝、孩子、我们的使命，至少选一个。”

sentences.en: That's right. Preferably all three. it's very liberating.
sentences.zh: 没错。最好三个都选。这非常令人解脱。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think overthinking about yourself is probably, it may not be the cause of depression, but it certainly doesn't help.
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得过度思考自己可能不是导致抑郁的原因，但肯定没好处。

sentences.en: Rumination. Yeah, I kind of had a self-induced Stockholm syndrome from this sort of a thing, because I like to think about stuff, and you provide you with an endless number of things to think about.
sentences.zh: 反刍思维。是的，我曾经因为这种事产生了一种自导自演的斯德哥尔摩综合征，因为我喜欢思考，而这种思维会为你提供无穷无尽的东西去思考。

sentences.en: So you're kind of, yeah, you have this, you're the prisoner and the prison guard at the same time.
sentences.zh: 所以你就像是……你既是囚犯，又是狱卒。

sentences.en: And I had Abigail Schreier on the show. She wrote this book called Bad Therapy, sort of pushing back against therapy culture specifically for kids.
sentences.zh: 我曾在节目中采访过Abigail Schreier。她写了一本叫《Bad Therapy》的书，专门反驳针对儿童的治疗文化。

sentences.en: But there was a blast radius that covered pretty much everything, including kind of CBT.
sentences.zh: 但其影响范围几乎覆盖了一切，包括认知行为疗法（CBT）。

sentences.en: And like, we're getting perilously close to some really evidence-based stuff here. but the more that I've thought about it and the more that I've looked at the evidence there is like basically a direct correlation between how much you think about yourself and how miserable you are.
sentences.zh: 我们正危险地接近一些非常有实证基础的东西。但我思考得越多，查看的证据越多，就越发现：你思考自己的程度与你的痛苦程度之间，基本上存在直接的相关性。

sentences.en: Therapy is great if it lets you vent and it solves the thing and then X session later you're done you're clear but if you're just looping on the same thing forever then it's actually the opposite.
sentences.zh: 如果治疗能让你发泄出来，解决了问题，然后几次疗程后你就结束了、清醒了，那很好。但如果你只是永远在同一件事上打转，那其实适得其反。

sentences.en: You're bathing in it you're indulging in it yeah yeah.
sentences.zh: 你沉浸在其中，你在放纵它。是的，没错。

sentences.en: How have your become happy techniques developed over time yeah i used to have a lot of them uh now i kind of try not to have any because i think the techniques themselves are kind of a struggle it's sort of like bidding for status implies your low status it reveals that your low status so someone who's basically trying to show off uh comes across as low status the same way someone who's trying to be happy is sort of saying I'm unhappy and creating that frame.
sentences.zh: 你那些“变快乐”的技巧随着时间推移是如何演变的？是的，我过去有很多技巧，现在我尽量一个都不留，因为我觉得技巧本身就是一种挣扎。就像竞标地位暗示你地位低下一样，它暴露了你的低地位。所以一个试图炫耀的人，给人的感觉就是地位低下；同样，一个试图变得快乐的人，其实是在说“我不快乐”，并创造了那种框架。

sentences.en: So it's better just to not even think in terms of- So you position yourself as being in lack in order to attain?
sentences.zh: 所以最好连这种想法都不要有。所以你把自己定位为处于匮乏状态，以便去获得？

sentences.en: Yeah. I don't even think in terms of happiness, unhappiness anymore.
sentences.zh: 是的。我甚至不再从快乐或不快乐的角度去思考了。

sentences.en: I just kind of just do my thing. Again, another question that's similar to a bunch of them.
sentences.zh: 我只是做我自己的事。又是那种类似的问题。

sentences.en: Do you think you could have got there had you have not done the procedural, systematic, sort of step by step by step, this is what it is, and then come out the other side?
sentences.zh: 你觉得如果你没有经历过那种程序化的、系统的、一步步来的过程，然后从另一端走出来，你能达到现在的境界吗？

sentences.en: I don't think there are any formulas. I I think it's unique to each person.
sentences.zh: 我不认为有什么公式。我认为这对每个人来说都是独特的。

sentences.en: It's like asking a successful person, how did you become successful?
sentences.zh: 这就像问一个成功人士：“你是怎么成功的？”

sentences.en: Each one of them will give you a different story.
sentences.zh: 他们每个人都会给你一个不同的故事。

sentences.en: You can't follow anyone else's path. And most of them are even probably telling you some narratized version of it that isn't quite true.
sentences.zh: 你无法遵循别人的路径。而且他们中的大多数人可能还在告诉你某种经过叙事加工的版本，那并不完全真实。

sentences.en: I mean, that's something that I continually realize, especially as I get to spend more time around people that are successful.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是我不断意识到的事情，尤其是在我花更多时间与成功人士相处之后。

sentences.en: And you hear, it's very important to prioritize work-life balance, right?
sentences.zh: 你会听到，“优先考虑工作与生活的平衡非常重要”，对吧？

sentences.en: That's one of the most common things that people who have attained success say.
sentences.zh: 这是那些已经取得成功的人最常说的话之一。

sentences.en: That's not my experience. but if you look at you shouldn't be asking somebody who is successful what they do to continue their success now you should be asking them what did they do to attain their success when they are where you were and the people who are really extraordinarily successful didn't sit around watching success porn they just went and did it they just had they had such an overwhelming desire to be successful at the thing that they were doing that they just went and did that thing they didn't have time to study and learn and listen and they just did it it's the overwhelming desire that's the most important and the focus that comes from that it's that tweet of yours that was uh people who are good at making wealth or people are good at attaining wealth don't need to teach anybody else how to do it yeah you don't need mentors you need action that was one of them another one is you know the uh uh, uh, the people who actually know how to make money you don't need to sell your course on it there it is um yeah there's lots of variations on it but if you don't another one if you don't lie awake at night thinking about it you don't want it badly enough yeah i think you i've heard you talk before about how um sort of unclosed loops problems that you're working on can cause you to be sleepless and uh this i'm not a good sleeper tell me about that oh i mean my eight sleep hates me it's always telling me i failed at sleeping again brian johnson thinks i'm gonna die early he's probably right but i how much do you reckon you sleep a night you got any idea oh it's so random some nights i'll sleep eight hours some nights i'll sleep four hours but it's literally just random are you bothered about that you're trying to optimize your sleep coach teaching you how to i don't flog myself over things uh if i want to sleep i'll sleep if i don't want to sleep i don't sleep it's not a i don't think i'm doing anything right or wrong You don't label it good night, bad night?
sentences.zh: 那不是我的经验。但如果你看……你不应该问一个已经成功的人现在做什么来维持成功，你应该问他们当初在你现在这个位置时，做了什么来获得成功。那些真正极其成功的人，并没有坐着看什么“成功色情片”（成功学），他们只是去做了。他们对正在做的事情有着压倒性的渴望，所以他们就去做了。他们没时间去学习、去听讲，他们只是去做了。那种压倒性的渴望才是最重要的，以及由此产生的专注力。这就是你那条推文说的：“擅长创造财富的人不需要教别人怎么做。”是的，你不需要导师，你需要行动。那是其中之一，另一个是：“真正知道怎么赚钱的人不需要卖课程。”是的，有很多变体，但如果你晚上不因为这件事而辗转反侧，说明你渴望得还不够强烈。是的，我以前听你谈过，未完成的循环、你正在处理的问题会让你失眠。我睡眠不好，跟我说说这个？哦，我的Eight Sleep（智能床垫）讨厌我，它总是告诉我我又没睡好。Brian Johnson觉得我会早死，他可能是对的。但你觉得你一晚睡多久？你有概念吗？哦，太随机了。有些晚上我睡八小时，有些晚上睡四小时，完全是随机的。你为此感到困扰吗？你在尝试优化睡眠，教练教你如何……我不会因为这些事而折磨自己。如果我想睡，我就睡；如果我不想睡，我就不睡。我不觉得我在做什么对或错的事。你不给它贴上“好觉”或“坏觉”的标签吗？

sentences.en: No, I work out every day because I think it gives me more energy and I've gotten into a good habit with it.
sentences.zh: 不，我每天都锻炼，因为我觉得这给了我更多能量，而且我已经养成了好习惯。

sentences.en: Maybe I'll do the same thing with sleep.
sentences.zh: 也许我也会对睡眠做同样的事。

sentences.en: Maybe I'll develop a good habit, but I'm not going to beat myself up over it.
sentences.zh: 也许我会养成一个好习惯，但我不会因此而自责。

sentences.en: There'll come a point where it's important to me, and when it's important to me, I'll just do it.
sentences.zh: 总有一天它会对我变得重要，当它重要时，我自然会去做。

sentences.en: You know, most of, like, for example, you look at people with addictions, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，大多数……比如，你看那些有瘾的人，对吧？

sentences.en: Overeating or smoking or whatever. They can kind of go through all the different methods, but it's half-hearted.
sentences.zh: 暴饮暴食或吸烟什么的。他们可能会尝试各种方法，但都是三心二意。

sentences.en: And then one day they're like, oh, shit, I've got lung cancer. or my dad has lung cancer and they drop it immediately.
sentences.zh: 然后有一天他们会想：“哦，该死，我得了肺癌”，或者“我爸爸得了肺癌”，然后他们立刻就戒了。

sentences.en: So I think a lot of change is more about desire and understanding than it is about forcing yourself or trying to domesticate yourself.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为很多改变更多是关于渴望和理解，而不是强迫自己或试图驯化自己。

sentences.en: So it's efficiency again, I guess, you know, aligning the thing that you want to do with the way that you feel about what it is that you want to do.
sentences.zh: 所以这又是效率问题，我想，将你想做的事与你对这件事的感受对齐。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's not getting caught up in a half desire or mimetic desire. it's really just being aware of what it is that you actually want at this point in time and when you want something then you will act on it with maximal capability and that's the time to act on it in the meantime just doing it because other people tell you you should do it or society tells you you should do it or you feel slightly guilty about it these are these are half-hearted efforts and half-hearted efforts don't get you there you mentioned anxiety before uh imagine how effective you'd be if you weren't anxious all the time is one of yours.
sentences.zh: 是的，不要陷入半吊子的渴望或模仿性渴望。这真的是要意识到你在此时此刻真正想要的是什么。当你想要某样东西时，你会以最大的能力去行动，那才是行动的时候。在此期间，仅仅因为别人告诉你应该做，或者社会告诉你应该做，或者你对此感到有点内疚，这些都是半吊子的努力，而半吊子的努力是不会带你到达目的地的。你之前提到了焦虑，你的一条推文是：“想象一下，如果你不再整天焦虑，你会多么高效。”

sentences.en: And anxiety is the emotion du jour of the 21st century.
sentences.zh: 焦虑是21世纪的情绪代名词。

sentences.en: And lots of driven people, very anxious, very paranoid.
sentences.zh: 很多有干劲的人，非常焦虑，非常多疑。

sentences.en: That's what's caused them to be affected.
sentences.zh: 这就是导致他们高效的原因。

sentences.en: It pays so much attention, detail-oriented, not letting things go, staying up at night, thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 投入了太多注意力，注重细节，不放过任何事情，彻夜难眠，思考它。

sentences.en: That's the paranoia coming in. What have you come to learn about anxiety and dealing with it?
sentences.zh: 这就是偏执带来的影响。关于焦虑以及如何应对它，你学到了什么？

sentences.en: So anxiety and stress are interesting. They're very related.
sentences.zh: 焦虑和压力很有趣。它们非常相关。

sentences.en: Stress is when, like if you look at an iron beam, when an iron beam is under stress, it's because it's being bent in two different directions at the same time.
sentences.zh: 压力是……就像你看一根铁梁，当铁梁处于压力下时，是因为它同时被向两个不同的方向弯曲。

sentences.en: So when your mind is under stress, it's because it has two conflicting desires at once.
sentences.zh: 所以当你的头脑处于压力下时，是因为它同时有两个相互冲突的渴望。

sentences.en: So for example, you know, you want to be liked, but you want to do something selfish and you can't reconcile the two.
sentences.zh: 例如，你想被人喜欢，但你想做一些自私的事，你无法调和这两者。

sentences.en: And so you are under stress. You want to do something for somebody else.
sentences.zh: 所以你处于压力之下。你想为别人做点事。

sentences.en: You want to do something for yourself, right?
sentences.zh: 你想为自己做点事，对吧？

sentences.en: These are examples. You don't want to go to work, but you want to make money.
sentences.zh: 这些都是例子。你不想去上班，但你想赚钱。

sentences.en: So you're under stress, right? So you have two conflicting desires.
sentences.zh: 所以你处于压力之下，对吧？你有两个相互冲突的渴望。

sentences.en: And I think one of the ways to get through stress is to acknowledge that, oh, I actually have two conflicting desires.
sentences.zh: 我认为缓解压力的方法之一是承认：“哦，我实际上有两个相互冲突的渴望。”

sentences.en: And either I need to resolve it, I need to pick one and then be okay losing the other, or I will decide later.
sentences.zh: 要么我需要解决它，选一个并接受失去另一个的代价，要么我以后再决定。

sentences.en: But at least just being aware of why your stress can help alleviate a lot of stress. and then anxiety i think is sort of this pervasive unidentifiable stress where you're just kind of stressed out all the time and you're not even sure why and you can't even identify the underlying problem and the reason for that is because you you have so many uh unresolved problems unresolved stress points that are piled up in your life that you can no longer identify what the problems are and there's this mountain of garbage in your mind and it's a little bit of a Thank you. poking out the top like an iceberg and that's anxiety but underneath there's a lot of unresolved things and so you just need to kind of go through very carefully every time you're anxious like okay why am i anxious this time i don't know why oh well let me sit here and just think about it let me write down what the possible causes could be let me meditate on it let me journal let me talk to a therapist let me talk to my friends let me just kind of see like when does that stress go away.
sentences.zh: 但至少意识到为什么会感到压力，可以帮助减轻很多压力。至于焦虑，我认为这是一种普遍的、无法识别的压力，你整天都感到压力很大，甚至不知道为什么，甚至无法识别潜在的问题。原因在于，你生活中堆积了太多未解决的问题、未解决的压力点，以至于你无法再识别出问题到底是什么。你的头脑里有一座垃圾山，只有一点点像冰山一样露在顶端，那就是焦虑，但在下面有很多未解决的事情。所以你需要非常仔细地梳理，每次感到焦虑时，就想：“好吧，这次我为什么焦虑？我不知道为什么。”哦，好吧，让我坐在这里思考一下，让我写下可能的原因，让我冥想，让我写日记，让我和治疗师谈谈，让我和朋友谈谈，让我看看这种压力什么时候消失。

sentences.en: If you can kind of identify and unravel and resolve these issues, then I think that helps get rid of anxiety.
sentences.zh: 如果你能识别、拆解并解决这些问题，那么我认为这有助于消除焦虑。

sentences.en: A lot of the anxiety is piled up because we move through life too quickly, not observing our own reactions to things.
sentences.zh: 很多焦虑的堆积是因为我们生活节奏太快，没有观察自己对事物的反应。

sentences.en: We don't resolve them. So this goes counter to what I was saying earlier about not reflecting too much on things.
sentences.zh: 我们没有解决它们。这与我之前说的不要过度反思相矛盾。

sentences.en: But you reflect on the problems to observe them and solve them.
sentences.zh: 但你反思问题是为了观察它们并解决它们。

sentences.en: You don't reflect on them to feel better about yourself.
sentences.zh: 你不是为了让自己感觉更好而反思它们。

sentences.en: To indulge them. Well, if you're doing it to just feel better about yourself, that could be strengthening your personality and your ego and could be creating a more fragile personality um you know one one big anxiety result for me is just ruminating on death i think that's a good one you're gonna die it's all going to zero you cannot take anything with you and i know this is trite and i know the the we don't spend enough time thinking about the big questions we kind of give up on them when we're very very young you know a little child might ask the big questions like why are we here?
sentences.zh: 为了放纵它们。嗯，如果你这样做只是为了让自己感觉更好，那可能会强化你的个性和自我，并可能创造一个更脆弱的个性。你知道，对我来说，一个巨大的焦虑来源就是对死亡的沉思，我觉得这很好。你会死，一切都会归零，你什么都带不走。我知道这很陈词滥调，我知道我们没有花足够的时间思考大问题，我们在很小的时候就放弃了它们。你知道，一个小孩子可能会问大问题，比如“我们为什么在这里？”

sentences.en: What's the meaning of life? What is this all about?
sentences.zh: “生命的意义是什么？这一切是为了什么？”

sentences.en: You know, is there Santa Claus? Is there God?
sentences.zh: “你知道，有圣诞老人吗？有上帝吗？”

sentences.en: But then as adults, we're taught not to think about these things.
sentences.zh: 但作为成年人，我们被教导不要思考这些事情。

sentences.en: We've given up on them. But I think the big questions are the big questions for good reasons.
sentences.zh: 我们放弃了它们。但我认为大问题之所以是“大问题”是有充分理由的。

sentences.en: And if you can keep the idea in front of you at all times that you're going to die and that everything goes literally to zero, what's there to stress about?
sentences.zh: 如果你能时刻保持这个想法：你会死，一切最终都会归零，那还有什么好焦虑的呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, for better or worse, life is very short.
sentences.zh: 是的，不管好坏，生命都很短暂。

sentences.en: How should people deal with its briefness? enjoy it make the best of it you know it's it's even briefer than that each moment just disappears it's gone there's only a present moment and it's gone instantly so if you're not if you're not there for it if you're stressed out or you're anxious or you're thinking about something else you missed it so you're any moment when you're not in that moment you are dead to that moment you might as well be dead because your mind is off doing something else or you know living in some imagined reality that is just a very poor substitute for the actual reality so one of my recent realizations was what is wasted time what is what is a waste of time so i don't like to waste time but what is wasted time and everything is wasted time in a sense because nothing matters in the ultimate.
sentences.zh: 人们应该如何面对它的短暂？享受它，充分利用它。你知道，它甚至比那更短暂，每一刻都在消失，它走了。只有当下这一刻，而且它瞬间即逝。所以如果你不在当下，如果你感到压力、焦虑或在想别的事情，你就错过了。所以任何你不在当下的时刻，你对那一刻来说就是死的。你还不如死了，因为你的头脑在做别的事情，或者生活在某种想象的现实中，那只是对真实现实的一个非常糟糕的替代品。所以我最近的感悟之一是：什么是浪费时间？什么是浪费时间？我不喜欢浪费时间，但什么是浪费时间？从某种意义上说，一切都是浪费时间，因为从终极意义上讲，什么都不重要。

sentences.en: But in each moment, the thing matters. In each moment, it's the only thing that matters, actually.
sentences.zh: 但在每一刻，这件事很重要。实际上，在每一刻，它是唯一重要的事情。

sentences.en: What's happening in front of you literally has all the meaning in the world.
sentences.zh: 发生在你面前的事情，字面上拥有世界上所有的意义。

sentences.en: And so what matters is just being present for the thing.
sentences.zh: 所以重要的是要活在当下。

sentences.en: So if you're doing something that you want to do and you're fully there for it, then it's not wasted time.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你正在做你想做的事，并且全身心地投入其中，那就不算浪费时间。

sentences.en: If you don't want to do it and your mind is running away from it and you're reacting against it and you're wishing you were somewhere else and you're thinking about some other thing or you're anticipating some future thing or regretting some past thing or being fearful of something, then that's wasted time.
sentences.zh: 如果你不想做它，你的头脑在逃避它，你在抵触它，你希望自己在别的地方，你在想别的事情，或者你在期待未来的某事，或者后悔过去的某事，或者对某事感到恐惧，那么那就是浪费时间。

sentences.en: That's time that's being wasted when you're not actually present for the reality in front of you.
sentences.zh: 当你没有真正活在眼前的现实中时，时间就被浪费了。

sentences.en: So my definition of wasted time, yes, I do want some material things in life and there are things that have more value than others within this life, but this life is very short and bounded.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我对浪费时间的定义。是的，我确实想要生活中的一些物质东西，在这个生命中有些东西比其他东西更有价值，但这个生命是非常短暂且有边界的。

sentences.en: So the true wasted time is a time that you are not present for when you are not there for it, when you're not doing the thing you want to do to the best of a capability such that you're immersed in it.
sentences.zh: 所以真正的浪费时间是你没有活在当下的时间，当你不在那里时，当你没有尽最大能力去做你想做的事以至于沉浸其中时。

sentences.en: If you're not immersed in this moment, then you're wasting your time.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有沉浸在这一刻，那你就是在浪费时间。

sentences.en: People get worried about dying and no longer being here, but they don't realize that so much of their life is spent not being here in any case.
sentences.zh: 人们担心死亡和不再存在，但他们没有意识到，无论如何，他们生命中的大部分时间都花在“不在场”上。

sentences.en: That's right. And I think people crave being here for it.
sentences.zh: 没错。而且我认为人们渴望活在当下。

sentences.en: And when you're here for it, you're actually not thinking about yourself.
sentences.zh: 当你活在当下时，你其实并没有在想自己。

sentences.en: You are more immersed in the thing, the moment, the task at hand.
sentences.zh: 你更沉浸在事物、当下、手头的任务中。

sentences.en: We don't want peace of mind. We want peace for our mind.
sentences.zh: 我们不需要“心安”（peace of mind），我们需要“让心安宁”（peace for our mind）。

sentences.en: That's right. Yeah. You don't peace. The mind is what will eat you alive if you let it.
sentences.zh: 没错。是的。你不需要“心安”。如果你任由头脑摆布，它会把你活活吃掉。

sentences.en: And there's more to you than the mind. How so?
sentences.zh: 而且你不仅仅是你的头脑。怎么说？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, it's very, I don't want to disassemble the body, so to speak, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是说，我不想拆解身体，对吧？

sentences.en: Because. Please go on. Yeah. At the end of the day, like everything arises within your consciousness, right?
sentences.zh: 因为……请继续。是的，归根结底，一切都产生于你的意识之中，对吧？

sentences.en: You've got nowhere else to experience it.
sentences.zh: 你没有别的地方可以体验它。

sentences.en: Sorry? You've got nowhere else to experience it.
sentences.zh: 抱歉？你没有别的地方可以体验它。

sentences.en: And that consciousness is relatively static in the sense that it's been exactly the same from the moment you were born to the moment you die.
sentences.zh: 而那种意识是相对静态的，从你出生那一刻到你死亡那一刻，它完全一样。

sentences.en: And everything that you experience from your body, from your mind to the world, to everything is within that consciousness.
sentences.zh: 你体验到的一切，从你的身体、你的头脑到世界，到一切，都在那个意识之内。

sentences.en: And that thing, that base layer of being, and this is what the Buddhists will tell you, is the real thing.
sentences.zh: 而那个东西，那个存在的底层——这就是佛教徒会告诉你的——才是真实的东西。

sentences.en: Everything that comes and goes in the middle, including your mind, including your body, is unreal. and trying to find stability in those transient things is your castle that you're building on sand that's going to crumble.
sentences.zh: 中间来来去去的一切，包括你的头脑、你的身体，都是不真实的。试图在那些短暂的事物中寻找稳定性，就像你在沙滩上建造城堡，最终会崩塌。

sentences.en: Life is going to play out the way it's going to play out.
sentences.zh: 生活会按照它该有的方式展开。

sentences.en: There will be some good and some bad. Most of it is actually just up to your interpretation.
sentences.zh: 会有一些好的，也会有一些坏的。大部分其实取决于你的解读。

sentences.en: You're born, you have a set of sensory experiences, and then you die.
sentences.zh: 你出生，你有一系列感官体验，然后你死亡。

sentences.en: How you choose to interpret those experiences is up to you and different people interpret them in different ways.
sentences.zh: 你选择如何解读这些体验取决于你自己，不同的人以不同的方式解读它们。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's the old line about two people walking down the street.
sentences.zh: 是的，就像那句老话，两个人走在街上。

sentences.en: They're having the exact same experience one is happy one is sad right it's a narrative in their heads it's how they choose to interpret um so i think when i said that it was a long time ago i was talking more about having positive interpretations and negative interpretations but these days i think it's better just not to have any interpretations and to just allow things to be you're still going to have interpretations you can't stop it and nor should you try but even that having an interpretation is just a thing you can leave alone.
sentences.zh: 他们有着完全相同的经历，一个快乐，一个悲伤，对吧？这是他们脑子里的叙事，是他们选择解读的方式。所以我想，我很久以前说那话时，更多是在谈论拥有积极的解读和消极的解读，但现在我认为最好什么解读都不要有，只是让事物顺其自然。你仍然会有解读，你无法阻止，也不应该尝试。但即使是拥有解读，也只是你可以放下不管的一件事。

sentences.en: Yeah, I really want to try and just dig in a little more to the best way to remind people that they should value their time.
sentences.zh: 是的，我真的很想尝试深入探讨一下，提醒人们应该珍惜时间的最好方法。

sentences.en: Just how brief it is that the time that you spend ruminating, being distracted, fears of the past, regrets.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是因为它太短暂了，你花在反刍、分心、对过去的恐惧、后悔上的时间。

sentences.en: Well, I don't want to tell anybody how to live their life.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不想告诉任何人该如何生活。

sentences.en: I would just say that to the extent that you want to improve your quality of life, the easiest and best way to do that is to observe your own mind and your own thoughts and be a little, not necessarily critical, but be observant of yourself more objectively.
sentences.zh: 我只想说，如果你想提高生活质量，最简单、最好的方法就是观察自己的头脑和想法，不必非要批判，但要更客观地观察自己。

sentences.en: And then you'll kind of realize your own loops and patterns.
sentences.zh: 然后你就会意识到自己的循环和模式。

sentences.en: It takes time. It's not overnight. It's not instantaneous.
sentences.zh: 这需要时间。不是一夜之间，不是瞬间发生的。

sentences.en: So you mean letting go is not a one-time event?
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是“放下”不是一次性的事件？

sentences.en: Yeah, and letting go is not necessarily even the right answer.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且“放下”甚至不一定是正确的答案。

sentences.en: Like, yes, if you're trying to be an enlightened being and you want to live like a god and everything's gonna be perfect and be a Buddha, sure, you can let go.
sentences.zh: 比如，是的，如果你试图成为一个开悟的人，你想像神一样生活，一切都完美无缺，成为佛陀，当然，你可以放下。

sentences.en: But I think in practice, it's actually quite hard to do.
sentences.zh: 但我认为在实践中，这实际上很难做到。

sentences.en: I think I would say that you're going to find a lot of fulfillment out of life by just doing what you want to do and genuinely exploring what it is that you want, rather than doing what other people expect you to do or society expects you to do or what you might just think should be done by default. um you know i think most older successful people will tell you that their life was best when they lived it unapologetically on their own terms be selfish holistic selfishness there we go exactly we can clip that little i'm telling you about being selfish yeah yeah yeah just keep running about bad guy uh great i i had this insight or a question i guess how much do you think that we should trust the voice in our heads because half of wisdom suggests to rely on your sort of bottom up intuition and then half of it has to be sort of top-down rational as possible.
sentences.zh: 我想我会说，你会通过做你想做的事，真正探索你想要什么，而不是做别人期望你做的事、社会期望你做的事，或者你认为默认应该做的事，从而在生活中找到很多满足感。你知道，我认为大多数年长的成功人士会告诉你，当他们不道歉地按自己的方式生活时，他们的生活是最好的。做一个自私的人，整体性的自私。就是这样，我们可以剪辑这一段，我正在谈论自私。是的，是的，继续谈论坏人。太棒了。我有一个洞察或一个问题，你认为我们应该多大程度上信任脑子里的声音？因为一半的智慧建议依赖你自下而上的直觉，而另一半必须尽可能自上而下地理性。

sentences.en: How do you navigate the tension between head and gut in this way?
sentences.zh: 你如何在这种方式下处理头脑和直觉之间的张力？

sentences.en: I think the gut is what decides. The head is kind of what rationalizes it afterwards.
sentences.zh: 我认为直觉是做决定的东西。头脑是事后将其合理化的东西。

sentences.en: The gut is the ultimate decision maker. And what is the gut?
sentences.zh: 直觉是最终的决策者。什么是直觉？

sentences.en: The gut is refined judgment. It's taste.
sentences.zh: 直觉是提炼后的判断力。是品味。

sentences.en: Aggregates. So aggregated. And it could be aggregated through evolution and it's in your genes and your DNA, or it could be aggregated through your experiences and what you've thought through.
sentences.zh: 聚合。所以是聚合的。它可以通过进化聚合，存在于你的基因和DNA中，或者通过你的经历和你思考过的事情聚合。

sentences.en: The mind is good at solving new problems and new problems in the external world that have defined edges, beginnings and ends and objectives.
sentences.zh: 头脑擅长解决新问题，以及外部世界中那些有明确边界、起点、终点和目标的新问题。

sentences.en: What the mind is actually really bad at is making hard decisions.
sentences.zh: 头脑实际上非常不擅长做艰难的决定。

sentences.en: So when you have a hard decision to make, I find it's better to, yes, you ruminate on it, you think through all the pros and cons, but then you sleep on it.
sentences.zh: 所以当你必须做一个艰难的决定时，我发现最好是……是的，你反思它，你想清楚所有的利弊，但然后你要“睡一觉”。

sentences.en: You wait a couple of days, you wait until the gut answer appears with conviction and it feels right.
sentences.zh: 你等几天，等到直觉的答案带着信念出现，感觉对了。

sentences.en: And when you're younger, it takes longer because you just don't have as much experience.
sentences.zh: 当你年轻时，这需要更长时间，因为你没有那么多经验。

sentences.en: And when you're older, it can happen much faster, which is why, you know, and you have less time to.
sentences.zh: 当你年长时，它发生得更快，这就是为什么……而且你没有那么多时间。

sentences.en: Yeah. And old people are more set in their way as a consequence, right?
sentences.zh: 是的。所以老年人因此更固执，对吧？

sentences.en: They know what they want. They know what they don't want.
sentences.zh: 他们知道自己想要什么。他们知道自己不想要什么。

sentences.en: So it takes time to develop your gut instinct and judgment.
sentences.zh: 所以培养直觉和判断力需要时间。

sentences.en: But once you've developed them, don't trust anything else because you can't go against your gut.
sentences.zh: 但一旦你培养了它们，就不要相信其他任何东西，因为你不能违背你的直觉。

sentences.en: It'll bite you in the end. Usually in relationships that failed, you can look back and say, oh, actually I knew it was going to fail because of this reason, but I kind of went ahead anyway, because I wanted it to be this way, right?
sentences.zh: 它最终会反噬你。通常在失败的关系中，你可以回顾过去说：“哦，其实我因为这个原因知道它会失败，但我还是继续了，因为我希望它是这样的，对吧？”

sentences.en: I wanted this person to be a different way than they are.
sentences.zh: 我希望这个人变得与他们实际的样子不同。

sentences.en: I wanted to get a different thing out of it than I thought I was going to, than I knew I was going to get, but I just wanted it.
sentences.zh: 我希望从中得到与我预想不同的东西，尽管我知道我会得到什么，但我就是想要它。

sentences.en: So sometimes desire will override your judgment and then wishful thinking.
sentences.zh: 所以有时欲望会凌驾于你的判断力之上，然后是“一厢情愿”。

sentences.en: It traps you into a pathway that just chews up time.
sentences.zh: 它把你困在一条只会消耗时间的路径上。

sentences.en: What's that insight of yours? We think we can't change ourselves, but we can.
sentences.zh: 你那句洞察是什么？“我们认为我们无法改变自己，但我们可以。”

sentences.en: We think we can change other people, but we can't.
sentences.zh: “我们认为我们可以改变别人，但我们不能。”

sentences.en: Exactly. I think to add to that, you can't change other people.
sentences.zh: 没错。我想补充一点，你无法改变别人。

sentences.en: You can change your reaction to them. You can change yourself, but other people only change through trauma or their own insight on their own schedule and never in a way that you like.
sentences.zh: 你可以改变你对他们的反应。你可以改变自己，但别人只会通过创伤或他们自己的洞察，按他们自己的时间表改变，而且永远不会以你喜欢的方式改变。

sentences.en: Yeah, Alain de Botton says that people do sometimes change, but rarely in relationships and never when they're told to.
sentences.zh: 是的，Alain de Botton说人们有时确实会改变，但很少在关系中改变，而且永远不会在被告知要改变时改变。

sentences.en: Absolutely. Yeah, the fastest way to kind of alienate somebody is to tell them to change.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。是的，疏远某人最快的方法就是告诉他们去改变。

sentences.en: In fact, the Dale Carnegie School of Public Speaking, you know, the way that operates is they get you up there and they realize that the number one problem with public speaking is that people are very self-conscious. and so people who are practicing in the Dale Carnegie School of Public Speaking, I don't know, I never went through it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，Dale Carnegie演讲学校，你知道，它的运作方式是他们让你站上去，他们意识到公开演讲的头号问题是人们非常自我意识。所以那些在Dale Carnegie演讲学校练习的人……我不知道，我从没去过。

sentences.en: I heard this second hand, so I could be wrong, but I like the story where they get up and they start speaking and the people in the audience are only allowed to compliment them, genuine compliments, not fake compliments, on things that they did well, but you're not allowed to criticize them on things that they did poorly and eventually they kind of get through it and they develop self-confidence.
sentences.zh: 我是二手听说的，所以我可能是错的，但我喜欢这个故事：他们站起来开始演讲，观众只被允许称赞他们，真诚的称赞，不是虚假的称赞，称赞他们做得好的地方，但不允许批评他们做得不好的地方。最终他们克服了，并建立了自信。

sentences.en: The same way there's like the Michelle Thomas School of Language Learning and on that one what they do is you listen to a teacher talking to a student they're not teaching you you're not expected to remember or memorize anything you just listen to a student stumbling over the language it's a better way to learn because you yourself don't feel flustered you're being tested graded oh so you're not in your own head as much correct you're not in your own head and you're just you might even be laughing at the student or you might be agreeing with the teacher or vice versa or sympathizing with the student but because you are a passive observer you can be more objective about it and you aren't threatened or fearful and you can learn better and coming back to the original point of you can't change people if you do want to change someone's behavior i i think the only effective way to do it is to compliment them when they do something you want not to positive yeah exactly not to insult them or be negative or critical when they do something you don't want and we can't help it it's obviously in our nature to criticize and i do it as well but it just reminds me that like when somebody does something praiseworthy don't forget to praise them like definitely go out of your way and it'll be genuine.
sentences.zh: 同样，有Michelle Thomas语言学习法，在那门课上，他们做的是你听老师和学生交谈，他们不是在教你，你不被期望记住或背诵任何东西，你只是听学生在语言上磕磕绊绊。这是一种更好的学习方式，因为你自己不会感到慌乱，你没有被测试、打分。哦，所以你没有那么沉浸在自己的头脑里？正确，你没有沉浸在自己的头脑里，你可能甚至在嘲笑那个学生，或者你可能在同意老师，反之亦然，或者同情学生，但因为你是一个被动的观察者，你可以更客观地看待它，你没有受到威胁或恐惧，你可以学得更好。回到最初的观点，你无法改变别人，如果你确实想改变某人的行为，我认为唯一有效的方法是在他们做你想做的事时称赞他们，而不是……积极的，是的，没错，而不是在他们做你不想要的事时侮辱他们或消极、批评。我们无法避免，批评显然是我们的天性，我也这样做，但这只是提醒我，当某人做了值得称赞的事时，别忘了称赞他们，一定要不遗余力，而且要是真诚的。

sentences.en: It has to be genuine. It can't be a fake thing.
sentences.zh: 它必须是真诚的。不能是虚假的东西。

sentences.en: This is not you know, one of those just dropping compliments type thing eventually that people will see through that.
sentences.zh: 这不是那种……你知道，那种随便抛出赞美之类的事情，人们最终会看穿的。

sentences.en: They want authenticity, but just don't forget to praise people when they do something praiseworthy and you'll get more of that behavior.
sentences.zh: 他们想要真实性，但只是别忘了在人们做值得称赞的事时称赞他们，你会得到更多那样的行为。

sentences.en: There was a really famous thread on Reddit about five questions to ask yourself if you're uncertain about your relationship.
sentences.zh: Reddit上有一个非常著名的帖子，关于如果你对关系不确定，可以问自己的五个问题。

sentences.en: One of the questions was, are you truly in love with your partner or just their potential or the idea of them?
sentences.zh: 其中一个问题是：“你是真的爱你的伴侣，还是仅仅爱他们的潜力或关于他们的想法？”

sentences.en: And that's the, you know, they show such great promise.
sentences.zh: 这就是……你知道，他们表现出如此巨大的希望。

sentences.en: They look at their ability for for change and growth they they they're on the right path the partner matching thing is so hard uh you know when people come and ask me like oh should i be with this person like well if you're asking me the answer is clearly no right because you wouldn't have to ask if you were with the right person or when you ask someone like why they're uh in a relationship with somebody they start reading out his or her resume right that's also a bad sign so what do you mean oh it's like oh we have so much in common we like to golf together it's like it's not a basis for a relationship or oh it's uh you know she's a ballerina or you know he went to harvard or what have you this is a resume item so that's not who the person actually is what's a better more the the more materially and concretely definable the reasons are you're together the worse they are the ineffable is actually where the sort of true love lies because real love is a form of unity it's a form of connection it's connecting spirits oh you too my consciousness meets your consciousness it's that it the the underlying drive uh in love in art in uh science in uh mysticism is the desire for unity it's a desire for connection as you know bor has famously wrote in every human there's a sense that something infinite has been lost you know there's a god shaped hole in you you're trying to fill and so we're always trying to find that connection love is trying to find it in one other person and saying okay you're male i'm female or whatever and you know whatever your predilections are and now we connect now we form a whole a connected hole or in mysticism it's like it's all about okay sit down meditate and you'll feel the hole in science it's like oh you know
