creates that sense of awe in art it's like i feel an emotion i create a piece of art around it and then you see that painting or you see the Sistine Chapel or you read the poem and you feel that emotion.
sentences.zh: 他们看着他们改变和成长的能力，他们走在正确的道路上。伴侣匹配这件事太难了。你知道，当人们来问我：“哦，我应该和这个人在一起吗？”嗯，如果你在问我，答案显然是否定的，对吧？因为如果你和对的人在一起，你就不需要问了。或者当你问某人为什么他们和某人在一起时，他们开始背诵他或她的简历，那也是一个坏迹象。所以你是什么意思？哦，就像“哦，我们有很多共同点，我们喜欢一起打高尔夫”，这不是关系的基础。或者“哦，她是芭蕾舞演员”，或者“他去了哈佛”之类的，这是简历项目。所以那不是那个人实际的样子。什么是更好的答案？“我只是喜欢和这个人在一起，我只是信任他们，我喜欢和他们在一起，我喜欢他有多能干，我喜欢她有多善良，我喜欢她的精神，我喜欢他的能量。”你在一起的理由越是物质和具体可定义的，它们就越糟糕。不可言喻的东西实际上才是真爱所在，因为真正的爱是一种统一的形式，它是一种连接，它是连接灵魂。哦，你也是，我的意识遇见你的意识，这就是它。在爱、艺术、科学、神秘主义中，潜在的驱动力是渴望统一，是渴望连接。正如Bohr著名地写道：“在每个人心中，都有某种无限的东西已经丢失的感觉。”你知道，你内心有一个上帝形状的洞，你试图填补它。所以我们总是试图找到那种连接。爱是试图在另一个人身上找到它，说：“好吧，你是男的，我是女的，或者无论你的偏好是什么，现在我们连接了，现在我们形成了一个整体，一个连接的整体。”或者在神秘主义中，它是关于“好吧，坐下来冥想，你会感觉到那个洞”。在科学中，它是“哦，原子碰撞是力学，但这会产生热量，所以热力学和运动或动力学是一个组合理论，那是一个整体”。电和磁是一回事，那是整体，创造了那种敬畏感。在艺术中，它是“我感受到一种情绪，我围绕它创作了一件艺术品，然后你看到那幅画，或者你看到西斯廷教堂，或者你读那首诗，你感受到了那种情绪”。

sentences.en: So again, it's creating unity, it's creating connection.
sentences.zh: 所以，这又是创造统一，创造连接。

sentences.en: And I think everybody craves that. And so when you really love somebody, it's because you feel a sense of wholeness by being around them.
sentences.zh: 我认为每个人都渴望那个。所以当你真正爱某人时，是因为你通过和他们在一起感到了一种完整感。

sentences.en: And that sense of wholeness probably doesn't have anything to do with what school they went to, you know, or what career they're in.
sentences.zh: 而那种完整感可能与他们上了什么学校，或者他们从事什么职业无关。

sentences.en: Just sort of tying that into the life is short, stop fucking about.
sentences.zh: 只是把这一点和“生命短暂，别瞎折腾”联系起来。

sentences.en: If you're faced with a difficult choice and you cannot decide, the answer is no.
sentences.zh: 如果你面临一个艰难的选择，而你无法决定，答案就是“不”。

sentences.en: And the reason is modern society is full of options.
sentences.zh: 原因在于现代社会充满了选择。

sentences.en: Knowing this rationally sounds great, but having the courage to commit to it in reality, I think is a different task and cutting your losses quickly in the big three relationships, jobs, and locations is hard.
sentences.zh: 理性上明白这一点听起来很棒，但要在现实中拿出勇气去践行，我认为是另一回事，而且在工作、居住地和人际关系这三大领域及时止损是非常困难的。

sentences.en: What would you say to someone who may cerebrally be able to agree with you and say, I understand.
sentences.zh: 对于那些在理智上能认同你并说“我理解”的人，你会对他们说什么？

sentences.en: My cousin said this about me. He said that, he said, what I really, he says, what I've really noticed about you is your ability to walk away from situations that are just not. great enough for you or not good enough for you.
sentences.zh: 我表弟曾这样评价我。他说，他真正注意到我的一点是，我有能力离开那些对我不够好、或者说不够理想的处境。

sentences.en: And I think that is a characteristic that I have.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实是我的一种特质。

sentences.en: I will not accept second best outcomes in my life.
sentences.zh: 我绝不会在生活中接受次优的结果。

sentences.en: Ultimately, you will end up wherever is acceptable to you.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，你最终会停留在你所能接受的地方。

sentences.en: You will get out of life whatever is acceptable to you.
sentences.zh: 你从生活中得到的，正是你所能接受的一切。

sentences.en: And there are certain things to me that are very, very important where I will not settle for second best.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，有些事情非常非常重要，在这些事上我绝不妥协，不接受次优选择。

sentences.en: But then there are a lot of other things I just don't care about.
sentences.zh: 但同时，也有很多其他事情我根本不在乎。

sentences.en: Because if I spend all my time caring about those things.
sentences.zh: 因为如果我把所有时间都花在关心那些琐事上，

sentences.en: I don't have the energy for the few things that matter.
sentences.zh: 我就没有精力去处理那几件真正重要的事情了。

sentences.en: And so in decision making, I have a few heuristics for myself.
sentences.zh: 所以在决策时，我为自己设定了一些启发式原则。

sentences.en: Other people can use their own, but mine are, if you can't decide, the answer is no.
sentences.zh: 别人可以用他们自己的，但我的原则是：如果你无法决定，答案就是“不”。

sentences.en: If you're offered an opportunity, if you have a new thing that you're saying yes or no to, that is a change from where you're starting, the answer is by default, always no.
sentences.zh: 如果有人给你提供一个机会，或者你面临一件需要决定是否接受的新事物，而这与你目前的起点有所不同，那么默认答案永远是“不”。

sentences.en: Secondly, if you have two decisions, if you have A or B, and both seem like very equal, take the path that's more painful in the short term the one that's going to be painful immediately because your brain is always trying to avoid pain so any pain that is imminent it is going to treat as much larger than it actually is this is kind of like a decision-making equivalent of taleb surgeon uh taleb surgeon whether you want the surgeon doesn't look as good because he's more likely to be a good surgeon yeah it's similar in that appearances are deceiving because you're avoiding conflict you're avoiding pain so take the path that's more painful in the short term because your brain is creating this illusion that the short-term pain is greater than the long-term pain because long-term yeah you'll commit your future self to all kinds of long-term exactly so take the more short-term painful one and then finally the last one which i would try to couple gupta with uh is that you want to take it take the choice that will leave you more equanimous in the long term by quantumus he means like more peace more mental peace in the long term.
sentences.zh: 其次，如果你有两个选择，A或B，而且看起来不相上下，那就选择短期内更痛苦的那条路，也就是会立即带来痛苦的那条，因为你的大脑总是试图逃避痛苦，所以任何迫在眉睫的痛苦在它看来都会被放大，这有点像Nassim Taleb所说的决策等价物，比如你为什么不想找一个看起来不够好的外科医生，因为他可能反而是一位好医生，是的，这很相似，因为表象往往具有欺骗性，你在逃避冲突，逃避痛苦，所以选择短期内更痛苦的那条路，因为你的大脑制造了一种幻觉，让你觉得短期痛苦比长期痛苦更严重，因为从长远来看，你会把未来的自己投入到各种长期的承诺中，没错，所以选择短期更痛苦的那一个，最后一点，我想结合Gupta的观点，那就是你要选择那个能让你在长期内保持内心平静的选择，所谓“内心平静”是指更平和、更安宁。

sentences.en: So whatever clears your mind more and will have you having less self-talk in the future, if you can model that out, that is probably the better route to go.
sentences.zh: 所以，无论什么能让你的思绪更清晰，让你未来减少内耗，如果你能模拟出结果，那可能就是更好的选择。

sentences.en: And then I would focus decision-making down on the three things that really matter because everything else is downstream of these three decisions, especially these are early life decisions.
sentences.zh: 然后我会把决策重点放在那三件真正重要的事情上，因为其他一切都是这三个决策的下游，尤其是这些早期的人生决策。

sentences.en: Later in life, you have different things to optimize for, but early in life, you're trying to figure out who you're with, what you're doing, and where you live.
sentences.zh: 人生后期，你有不同的优化目标，但在人生早期，你是在试图弄清楚你和谁在一起、你在做什么、以及你住在哪里。

sentences.en: And I think on all three of those, you want to think pretty hard about it.
sentences.zh: 我认为在这三点上，你都需要深思熟虑。

sentences.en: And people do some of these unconsciously.
sentences.zh: 而且人们往往会无意识地处理其中一些问题。

sentences.en: You know, who you're with very often is like, well, we were in a relationship, we stumbled along, it felt okay, it had been enough time, so we got married, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，关于“和谁在一起”，通常是这样的：我们谈恋爱了，顺其自然，感觉还行，时间也够久了，所以我们就结婚了，对吧？

sentences.en: Not great reasons. Maybe not terrible reasons either.
sentences.zh: 这并不是什么伟大的理由。但也可能不算太糟糕。

sentences.en: I mean, it's people who overthink these things sometimes don't get the right answer, but maybe here, if you are the kind of person that's not going to settle for second best, you iterate, you iterate on a closed timeframe, so you don't run out the clock, and then you decide.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有时过度思考这些事情的人反而得不到正确答案，但也许在这里，如果你是一个绝不接受次优选择的人，你会进行迭代，在有限的时间框架内迭代，这样你就不会虚度光阴，然后做出决定。

sentences.en: On what you do, you try a whole bunch of different things until you find the one that feels like play to you, looks like work to others, you can't lose at it.
sentences.zh: 关于“做什么”，你要尝试各种不同的事情，直到找到那件对你来说像玩耍、对别人来说像工作，而且你注定不会输的事情。

sentences.en: Get some leverage, try to find some practical application of it and go into that.
sentences.zh: 获得一些杠杆，尝试找到它的实际应用，然后投入其中。

sentences.en: And then where you live, where you live is really important.
sentences.zh: 至于“住在哪里”，这真的很重要。

sentences.en: I don't think people spend enough time on that one.
sentences.zh: 我不认为人们在这上面花了足够的时间。

sentences.en: I think people pick cities randomly based on where I went to school or where my family happened to be or where my friend was or I visited one weekend, I really liked it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得人们选择城市很随意，基于我去了哪所学校，或者我的家人碰巧在哪里，或者我的朋友在哪里，或者我某个周末去玩过，觉得很喜欢。

sentences.en: You really want to think it through because where you live really constrains and defines your opportunities.
sentences.zh: 你真的需要深思熟虑，因为你居住的地方极大地限制并定义了你的机会。

sentences.en: It's going to determine your friend circle.
sentences.zh: 它将决定你的朋友圈。

sentences.en: It's going to determine your dating pool.
sentences.zh: 它将决定你的择偶范围。

sentences.en: It's going to determine your job opportunities.
sentences.zh: 它将决定你的工作机会。

sentences.en: It's going to determine the food and air and water quality that you receive.
sentences.zh: 它将决定你所接触的食物、空气和水质。

sentences.en: It's going to determine your proximity to your family, which might be important as you get older and have kids.
sentences.zh: 它将决定你与家人的距离，这在你变老和有了孩子后可能很重要。

sentences.en: So very, very, very important decision. Weather, you know, quality of life, how much do you stay inside or outside, how long you'll live based on that.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常、非常、非常重要的决定。天气、生活质量、你待在室内还是室外的时间，以及基于这些因素你的寿命长短。

sentences.en: And I think people choose that one probably more poorly than, They put a lot less thought into that one than the other two.
sentences.zh: 我觉得人们在这一点上的选择可能比其他两点更糟糕，他们在这上面投入的思考远少于前两点。

sentences.en: In some ways, yeah, but also you're so right how many people fall backward into a relationship, and before they know it, we're living together.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面确实如此，而且你说得太对了，有多少人稀里糊涂地进入一段关系，还没反应过来就已经住在一起了。

sentences.en: We got a dog, we got a kid, we would marry, wouldn't we?
sentences.zh: 我们养了狗，有了孩子，我们结婚吧，好吗？

sentences.en: And then when you have kids, because then that's half of you and half of them running around, you're never going to separate yourself from that.
sentences.zh: 然后当你有了孩子，因为那是你和对方的一半血脉在奔跑，你永远无法真正与那个人彻底切割。

sentences.en: So once you have a child with somebody, then the most important thing in the world to you is half that other person, whether you like them or not.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦你和某人有了孩子，那么世界上最重要的事情就是那个人的一半，无论你是否喜欢对方。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Jeffrey Miller had a tweet a long time ago that I always think about, and he said, every parenting book in the world could be replaced with one book on behavioral genetics. that i'm a big believer in genetics yes i do think a lot of behavior is downstream of genetics and i think we underplay that we like to overplay nurture and underplay nurture for us or say we'll underplay nature for societal reasons but nature is a big deal um the temperament of the person you marry is probably going to be reflected in your child by default people can change securely attached kid pick a securely attached partner well the secret to a happy relationship is two happy people right so i would say if you want to be happy then uh be with a happy person don't think you're going to be with someone who's unhappy and then make them happy down the road or if you're okay with them being unhappy but there are other things you like about them that's fine but this goes back to their unhappiness with other things yes and actually we talked a little bit about how people do connect successfully you know on spirit and and those things but that's maybe a little too abstract if you want to get a little more practical it could be based on values and values are a set of things you won't compromise on values are the tough decisions of oh my parent got sick, do they move in with us or do we put them in a nursing home?
sentences.zh: Jeffrey Miller很久以前发过一条推文，我一直记在心里，他说，世界上所有的育儿书都可以被一本行为遗传学书所取代。我非常相信遗传学，是的，我确实认为很多行为都是遗传的下游产物，我认为我们低估了这一点，我们喜欢过度强调后天培养，而为了社会原因低估了先天因素，但先天因素影响巨大，你结婚对象的脾气很可能会反映在你的孩子身上，默认情况下，人们是可以改变的，比如找一个依恋类型安全的孩子，选一个依恋类型安全的伴侣，嗯，幸福关系的秘诀是两个幸福的人，对吧？所以我认为如果你想幸福，那就和一个幸福的人在一起，不要指望和一个不幸福的人在一起，然后以后再让他们变得幸福，或者如果你能接受他们不幸福，但你喜欢他们身上的其他特质，那也可以，但这又回到了他们对其他事情的不满上，是的，其实我们之前聊过人们是如何成功建立联系的，比如在精神层面等等，但这可能太抽象了，如果想更实际一点，可以基于价值观，价值观是一套你绝不妥协的东西，价值观是那些艰难的抉择，比如：我父母生病了，他们是搬来和我们住，还是送去养老院？

sentences.en: Do we give the children money or do we not?
sentences.zh: 我们要给孩子们钱吗，还是不给？

sentences.en: Do we move across the country to be closer to our family or do we stay put where we are?
sentences.zh: 我们要搬到全国各地去离家人更近，还是留在原地？

sentences.en: Do we argue about politics? Do we care or do we not?
sentences.zh: 我们要为政治争论吗？我们在乎还是不在乎？

sentences.en: Values are way more important than checklist items.
sentences.zh: 价值观远比清单上的条目重要得多。

sentences.en: And I think if people were to align much more on their values, they would have much more successful relationships the emotional pain of fearing change i have this thing the job the location the partner i'm going to enter or not enter this thing for the most part it's leaving i think we have this sort of loss aversion that we really evolve loss aversion it's just painful separating yourself in front of your friends it's embarrassing and how would you advise people to uh get past themselves with that loss aversion that fear of change oh my god am i going to yeah it's the hardest thing in the world uh starting over it's back to the zero to one thing it's a it's the mountain climbing thing you're not going to find your path to the top of the mountain in the first go around sometimes you go up there you get stuck and you come back down and the difference between all the successful people and the ones who are not is the ones who are successful wanted so badly they're willing to go back and start over again and again whether in their career or in their relationships or in anything else the most seriously you take yourself the unhappier you're going to be.
sentences.zh: 我认为如果人们能在价值观上达成更多共识，他们的关系会成功得多。关于害怕改变的情感痛苦，我有这种感觉，工作、地点、伴侣，我要进入或不进入这件事，大部分时候是离开，我认为我们有一种损失厌恶，我们进化出了损失厌恶，在朋友面前分开真的很痛苦，很尴尬，你会建议人们如何克服这种损失厌恶、这种对改变的恐惧？天哪，我会吗？是的，这是世界上最难的事情，重新开始，这又回到了从0到1的事情，就像爬山，你不可能第一次尝试就找到通往山顶的路径，有时你爬上去，被困住了，然后又退下来，所有成功人士与不成功人士的区别在于，成功的人渴望成功，以至于他们愿意一次又一次地回去重新开始，无论是在事业、人际关系还是其他任何事情上。你把自己看得越重，你就会越不快乐。

sentences.en: You learned how to take yourself less seriously?
sentences.zh: 你学会了如何不把自己看得那么重？

sentences.en: Well, fame doesn't help on that one because that is one of the traps of fame.
sentences.zh: 嗯，名气在这方面没什么帮助，因为这是名气的陷阱之一。

sentences.en: People are always talking about you. They have a certain view of you and you start believing that and then you take yourself seriously and then that limits your own actions.
sentences.zh: 人们总是在谈论你。他们对你有某种看法，你开始相信这些看法，然后你开始把自己当回事，这反而限制了你自己的行动。

sentences.en: You can't look like a fool anymore. You can't do new things anymore.
sentences.zh: 你不能再看起来像个傻瓜了。你不能再做新鲜事了。

sentences.en: You know, tomorrow I announce I'm a breakdancer, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果明天我宣布我要去跳街舞，对吧？

sentences.en: That's going to be met with a lot of scorn and ridicule.
sentences.zh: 那会招来很多嘲笑和讥讽。

sentences.en: But what if I want to be a breakdancer? I'd back you if you want to make that pivot.
sentences.zh: 但如果我想跳街舞呢？如果你想做出那种转变，我会支持你。

sentences.en: Yeah, the truth is if I want to be a break dancer, I'd be break dancing.
sentences.zh: 是的，事实是如果我想跳街舞，我就会去跳。

sentences.en: But, you know, like I'm starting a new company, zero to one again from scratch.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，就像我现在从零开始创办一家新公司一样。

sentences.en: Let's do it, you know, one more time. And not just going and raising a big VC fund or retiring or what have you.
sentences.zh: 让我们再做一次，你知道，再来一次。不仅仅是去筹集一大笔风投基金或者退休什么的。

sentences.en: But that's because I want to build the product.
sentences.zh: 但那是因为我想打造这个产品。

sentences.en: I want to see it exist. So I think that you constantly just have to force yourself.
sentences.zh: 我想看到它存在。所以我认为你必须不断地强迫自己。

sentences.en: You have to remind yourself. look deep down you're still the same chris you were when you were nine years old deep down you're still a kid uh you know you're still curious about the world you still have a lot of the same predilections and desires and wants you've got a nice veneer on it but one of the nice things when you have kids is you realize how much closer they are to you in personality and knowledge and know-how like i look at my son who's uh you know he's eight and uh that.
sentences.zh: 你必须提醒自己：看，在内心深处，你还是那个九岁时的Chris。在内心深处，你仍然是个孩子，你对世界依然充满好奇，你依然有很多相同的偏好、欲望和需求，你只是在外面涂了一层漂亮的漆。但当你有了孩子后，一件好事就是你意识到他们在个性和知识、见识上离你有多近，比如我看着我儿子，他才八岁，然后……

sentences.en: I just noticed like, wow, he's probably has 60 to 80% of my knowledge and development wisdom.
sentences.zh: 我注意到，哇，他可能已经拥有了我60%到80%的知识和发展智慧。

sentences.en: And he's a lot more freedom and he has a lot more spontaneity.
sentences.zh: 而且他更自由，更自发。

sentences.en: In some ways he's smarter. And there's not a big gap here left to close.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面他甚至更聪明。这里剩下的差距已经不大了。

sentences.en: This kid's going to be, you know, done very soon and caught up to me.
sentences.zh: 这孩子很快就会完成成长，赶上我了。

sentences.en: And so to the extent that I think I know better or that I'm somewhere or that I'm someone, it's just an illusion.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我认为自己懂得更多，或者认为自己是什么了不起的人物，那都只是幻觉。

sentences.en: It's just a belief. What's the lineage between that and taking yourself too seriously?
sentences.zh: 那只是一个信念。这和“不要把自己看得太重”之间有什么联系？

sentences.en: I shouldn't take myself too seriously because there's nothing here to take that seriously.
sentences.zh: 我不应该把自己看得太重，因为这里没什么值得那么严肃对待的。

sentences.en: And if I take myself too seriously, then I'm going to get trapped.
sentences.zh: 如果我把自己看得太重，我就会被困住。

sentences.en: I'm going to circumscribe myself again into a limited set of behaviors and outcomes that keep me from being free, keep me from being spontaneous, keep me from being happy.
sentences.zh: 我会再次把自己局限在一套有限的行为和结果中，这会让我无法自由，无法自发，无法快乐。

sentences.en: So it just goes back to the, you know, don't think about yourself too much.
sentences.zh: 所以这又回到了那句话，不要太在意自己。

sentences.en: There's a special type of pain in realizing that the advice that you need to hear right now is something that almost always you learned a long time ago.
sentences.zh: 意识到你现在需要听到的建议，几乎总是你很久以前就学过的东西，这是一种特别的痛苦。

sentences.en: And that, you know, you're basically sort of the same person you were as you were nine.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你基本上还是那个九岁时的自己。

sentences.en: And a lot of the time people ask questions like, what advice do you wish that you would give yourself 10 years ago?
sentences.zh: 很多时候人们会问这样的问题：你希望给十年前的自己什么建议？

sentences.en: People ask themselves that question.
sentences.zh: 人们会问自己这个问题。

sentences.en: Almost invariably, the advice that you would give yourself 10 years ago is still the advice that you need to hear today.
sentences.zh: 几乎无一例外，你给十年前自己的建议，依然是你今天需要听到的建议。

sentences.en: Absolutely. That's why I did that exercise of thinking back, you know, 10 years, 20 years, 30 years ago, what advice would I give myself for me is just be less emotional.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。这就是为什么我做了那个回顾练习，回想十年前、二十年前、三十年前，我会给自己什么建议？对我来说就是：少一点情绪化。

sentences.en: Don't take everything so seriously. Do the same things, but do them without all the emotional turbulence.
sentences.zh: 不要把一切都看得那么重。做同样的事情，但不要带着那些情绪波动去做。

sentences.en: And so that's the advice I'm giving myself going forward.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我给未来的自己的建议。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah. It's funny how we need that distance to be able to be a little bit more objective, to have a little bit more perspective.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，是的。有趣的是，我们需要那种距离感才能变得更客观，才能有更多的视角。

sentences.en: And it's almost a little bit of a trick, right?
sentences.zh: 这几乎像是一个小把戏，对吧？

sentences.en: Because typically when you do that, you say, what would you tell a friend that was going through this?
sentences.zh: 因为通常当你这样做时，你会问：你会告诉一个正在经历这些的朋友什么？

sentences.en: And then you try and turn the advice to the friend around onto yourself.
sentences.zh: 然后你试着把给朋友的建议转用到自己身上。

sentences.en: You always think, well, I'm not the friend.
sentences.zh: 你总是想，嗯，我不是那个朋友。

sentences.en: Okay, you, 10 years ago, there's enough distance in that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，十年前的你，这中间有足够的距离。

sentences.en: Oh, I actually am still that person. There's just a single line between that and me.
sentences.zh: 哦，我其实还是那个人。我和那时的我之间只有一线之隔。

sentences.en: And related to this story is I think understanding is way more important than discipline.
sentences.zh: 与这个故事相关的是，我认为理解远比纪律重要。

sentences.en: Now, Jocko would have a fit. But, you know, on physical things, discipline is important.
sentences.zh: 现在，Jocko可能会发火。但是，在身体层面，纪律很重要。

sentences.en: If I want to build a good body, I got to work out on a regular basis.
sentences.zh: 如果我想练出好身材，我必须定期锻炼。

sentences.en: But on mental things, I think understanding is way more important.
sentences.zh: 但在精神层面，我认为理解远比纪律重要。

sentences.en: Once you see the truth of something, you cannot unsee it.
sentences.zh: 一旦你看清了事物的真相，你就无法再假装看不见。

sentences.en: All of us have had experiences where we've seen a behavior in a person and then it just changes what we think about that person.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都经历过这样的时刻：看到一个人的某种行为，然后它彻底改变了我们对那个人的看法。

sentences.en: We no longer want to be friends with them or we deeply respect them if it was, you know, really good behavior that maybe was observed unintentionally. so when we when we really do see something clearly it changes our behavior immediately and that is far more efficient than trying to change your behavior through repetition could you give me an example um if you were let's say that you know you have a friend and that person turns out to be a thief you see that person stealing something you're done with them if you are you know the smoking lung cancer example is a good one right someone close to you or anytime someone close to you dies or you even hear about someone dying you hear about someone what's the first thing you do the first thing assuming that you weren't that close to them obviously you're close to them it's different but if you weren't that close to them but you know you hear about someone in your extended social circle dying you immediately start trying to distinguish yourself from them you're like oh well how old was this person you know did they Were they a smoker?
sentences.zh: 我们不再想和他们做朋友，或者如果那是非常好的行为，即使是无意中观察到的，我们也会深深地尊重他们。所以当我们真正清晰地看到某件事时，它会立即改变我们的行为，这比试图通过重复来改变行为要高效得多。你能给我举个例子吗？嗯，假设你有一个朋友，那个人后来被发现是个小偷，你看到那个人偷东西，你就和他们绝交了。如果你知道吸烟导致肺癌的例子，这是一个很好的例子，对吧？你身边的人，或者任何你身边的人去世，或者你甚至听说有人去世，你做的第一件事是什么？第一件事，假设你和他们不是特别亲近，当然如果你和他们很亲近，情况就不同了，但如果你和他们没那么亲近，但你听说你的社交圈里有人去世了，你立刻开始试图将自己与他们区分开来，你会想：哦，那个人多大年纪？他们是吸烟者吗？

sentences.en: Do they have an issue? Do I have that issue?
sentences.zh: 他们有什么问题吗？我有那个问题吗？

sentences.en: You immediately start comparing. And what you're doing there is you're sort of just trying to see if there's an overlap here.
sentences.zh: 你立刻开始比较。你在那里所做的，其实只是在试图看看是否有重叠。

sentences.en: But if you see the truth in something, if you're like, oh my God, this person was the same age as me and they died.
sentences.zh: 但如果你看清了事物的真相，如果你想：天哪，这个人和我同龄，他们却死了。

sentences.en: And that's starting to happen at my age where I'm starting to hear about extended circle people. just reminds you time is really short there's a truth there there's a truth there that you cannot reaction of distancing yourself the truth there that you cannot unsee uh you know or for example i think were you into bodybuilding or something back when i don't know just like bro lifting stuff okay bro lifting less of a skinny bitch yeah right but there probably was a point where you were uh being really aggro in the gym and you injured yourself many times right and each one of those was a deep understanding of don't go beyond this point right there was a truth there.
sentences.zh: 而且这开始发生在我这个年纪，我开始听到社交圈里的人去世的消息。这提醒你时间真的很短，这里有一个真相，这里有一个你无法忽视的真相，那种试图拉开距离的反应，这里有一个你无法假装看不见的真相。或者，举个例子，我记得你以前是不是练过健美之类的？我不知道，就是那种举铁之类的，好吧，举铁，少做点瘦弱的弱鸡，对吧？但可能有一个阶段，你在健身房里非常激进，你受了很多次伤，对吧？每一次受伤都是一次深刻的理解：不要超过这个点，这里有一个真相。

sentences.en: So again, when you see these things in such a way that you can't unsee them, that changes your behavior instantly.
sentences.zh: 所以再次强调，当你以一种无法再假装看不见的方式看到这些事情时，它会瞬间改变你的行为。

sentences.en: And I would argue that that introspection to find those truths is actually very useful.
sentences.zh: 我会说，那种寻找真相的内省实际上是非常有用的。

sentences.en: Is that a justification for more experimentation, exploration, experience in life, sort of trying to find serendipity because all of these experiences are going to teach you an inescapable lesson? you're going to do what you're going to do i mean your level of exploration i think is sort of up to you but life is always throwing truth back at you uh it's about whether you choose to see it whether you choose to acknowledge it uh even if it's painful truth is often painful right if it wasn't we'd all be seeing truth all the time reality is always reflecting truth that's all it is why would you not have accessed it already exactly uh you know all the all the philosophy that's out there for example uh it's almost trite like most people they look at philosophy like until they discover it for themselves and because because wisdom is the set of things that that cannot be transmitted if they could be transmitted you know we'd read the same five philosophy books it would all be done we'd all be wise you have to learn it for yourself it has to be rediscovered for yourself in your own context you have to have specific experiences that then allow you to generalize and see the truth in those things in such a way that you're not going to unsee them.
sentences.zh: 这是否证明了在生活中进行更多实验、探索、体验的合理性，比如试图寻找机缘巧合，因为所有这些经历都会给你上一堂不可避免的课？你会做你该做的事，我的意思是，你的探索程度取决于你自己，但生活总是不断地把真相抛向你，关键在于你是否选择去看，是否选择去承认，即使它是痛苦的。真相往往是痛苦的，对吧？如果不是这样，我们早就看清一切了。现实总是反映真相，仅此而已。为什么你还没有接触到它？完全正确。你知道，所有现存的哲学，举个例子，几乎都是陈词滥调，大多数人看待哲学，直到他们自己发现它，因为智慧是一套无法被传授的东西，如果它们能被传授，我们读同样的五本哲学书就够了，一切都完成了，我们都会变得睿智。你必须自己去学习，它必须在你自己的语境中被重新发现。你必须有特定的经历，然后这些经历让你能够概括并看清其中的真相，以至于你无法再假装看不见。

sentences.en: But each person is going to see them in a different way.
sentences.zh: 但每个人都会以不同的方式看到它们。

sentences.en: I can tell you that Socrates' story, and it's not going to resonate until there's something that other people desire that you realize you yourself don't want.
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉你苏格拉底的故事，但在你意识到别人渴望的东西而你自己并不想要之前，它不会引起共鸣。

sentences.en: And the moment that happens, then you'll see the truth in the general statement.
sentences.zh: 而那一刻发生时，你就会看清那个普遍陈述中的真相。

sentences.en: I want to just read you a two-minute essay that I wrote a couple of weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 我想读给你听一篇我几周前写的两分钟短文。

sentences.en: It's called Unteachable Lessons. I've been thinking about a special category of lesson, one which you cannot discover without experiencing it firsthand.
sentences.zh: 它叫《无法传授的课程》。我一直在思考一类特殊的课程，即那些不亲身经历就无法发现的课程。

sentences.en: There is a certain subset of advice that for some reason we all refuse to learn through instruction.
sentences.zh: 有一部分建议，出于某种原因，我们都拒绝通过指导来学习。

sentences.en: These are unteachable lessons. No matter how arduous or costly or effortful it is going to be for us to find out ourselves, we prefer to disregard the mountains of warnings from our elders, songs, literature, historical catastrophes, public scandals, and instead think some version of, yeah, that might be true for them, but not for me.
sentences.zh: 这些就是无法传授的课程。无论我们自己去发现它会有多么艰苦、昂贵或费力，我们都宁愿无视长辈、歌曲、文学、历史灾难、公共丑闻中堆积如山的警告，反而想出某种版本的：是的，那对他们来说可能是真的，但对我来说不是。

sentences.en: We decide to learn the hard lessons the hard way over and over again.
sentences.zh: 我们决定一次又一次地以艰难的方式学习那些艰难的课程。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, they all seem to be the big things, too.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，它们似乎都是些大事。

sentences.en: It's never new insights about how to put up level shelves or charmingly introduce yourself at a cocktail party.
sentences.zh: 从来都不是关于如何安装架子或在鸡尾酒会上如何迷人地介绍自己的新见解。

sentences.en: Instead, we spend most of our lives learning firsthand the most important lessons that the previous generations already warned us about.
sentences.zh: 相反，我们花了一辈子的大部分时间亲身学习那些前几代人已经警告过我们的最重要的课程。

sentences.en: Things like, money won't make you happy.
sentences.zh: 比如：金钱不会让你快乐。

sentences.en: Fame won't fix your self-worth. You don't love that pretty girl.
sentences.zh: 名声不会修复你的自我价值。你并不爱那个漂亮的女孩。

sentences.en: She's just hot and difficult to get. Nothing is as important as you think it is when you're thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 她只是性感且难以得到。当你思考某件事时，没有什么比你想象的那么重要。

sentences.en: You will regret working too much. worrying is not improving your performance all your fears are a waste of time you should see your parents more you'll be fine after the breakup and will be grateful that you did it it's perfectly okay to cut toxic people out of your life and even reading this list back I'm rolling my eyes at how fucking trite it is these are all basic bitch obvious insights that everybody has heard before but if they're so basic why does everyone so reliably fall prey to them throughout our lives and if they're so obvious Why do people who have recently become famous or wealthy or lost a parent or gone through a breakup start to proclaim these facts with the renewed grandiose ceremony of someone who's just gone through religious revelation?
sentences.zh: 你会后悔工作太多。担忧并不能提高你的表现，你所有的恐惧都是在浪费时间，你应该多看看你的父母，分手后你会好起来的，你会感激你这么做了，把有毒的人从你的生活中剔除是完全没问题的。即使读回这份清单，我也在翻白眼，觉得它太陈词滥调了，这些都是每个人都听过的基本常识，但如果它们如此基础，为什么每个人在生活中还是会如此可靠地沦为它们的牺牲品？如果它们如此显而易见，为什么那些刚出名、变富、失去亲人或经历分手的人，会开始以一种刚刚经历过宗教启示的人那种宏大的仪式感来宣扬这些事实？

sentences.en: It's also a very contentious list of points to say on the internet.
sentences.zh: 在互联网上说出这些观点也是一个非常有争议的清单。

sentences.en: If you interview a billionaire who says that all of his money didn't make him happy, or a movie star who said that her fame felt like a prison, the internet will tear them apart for being ungrateful and out of touch.
sentences.zh: 如果你采访一位亿万富翁，他说他所有的钱并没有让他快乐，或者一位电影明星说她的名声感觉像一座监狱，互联网会因为他们不知感恩和脱离现实而把他们撕碎。

sentences.en: So not only do we refuse to learn these lessons, we even refuse to hear the message from those warning us about them.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不仅拒绝学习这些课程，我们甚至拒绝听取那些警告我们的人传达的信息。

sentences.en: And even more than that, I think for every one of these, if I consider a bit deeper, I can recall a time, including right now, where I convinced myself that I am the exception to the rule.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，我认为对于其中每一条，如果我深入思考，我都能回想起某个时刻，包括现在，我曾说服自己我是规则的例外。

sentences.en: That my particular mental makeup or life situation or historical wounds or dreams for the future render me immune to these lessons being applicable.
sentences.zh: 我特殊的心理构成、生活状况、历史创伤或对未来的梦想，使我免于这些课程的适用。

sentences.en: No, no, no. My inner landscape would be solved by skirting around the most well-known wisdom of the ages.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不。我的内心世界可以通过绕过那些众所周知的古老智慧来解决。

sentences.en: No, no, no. I can thread this needle properly.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不。我可以正确地穿过这根针。

sentences.en: Watch me dance through the minefield and avoid all of the tripwires that everyone else kicks and then you kick one and you share a knowing look the kind that can only occur between two people who've been hurt in the exact same way and a voice in the back of your mind will say i told you so that's unteachable it's a good essay i think one of the reasons why these lessons are unteachable is because uh they're too broad they have to be applied in context a number of the ones that you let out contradict each other like spend more time with your parents and And, you know, don't work so hard.
sentences.zh: 看着我在雷区中跳舞，避开所有其他人踩到的绊线，然后你踩中了一个，你们分享了一个会意的眼神，那种只有两个以同样方式受过伤的人之间才会出现的眼神，你脑海深处的一个声音会说：我告诉过你吧。那是无法传授的，这是一篇好文章。我认为这些课程之所以无法传授，是因为它们太宽泛了，它们必须在语境中应用。你列出的许多课程相互矛盾，比如“多花时间陪父母”和“不要工作太努力”。

sentences.en: But, you know, at the same time, you do want to be successful, right?
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，与此同时，你确实想成功，对吧？

sentences.en: I think a lot of these lessons come from down on high from, as you said, like the famous movie star or the billionaire saying, oh, you don't need money to be happy.
sentences.zh: 我认为很多这些课程来自高处，正如你所说，比如著名的电影明星或亿万富翁说，哦，你不需要钱就能快乐。

sentences.en: It's like, well, okay, then give it up, bitch.
sentences.zh: 就像，好吧，那把它放弃吧，贱人。

sentences.en: So in reality, I think many of these contradict each other.
sentences.zh: 所以在现实中，我认为其中许多是相互矛盾的。

sentences.en: And it's like if you went to school and you just studied philosophy for four years, you would not know how to live life because you wouldn't know which philosophical doctrine to apply in which circumstance. you have to actually live life, go through all of the issues to figure out what it is that you want, what's the context in which some of these things apply and some of them don't.
sentences.zh: 这就好比如果你去学校，只学了四年哲学，你还是不知道如何生活，因为你不知道在什么情况下应用哪种哲学教条。你必须真正去生活，经历所有的问题，才能弄清楚你想要什么，哪些事情在什么语境下适用，哪些不适用。

sentences.en: Yes, you want to visit your parents more often, but you don't want to live with your parents and you don't want to necessarily see them every day or every weekend, depending on the parent.
sentences.zh: 是的，你想更频繁地探望父母，但你不想和父母住在一起，也不一定想每天或每个周末都见到他们，这取决于父母是谁。

sentences.en: You might not get along with one of them.
sentences.zh: 你可能和其中一位相处不来。

sentences.en: So I think it is highly contextual.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是高度依赖语境的。

sentences.en: That said, I would argue that once you figure it out for yourself, you can kind of carve these variations on these maxims that apply to you.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我会说一旦你自己弄明白了，你就可以雕琢出适用于你自己的这些格言的变体。

sentences.en: And then you'll have a specific experience that helps you remember it and actually execute on it.
sentences.zh: 然后你就会有一次具体的经历，帮助你记住它并真正去执行它。

sentences.en: And you can also phrase it in a way where it's not trite anymore.
sentences.zh: 你也可以用一种不再陈词滥调的方式来表达它。

sentences.en: So like my personal. Yeah. So a lot of my maxims and notes to self are carved in a way that they're modernized.
sentences.zh: 所以就像我个人的……是的。所以我很多格言和给自己的笔记都是以现代化的方式雕琢出来的。

sentences.en: They're saying something true, which might be trite if I didn't say it in a new way or in an interesting way that is more relevant to me today.
sentences.zh: 它们在说一些真实的事情，如果我不以一种新的方式，或者以一种对我今天更相关、更有趣的方式说出来，它可能就是陈词滥调。

sentences.en: There was a Nobel Prize winner who said something to the effect of, everything worth saying may have been said before, but given that nobody was listening, it must be said again.
sentences.zh: 有一位诺贝尔奖得主说过类似的话：所有值得说的话可能都被说过了，但鉴于没人听，它必须再说一遍。

sentences.en: Yeah, it has to be said again, has to be recontextualized for the modern age.
sentences.zh: 是的，它必须再说一遍，必须为现代重新语境化。

sentences.en: Things do change, technology changes, culture changes, people change.
sentences.zh: 事情确实在变，技术在变，文化在变，人也在变。

sentences.en: On that, I've heard you say, you talk about the difference between seeming wise and being wise, that you tried to appear smart as a kid by sort of- Still do. rote memorization masquerading as insight and wisdom and uh i i'd certainly feel that you know a lot of the show for me i think has been was and still is a redemption arc from this you know decade of my life where i completely suppressed any intellectual curiosity it's like okay i'll be a professional party boy for 10 years stand on the front door of a nightclub and give out vip wristbands and have access to all of the pretty girls or you know the cool parties or whatever it might be seems like it worked out okay it did in some ways i mean it's not fun it's it was look it was a good way to spend my 20s but to sort of come back above put your head above water two degrees one of which was a master's and then this like just shut down any of that learn i mean i did that while i was at uni while i was at uni i was running the events so it was actually a decade and a half uh Uh...
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，我听你说过，你谈到了看起来睿智和真正睿智之间的区别，你小时候试图通过某种方式显得聪明——现在依然如此。死记硬背伪装成洞察力和智慧，我当然感觉到了，你知道，对我来说，这个节目的很多内容，我想曾经是，现在依然是一个救赎弧线，来自我生命中那十年，我完全压抑了任何求知欲，就像，好吧，我做十年的专业派对男孩，站在夜店前门，分发VIP腕带，接触所有漂亮的女孩，或者你知道，酷派对什么的，看起来还行。在某些方面确实如此，我的意思是，这并不有趣，这是度过20岁的好方法，但要从那种状态中恢复过来，把头探出水面，两个学位，其中一个是硕士，然后这就像关闭了任何学习的欲望，我的意思是，我在大学时就这么做了，我在大学时负责组织活动，所以实际上是十五年……

sentences.en: I think there was a big redemption arc within this show.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个节目中有一个巨大的救赎弧线。

sentences.en: And I constantly have to kind of wipe the slime off me of this sense that I need to prove myself.
sentences.zh: 我必须不断地擦掉我身上那种需要证明自己的粘液。

sentences.en: And so much of it, it's why it really resonates with me.
sentences.zh: 这其中有很多原因，这就是为什么它真的能引起我的共鸣。

sentences.en: When you're memorizing things, it indicates that you don't understand them or that sort of, yeah, rote memorization and regurgitation masquerading as wisdom.
sentences.zh: 当你死记硬背时，这表明你不理解它们，或者说，是的，死记硬背和鹦鹉学舌伪装成智慧。

sentences.en: Because people use fluency as a proxy for truthfulness and insight.
sentences.zh: 因为人们把流利度当作真实性和洞察力的代理指标。

sentences.en: They use the complexity of your language and your communication.
sentences.zh: 他们利用你语言和沟通的复杂性。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's a lot of jargon out there.
sentences.zh: 是的，外面有很多行话。

sentences.en: I think it's the mark of a charlatan to explain a simple thing in a complex way.
sentences.zh: 我认为用复杂的方式解释简单的事情是江湖骗子的标志。

sentences.en: And so when you see people using very complicated language to explain simple things, they're either trying to impress you and obfuscate or they don't understand it themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以当你看到人们用非常复杂的语言来解释简单的事情时，他们要么是想给你留下深刻印象并混淆视听，要么是他们自己也不懂。

sentences.en: But there's an allure in that though. You know, this was one of the things I had to do when I went to therapy.
sentences.zh: 但这其中有一种诱惑。你知道，这是我去治疗时必须做的事情之一。

sentences.en: It's kind of an interesting, I think I've talked about this before.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，我想我以前谈过这个。

sentences.en: I needed to turn off podcast, Chris, when I stepped into therapy because most of the time that I spend one-on-one in a deep conversation that's undistracted throughout the week, I'd trained myself over, you know, when I started doing it, 700 episodes now, 900 and whatever.
sentences.zh: 当我走进治疗室时，我需要关掉“播客Chris”，因为大多数时候我花在一对一的深度对话中，整周都没有分心，我已经训练了自己，你知道，当我开始做的时候，现在已经700集了，900多集了。

sentences.en: And I knew what I could do to say to this therapist, some, you know, to just sort of veer off a little and create some nice story, put a bow on it, push it across the table and watch your eyes light up a little bit, like a little grin or a self-deprecating joke or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我知道我可以对这个治疗师说什么，你知道，稍微偏离一下，编造一些漂亮的故事，给它打个结，推到桌子对面，看着你的眼睛亮起来，比如一个小小的咧嘴笑或自嘲的笑话什么的。

sentences.en: I'm like, you're not here. You're performing.
sentences.zh: 我在想，你不在那儿。你在表演。

sentences.en: You're doing this. You're doing the Chris Williamson thing with the sort of jazz hands.
sentences.zh: 你在做这个。你在做那个带着爵士手势的Chris Williamson。

sentences.en: So I have my own version. Okay. Tell me.
sentences.zh: 所以我也有我自己的版本。好吧。告诉我。

sentences.en: Okay. So you have podcast, Chris. I have podcast guests in the ball.
sentences.zh: 好吧。所以你有播客Chris。我有播客嘉宾在球里。

sentences.en: Precisely. So very often I'll think of something.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。所以很多时候我会想到一些事情。

sentences.en: I'll have some, what I think is an insight and I want to tweet it or write it down.
sentences.zh: 我会有些我认为是洞察力的东西，我想发推特或写下来。

sentences.en: But in my mind, I'm talking about it on a podcast.
sentences.zh: 但在我的脑海里，我是在播客上谈论它。

sentences.en: That's kind of how my mind registers it.
sentences.zh: 这大概就是我的大脑记录信息的方式。

sentences.en: And for a while, I thought this was a bad thing and I tried to eradicate Podcast Naval.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，我觉得这很糟糕，还试图根除“播客Naval”这个形象。

sentences.en: And then I just realized that's just how it comes out.
sentences.zh: 后来我意识到，这就是我表达的方式。

sentences.en: So I might as well just be okay with it.
sentences.zh: 所以我最好还是接受它。

sentences.zh: 那么，你知道我为什么上这个播客吗？

sentences.en: No. You know, I haven't done a proper formal interview straight up top, whatever, 10, 20 podcasts in a long time.
sentences.zh: 不知道。你知道，我已经很久没有做过那种正儿八经的面对面采访了，大概有10到20个播客那么久吧。

sentences.en: Since Rogan, maybe? Probably since Rogan.
sentences.zh: 是从Rogan那次之后吗？大概是吧。

sentences.en: Yep. Yeah, I went out at the top, right?
sentences.zh: 没错。我是以巅峰状态退出的，对吧？

sentences.en: That was the theory. Yeah, but still at the top.
sentences.zh: 理论上是这样。是的，确实是在巅峰。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, I know. And then, you know, I've done some stuff with Tim, Tim Ferriss, a good friend, but that's been more co-hosting.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我知道。后来，我和好朋友Tim Ferriss做了一些节目，但那更多是联合主持。

sentences.en: I haven't been a guest. And then I did one or two random things where I just stumbled into a thing where there was a reason, but it wasn't like this.
sentences.zh: 我没当过嘉宾。后来我还做过一两件随性的事，那是为了某种原因，但和这次不一样。

sentences.en: And I reached out to you for this one, right?

sentences.zh: 有很多播客邀请我，我都没答应。但我联系了你。

sentences.en: I did not answer them. I reached out to you.
sentences.zh: 原因很有趣。因为当我在脑海里的“播客库”中播放播客时，不知为何，对面坐的总是你。

sentences.en: And the reason is a really funny one. It's because when I am playing podcasts in the vault in my head, for some reason you're on the other side.
sentences.zh: 我不知道为什么。我真的不知道为什么。

sentences.en: And I don't know why. I literally don't know why.
sentences.zh: 并不是说我看了你多少播客。

sentences.en: It's not like I've even seen many of your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 我想我只是零星看过一些片段。

sentences.en: I think I've seen some snippets here and there.
sentences.zh: 但不知何故，你就是我脑海里那个播客里的那个人。

sentences.en: But for some reason, you were the guy in the podcast, in podcast in the vault.
sentences.zh: 所以我心想，好吧，那我就去录一次吧。

sentences.en: And so I was like, oh, I might as well just do it.
sentences.zh: 所以我联系了你。我在想这会不会结束那个循环，还是会进一步加深它。

sentences.en: So I reached out to you. I wonder if this will close that loop or further entrench it.
sentences.zh: 我在想你现在是不是把情况搞得更糟了，你现在不仅有了梦境，还有了现实加梦境。

sentences.en: I wonder if you've made it way worse now and you're just going to have, well, first off, it was a dream and now it's reality plus a dream.
sentences.zh: 心想‘该死，我摆脱不了他了’。是的，我拒绝了很多人，我说我不再做播客了。

sentences.en: And fuck, I can't get away from him. Yeah, there are enough people that I turned down where I said I'm just not doing podcasts.
sentences.zh: 对此我感到很抱歉。我得回去把那些播客补上。

sentences.en: I feel bad about that. I got to go back and do those podcasts.
sentences.zh: 但我可能已经让人厌烦了。我没什么新鲜事可说了。

sentences.en: But I probably wear out my welcome. I have nothing new to talk about.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道该说什么。好吧，我很感激你能来。

sentences.en: So I don't know what I'm going to say. Well, I appreciate you said on.
sentences.zh: Rogan那次节目，你知道，为了回馈你，我在开始这个节目之前，心里有个“五巨头”嘉宾名单，分别是Jordan Peterson、Sam Harris、School of Life的Alain DeBaton，还有你和Rogan，那就是我心目中的“九头蛇”阵容。我知道，我想有人在Rogan之后问过你，或者是在推特上，甚至可能是在Rogan节目里说过，你说你不喜欢说同样的话，至少不喜欢用同样的方式说。

sentences.en: Rogan and this was something you know to kind of pay it back to you uh I had a five-headed Mount Rushmore of guests before I started this show and it was Jordan Peterson Sam Harris Alain DeBaton from the School of Life you and Rogan and that was my uh hydra of a Mount Rushmore and uh I knew I think someone had asked you at some point maybe it was a tweet or something after Rogan or maybe even said it on Rogan where you said I don't like to say the same thing twice at least not in the same way.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢续集。是的，没错。

sentences.en: I don't like sequels. Yeah. Yeah. And I really, really respected that.
sentences.zh: 我真的非常非常尊重这一点。

sentences.en: You know, that was 2019. You said it was eight or nine years ago.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那是2019年的事了。你说那是八九年前的事了。

sentences.en: It wasn't as long ago as you might think.
sentences.zh: 其实没你想的那么久。

sentences.en: I have a terrible memory. Yeah, yeah. You're right, 2019, right before COVID.
sentences.zh: 我记性很差。是的，没错，2019年，就在新冠疫情之前。

sentences.en: Yes. And I really appreciated that because there is something, the content game, you can continue to sort of, I'm sure I'll have said many things today that the audience will have already heard.
sentences.zh: 是的。我真的很感激这一点，因为内容行业确实存在一种现象，我敢肯定今天我会说很多听众已经听过的话。

sentences.en: But caring enough about having novel insights, or at least having a new perspective on similar insights. say, oh, well, you know, in the space of six years since you were on Joe, a lot of these that I'm coming at them.
sentences.zh: 但要在意是否有新颖的见解，或者至少对相似的见解有新的视角。比如，‘好吧，在你上Joe节目后的这六年里，我有很多新的看法。’

sentences.en: Actually, the first thing I said to you today, like, I'm not convinced that I actually fully agree with that thing that I used to say, which is cool, right?
sentences.zh: 其实，今天我对你说的第一句话就是，我并不确定我完全同意我过去说的那些话，这很酷，对吧？

sentences.en: That's you showing that the position that you put in the ground previously is not a tether.
sentences.zh: 这说明你之前设定的立场并不是一种束缚。

sentences.en: It's not you being held to it anymore. Well, I think the reason why I wanted to be on this is because for some reason, I have the impression that you engage in conversations. and I like conversations.
sentences.zh: 你不再被它所困。嗯，我想我之所以想参加这个节目，是因为不知何故，我印象中你是一个会进行对话的人，而我喜欢对话。

sentences.en: I don't like interviews. This is why I was doing my last startup air chat, which is all about conversations.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢采访。这就是我做上一个创业项目Air Chat的原因，它全是关于对话的。

sentences.en: And conversations to me are more genuine.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，对话更真诚。

sentences.en: They're more authentic. There's a give and take.
sentences.zh: 它们更真实。有来有往。

sentences.en: There's a back and forth. There's a genuine curiosity.
sentences.zh: 有互动。有真诚的好奇心。

sentences.en: It's not to say the other podcasters don't do it.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说其他播客主做不到。

sentences.en: They absolutely do do it. But for some reason in my mind, I had you as a guy that I would actually have a conversation with.
sentences.zh: 他们绝对做得到。但不知为何，在我心里，你就是那个我会真正与之对话的人。

sentences.en: And sure enough, you just read me your essay, which I don't think anybody else would really do, right?
sentences.zh: 果然，你刚才给我读了你的文章，我想没几个人会真的这么做，对吧？

sentences.en: That implies it's a give and take. There's a genuine curiosity.
sentences.zh: 这意味着这是一种互动。有一种真诚的好奇心。

sentences.en: And I think that's useful because then certain inexplicit knowledge that I had will be surfaced for myself.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很有用，因为这样一来，我内心某些未被表达的知识就会浮现出来。

sentences.en: And I think that's helpful. Well, you're seeing, you know, to kind of break the fourth wall a bit, you're seeing very much of some of the gateway drug insights that you had that you just don't get to choose.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很有帮助。嗯，你正在看到，为了打破一点“第四面墙”，你正在看到一些你曾经拥有的“入门级”见解，而你没得选。

sentences.en: I'm aware that you kind of have an anti-guru sentiment in you, like a very strong, like, don't listen to me.
sentences.zh: 我知道你内心有一种反导师的情绪，非常强烈，就像是‘别听我的’。

sentences.en: I don't know what I'm doing. That's a trap.
sentences.zh: ‘我不知道自己在做什么。’那是个陷阱。

sentences.en: No, guru is a trap. Do not follow me. Do not bow to me. do not do any of the other things to me.
sentences.zh: 不，导师是个陷阱。不要追随我。不要向我鞠躬。不要对我做任何其他类似的事情。

sentences.en: But if you see resonance in another person, and I think this is what we're all trying to find, you know, people can complain about the mountains of content creation that happens and maybe rightly so.
sentences.zh: 但如果你在另一个人身上看到了共鸣，我想这就是我们都在努力寻找的东西。你知道，人们可以抱怨现在泛滥的内容创作，也许确实应该抱怨。

sentences.en: But if you're able to find someone and you see in them a little bit of you, maybe not even much of you, but like, oh, that bit of them, their self-esteem or the way they look at relationships or what they want to do, the kind of life they want or the level of peace of mind that they want to have or whatever it might be.
sentences.zh: 但如果你能找到一个人，并在他们身上看到一点点自己的影子，哪怕只有一点点，比如，‘哦，他们那一点，他们的自尊心，或者他们看待关系的方式，或者他们想做什么，他们想要的生活，或者他们想要拥有的那种内心平静，等等。’

sentences.en: If you find in somebody else a little bit of that, it's kind of like what you're saying before.
sentences.zh: 如果你在别人身上找到了那一点点东西，就像你之前说的。

sentences.en: You can no longer be unconvinced of that.
sentences.zh: 你就再也无法否定它了。

sentences.en: And it steps in and becomes a part of you.
sentences.zh: 它会介入并成为你的一部分。

sentences.en: And yeah, you're maybe seeing reflected back to you some, you know, this sort of percolated, very meandering insight from however long ago that something's happened.
sentences.zh: 是的，你可能正在看到某种反射回来的东西，某种很久以前就酝酿的、非常漫无目的的见解。

sentences.en: And maybe in, you know, five years time you'll be like you know that thing that you said about the lessons and then i don't know it's cool that's like synthesis right it's this sort of blending of the reason i spend a lot of time in san francisco is because it's a gravitational attractor for the smartest people in the world and despite all the many problems the city had because it's mismanaged beyond belief it does just seem to pull in the young smart creative people not just the ones who are building technology but they're exploring every facet of life and they're weird and sometimes it's repulsive and it's bizarre but you talk to these people and you just see a very intelligent person coming at life in a completely different way putting it through the combinatorics of human dna which are uncountable and giving you a weird perspective that can twist your mind around and to do that you always have to be learning you you have you can't be the guru mentality If I'm with somebody and they're listening to every word I say and hanging on it, that's not interesting for me.
sentences.zh: 也许五年后你会说，‘你知道你当时说的关于那些教训的事……’，我不知道，这很酷，这就是综合，对吧？这就是融合。我花很多时间在旧金山的原因是，它对世界上最聪明的人有一种引力吸引，尽管这座城市有许多问题，因为它管理得极其糟糕，但它似乎确实吸引了年轻、聪明、有创造力的人，不仅仅是那些搞技术的人，他们还在探索生活的方方面面，他们很古怪，有时甚至让人反感，很离奇，但你和这些人交谈，你会看到一个非常聪明的人以完全不同的方式对待生活，将其放入人类DNA的组合中，这些组合是数不胜数的，并给你一个奇怪的视角，可以扭转你的思维。要做到这一点，你必须始终保持学习，你不能有导师心态。如果我和某人在一起，他们听我说的每一个字，并对此深信不疑，那对我来说没意思。

sentences.en: I'm not going to learn anything. I want people who are intelligent. who will say something back that is a little different and I may not agree with it, but it's going to leave a mark.
sentences.zh: 我学不到任何东西。我想要那些聪明的人，他们会回敬一些不同的东西，我可能不同意，但它会留下印记。

sentences.en: It's going to leave an impression. And it's going to leave an impression to the extent that both that they are correct and that I choose to listen.
sentences.zh: 它会留下印象。而且这种印象的程度取决于他们是否正确，以及我是否选择倾听。

sentences.en: And I'll choose to listen if I don't view myself as higher status or smarter than them.
sentences.zh: 如果我不认为自己比他们地位更高或更聪明，我就会选择倾听。

sentences.en: The flip side of that is I'm not really impressed by high status people.
sentences.zh: 反过来说，我并不太会被高地位的人打动。

sentences.en: Like I don't just because- Has that always been the case?
sentences.zh: 就像我不会仅仅因为……一直都是这样吗？

In fact, most of my friends who have gone on to become very famous or successful, the more famous successful they've been the less i spend time with them partially because they get surrounded by an army of sycophants which gets hard to break through uh and because i don't want anything from them and i don't and i don't like that i don't like these situations in which transactional relationships are implied that can be a gift though to people who are of that because the higher that they climb up that hierarchy the fewer and fewer people don't want anything from them so in that way yeah but what happens even better friend right but they get they get surrounded by people who do want things from them and are so good at pretending they don't that it's just not worth my time to try and break out from that group um so it does get lonely at the top so to speak but it's also by choice because you know it's champagne problem yeah you can be your own best friend too i am my own best friend actually so i really do enjoy spending time with myself yeah the smartest people aren't interested in appearing smart and don't care what you think is yeah i mean a lot of life is not giving a shit you know a lot of the best things in life come out of that does this mean you're just sort of talking about that rote memorization masquerading as wisdom and insight thing which i think perhaps almost certainly uh podcasts like this will have contributed to you know you hear a uh an alanda button who's you know like a painter with words very simple, very sort of unpretentious.
sentences.zh: 差不多。事实上，我大多数变得非常出名或成功的朋友，他们越出名、越成功，我花在他们身上的时间就越少，部分原因是他们被一群阿谀奉承的人包围，很难突破，而且因为我不求他们什么，我不喜欢这种隐含交易关系的情况。但对于那些人来说，这可能是一种礼物，因为他们爬得越高，不想从他们那里得到什么的人就越少，所以从这个角度看，是的。但更糟糕的是，他们被那些确实想从他们那里得到东西的人包围，而且这些人非常擅长假装他们不想，以至于我不觉得值得花时间去突破那个群体。所以，所谓的“高处不胜寒”确实存在，但这也是一种选择，因为你知道，这是“香槟问题”。是的，你可以成为自己最好的朋友。我确实是我自己最好的朋友，我真的很享受独处的时间。是的，最聪明的人对表现得聪明不感兴趣，也不在乎你怎么想。是的，我的意思是，生活很大一部分就是“不在乎”。你知道，生活中很多最好的事情都源于此。这是否意味着你只是在谈论那种伪装成智慧和洞察力的死记硬背？我想这也许几乎可以肯定，像这样的播客会对此有所贡献。你知道，你听到像Alain DeBaton这样的人，他就像一个用文字作画的人，非常简单，非常不装腔作势。

sentences.en: But if you're intellectually curious, you only see the production of his thoughts.
sentences.zh: 但如果你有求知欲，你只会看到他思想的产出。

sentences.en: You don't necessarily see the work that's gone into the thoughts behind.
sentences.zh: 你不一定能看到这些思想背后所付出的努力。

sentences.en: So you confuse the presentation of them for the insight.
sentences.zh: 所以你把它们的呈现误认为是洞察力。

sentences.en: Does that make sense? Of course. Yeah. A lot of my stuff is more polished.
sentences.zh: 这有道理吗？当然。是的。我的很多东西更精致。

sentences.en: Like one of the funny things. Yeah. One of the funny things that right before this podcast was, I thought, maybe I should go back and read my old tweets to sort of remember what I said and I can articulate it well.
sentences.zh: 就像一件有趣的事情。是的。在这个播客之前，有趣的事情之一是，我想，也许我应该回去读读我以前的推文，以便记住我说过的话，这样我能表达得更好。

sentences.en: Then I realized that's just performance.
sentences.zh: 然后我意识到那只是表演。

sentences.en: I would just be memorizing my whole stuff to perform.
sentences.zh: 我只是在背诵我自己的东西来表演。

sentences.en: Oh, well, that's an extra special level of hell that you've descended into.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧，那是你坠入的另一个特殊层级的地狱。

sentences.en: Exactly. I wrote memorizing me to be more me.
sentences.zh: 没错。死记硬背我自己，为了变得更像我自己。

sentences.en: Bingo. And to live up to some expectation or some famous personality that I now have to become, some straitjacket that I have to put on.
sentences.zh: 宾果。为了达到某种期望，或者为了维持我现在拥有的某种名人形象，某种我必须穿上的紧身衣。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm having to live up to in private the things that I perform.
sentences.zh: 是的，我不得不在私下里去活出我所表演出来的那些东西。

sentences.en: That's right. So of course, pretty quickly, I saw through that.
sentences.zh: 没错。所以很快我就看穿了这一点。

sentences.en: You know, it's nonsense. And it also constrains my time and it's just work.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很荒谬。而且它限制了我的时间，这纯粹是工作。

sentences.en: I think that's, you know, your meditation practice at work there, that mindfulness gap to be like, huh?
sentences.zh: 我想这就是你的冥想练习在起作用，那种正念的间隙，让你觉得，‘嗯？’

sentences.en: Yeah. There's that thing again. Exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的。那东西又来了。没错。

sentences.en: Exactly. So it's not about changing your thoughts.
sentences.zh: 没错。所以这与改变你的想法无关。

sentences.en: It's not about fixing your thoughts. It's not about changing yourself.
sentences.zh: 这与修正你的想法无关。这与改变你自己无关。

sentences.en: It's just about being observant of yourself so that you can then, it'll automatically change.
sentences.zh: 这只是关于观察你自己，这样你就可以……它会自动改变。

sentences.en: Whatever change needs to happen will happen.
sentences.zh: 任何需要发生的改变都会发生。

sentences.en: You trying to change yourself is very circular.
sentences.zh: 你试图改变自己是非常循环的。

sentences.en: The mind trying to change the mind, the mind doesn't like wrestling with itself.
sentences.zh: 大脑试图改变大脑，大脑不喜欢与自己搏斗。

sentences.en: I don't think it gets you anywhere. You've spent a lot of time either creating wealth or thinking about how to create wealth.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这能让你达到任何地方。你花了很多时间在创造财富或思考如何创造财富上。

sentences.en: What have you learned are the best places to spend wealth?
sentences.zh: 你学到了哪些是花钱最好的地方？

sentences.en: To spend wealth? Yeah, yeah. How you spend this time creating this wealth, accumulating.
sentences.zh: 花钱？是的，是的。你花时间创造这些财富，积累财富。

sentences.en: What are the best ways for you to put it back out?
sentences.zh: 你把钱重新投入出去的最好方式是什么？

sentences.en: I actually think Elon had this one figured out, which is he plowed his own money back into his own businesses to go and do bigger and better things for humanity. um so what i would like to you know you could give it to non-profits but a lot of non-profits are grifty or it's people who didn't earn it trying to spend it or they don't have tight feedback loops on having a good effect so One of the things I want to do as an aside is I want to create a little school for young physicists, but that's my non-profit.
sentences.zh: 我实际上认为Elon想通了这一点，那就是他把自己的钱重新投入到自己的企业中，去为人类做更大更好的事情。所以我想说的是，你可以把它捐给非营利组织，但很多非营利组织是骗人的，或者是那些没赚过钱的人试图去花钱，或者他们在产生良好效果方面没有紧密的反馈循环。所以，顺便说一句，我想做的一件事是为年轻的物理学家建立一所小学校，这就是我的非营利事业。

sentences.en: For young physicists? Yeah, that's my non-profit-y thing.
sentences.zh: 为年轻的物理学家？是的，这就是我做非营利的事情。

sentences.en: And I've actually underwritten media and some physics stuff.
sentences.zh: 我实际上已经资助了媒体和一些物理学项目。

sentences.en: I don't like to talk about it. I don't talk about whatever so-called philanthropy because I think that makes it less real.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢谈论它。我不谈论任何所谓的慈善事业，因为我认为这让它变得不那么真实。

sentences.en: That makes it more status-oriented. It makes it less philanthropic.
sentences.zh: 这让它变得更以地位为导向。这让它变得不那么慈善了。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly. Look at how charitable my charity is.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。‘看看我的慈善事业有多慈善。’

sentences.en: And then people also come hunting for money, so there's all that disease.
sentences.zh: 然后人们也会来寻求资金，所以所有这些弊病都随之而来。

sentences.en: I don't believe in giving to schools they have enough money.
sentences.zh: 我不相信给学校捐款，他们有足够的钱。

sentences.en: Ivy Leagues have enough money and they don't know how to spend it.
sentences.zh: 常春藤盟校有足够的钱，而且他们不知道怎么花。

sentences.en: So I think the best use of money is I think a good business creates a product for people that they voluntarily buy and they get value out of.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为金钱最好的用途是，我认为一家好的企业为人们创造了他们自愿购买并从中获得价值的产品。

sentences.en: So in that sense, I think Steve Jobs and Elon and entrepreneurs like that have created a lot of value for the world.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，我认为Steve Jobs和Elon以及像这样的企业家为世界创造了巨大的价值。

sentences.en: So one of the things I can do is I can take my own money and I can invest it in myself to go and build the next great thing that I think needs to exist.
sentences.zh: 所以我能做的一件事是，我可以拿我自己的钱，投资我自己，去构建我认为需要存在的下一个伟大的东西。

sentences.en: And that's basically what I'm doing right now.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是我现在正在做的事情。

sentences.en: I'm doing a new business. I'm self-funding it.
sentences.zh: 我正在做一个新的业务。我正在自筹资金。

sentences.en: I'm applying a lot of money into it. I'm going to build something that I think is beautiful that I want to see exist.
sentences.zh: 我投入了很多钱。我要构建一些我认为很美、我希望看到它存在的东西。

sentences.en: I really want to see it exist. Have you spoken about this yet or is it still dark mode?
sentences.zh: 我真的很想看到它存在。你谈论过这个吗，还是仍然处于保密模式？

sentences.en: It's so early. Maybe I'll show it to you in a few months.
sentences.zh: 还太早了。也许几个月后我会给你看。

sentences.en: Hopefully six months.
sentences.zh: 希望是六个月后。

sentences.en: And I'm excited about it. And that's a good use of money.
sentences.zh: 我很兴奋。这是一个很好的用钱方式。

sentences.en: What about the worst places to spend wealth?
sentences.zh: 那花钱最糟糕的地方是什么？

If it flies, floats or fornicates. very nice way to change the final f very impressive that's the way i heard it okay i'm pretty sure it's fox but yeah yeah yeah i think that was uh maybe it was uh felix dennis okay who who had that quote yeah he said if it flies floats or fornick gets rented i think the last one was a little too it's wrong that he didn't have a family didn't have kids so you know he missed the big one um but yeah there are lots of bad ways to spend money uh i i believe in investment you know i don't believe in consumption uh yes you can you're born with a short housing position you close that out you got yourself a nice house um get yourself some help to free up your time so you're not doing uh things that other people can do better um treat people well you know always overpay and expect the best uh pay them like they're the best and then expect the best but overall i think a good use of money is to take risks and build things and do things that other people can't do align it with your own unique talents so you can keep delivering to the world i'm not going to sit idle i'm not going to retire that's a that's a waste of whatever time i have left on this earth and if i'm doing something i enjoy then i'm already in perpetual retirement because work is just a set of things you want to do that that you have to do that you don't want to do.
sentences.zh: 那句老话怎么说来着？如果它会飞、会浮或会交配……把最后一个f换掉的方式很好，令人印象深刻。我听到的就是那样。好吧，我很确定是“fox”，但是的，是的，我想那是Felix Dennis，他有那句名言。是的，他说如果它会飞、会浮或会交配，就租吧。我想最后一个词有点太……他没有家庭，没有孩子，所以他错过了最重要的一点。但确实，花钱的坏方式有很多。我相信投资，我不相信消费。是的，你出生时处于住房短缺的状态，你解决了这个问题，给自己买了一套好房子。给自己找些帮手来腾出时间，这样你就不用做别人能做得更好的事情。善待他人，你知道，总是多付钱并期待最好的结果。像对待最好的人一样对待他们，然后期待最好的结果。但总的来说，我认为金钱最好的用途是承担风险，构建事物，做别人做不到的事情。把它与你独特的才能结合起来，这样你就可以继续为世界做出贡献。我不会坐以待毙，我不会退休，那是在浪费我在这地球上剩下的任何时间。如果我正在做我喜欢的事情，那么我就已经处于永久退休状态了，因为工作只是一系列你必须做但你不想做的事情。

sentences.en: So if you want to do it, it's not work. And so there are things that I want to do don't feel like work.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想做，那就不叫工作。所以有些我想做的事情感觉不像工作。

sentences.en: I can put money behind them and I can use that to instantiate them into reality.
sentences.zh: 我可以把钱投入到它们后面，并利用它将它们实例化到现实中。

sentences.en: And I don't want to say make the world a better place because that's too trite, but it's more just create a product that I'm proud of that wouldn't exist otherwise that other people will get tremendous value.
sentences.zh: 我不想说“让世界变得更美好”，因为那太陈词滥调了，但这更多是创造一个我引以为豪的产品，如果不是这样就不会存在，而其他人会从中获得巨大的价值。

sentences.en: And it's been enabled through wealth because you're able to take a level of risk that you wouldn't have been able to otherwise.
sentences.zh: 而且它是通过财富实现的，因为你能够承担你原本无法承担的风险水平。

sentences.en: Exactly. Yeah. Wealth gives you freedom.
sentences.zh: 没错。是的。财富给你自由。

sentences.en: It gives you freedom to explore more options.
sentences.zh: 它给你探索更多选择的自由。

sentences.en: And in my case, it gives me freedom to start businesses without having to ask other people for permission or to warp my vision based on their desires to make a return or how they think money should be made.
sentences.zh: 在我的情况下，它给了我创办企业的自由，而不必请求别人的许可，也不必为了获得回报或按照他们认为金钱应该如何赚取的方式来扭曲我的愿景。

sentences.en: Is there anything that you'd add to the How to Get Rich thread?
sentences.zh: 关于“如何致富”的推文系列，你有什么要补充的吗？

sentences.en: Is there anything where you thought, fuck, like just one, if I could go in and edit and add one more in or...
sentences.zh: 有没有什么地方你觉得，‘该死，如果我能进去编辑并再加一条……’

sentences.en: Oh, there's like 10,000 things. I could talk about that topic forever, to be honest.
sentences.zh: 哦，有成千上万的事情。老实说，我可以永远谈论那个话题。

sentences.en: Like that thread was so short and it was so limited and it was so like, you know, crafted in a sense, although I wrote it very spontaneously.
sentences.zh: 那个系列太短了，太有限了，而且在某种意义上是精心制作的，尽管我写得非常随性。

sentences.en: It left so much on the cutting room floor that I could just talk about that topic for days, but it's all contextual.
sentences.zh: 它留下了太多被剪掉的内容，我可以谈论那个话题好几天，但这一切都是情境化的。

sentences.en: Business is very, very, very contextual.
sentences.zh: 商业是非常、非常、非常情境化的。

sentences.en: You have to look at the particular business and understand what's being done and why it's being done and how it's being done, and then you can tear it apart and then reassemble it properly.
sentences.zh: 你必须观察特定的业务，了解正在做什么，为什么这样做，以及它是如何完成的，然后你才能把它拆解，再适当地重新组装。

sentences.en: And I like to think that that is actually where I have specific knowledge and expertise.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢认为这实际上是我拥有特定知识和专业知识的地方。

sentences.en: My specific knowledge and expertise is not in happiness, not in philosophy.
sentences.zh: 我的特定知识和专业知识不在于幸福，不在于哲学。

sentences.en: Yes, my life is very hacked to be very unique, but I don't think that's where my specific knowledge is.

sentences.zh: 它是坚固的，锁定在那里的。所以在播客上，我可以更深入地卸载这些话题。例如，我们可以谈论你喜欢的任何业务，但它必须在情境中，它必须是真实的，它必须是一个实际的问题，然后我们可以解决它。我真的很喜欢那个启发式方法：如果你不得不死记硬背某事，那是因为你不理解。你不理解它。没错，如果你不得不死记硬背某事，那是因为你不理解它；如果你理解某事，你就不需要死记硬背。是的，再次强调……我尝试做的很多事情，这种救赎弧线，如果我听起来很聪明，那就像是聪明，对吧？

sentences.zh: 品味是关键。而理解、判断、品味，这些都来自于拥有真正的问题，然后解决它们，然后找到共性。

sentences.en: What is philosophy? Everyone, you live long enough, you'll be a philosopher.
sentences.zh: 什么是哲学？每个人，你活得够久，你就会成为哲学家。

sentences.en: Philosophy is just when you find the hidden generalizable truths among the specific experiences that you've had in life.
sentences.zh: 哲学只是当你在你生活中经历的特定经验中找到隐藏的普遍真理时。

sentences.en: And then you know how to navigate future specific experiences based on some heuristics and you create a philosophy around that.
sentences.zh: 然后你知道如何根据一些启发式方法来导航未来的特定经验，并围绕它创造一种哲学。

sentences.en: Any subject pursued deeply enough will eventually lead to philosophy.
sentences.zh: 任何被深入追求的主题最终都会导向哲学。

sentences.en: Mastery in anything, literally anything. will lead you to being a philosopher.
sentences.zh: 在任何事情上的精通，字面上任何事情，都会引导你成为哲学家。

sentences.en: You just have to stick with it long enough and generalize the truths back out.
sentences.zh: 你只需要坚持得足够久，并将真理概括出来。

sentences.en: And these are universal truths. It's back to the unity and variety.
sentences.zh: 这些是普遍真理。这回到了统一与多样性。

sentences.en: You can find unity in anything if you go deep enough.
sentences.zh: 如果你深入挖掘，你可以在任何事物中找到统一性。

sentences.en: And that's why the trite stuff, unfortunately, sort of keeps coming back around.

sentences.en: You're like, well, look, this is cliche for kind of a reason.

sentences.en: It's cliche for reasons. But, you know, sometimes you learn new things.

sentences.en: Sometimes you do figure out new things too.
sentences.zh: 有时你也确实会弄清楚新东西。

sentences.en: Even in philosophy, for example, science has advanced. as science has advanced, it's actually expanded our boundaries of philosophy.
sentences.zh: 即使在哲学中，例如，科学已经进步。随着科学的进步，它实际上扩展了我们的哲学边界。

sentences.en: When we used to think that the earth was the center of the universe, you would actually have a different philosophical outlook than when you think the universe is vast and we're infinitesimally small.
sentences.zh: 当我们曾经认为地球是宇宙中心时，你实际上会有一种与认为宇宙浩瀚且我们微不足道时不同的哲学观。

sentences.en: It will give you a different philosophical outlook.
sentences.zh: 它会给你一种不同的哲学观。

sentences.en: The same way if you think that the nature is driven by angels and demons and gods versus if there are laws of physics that are computable and understandable, that will lead you to a different philosophical outlook.
sentences.zh: 同样，如果你认为自然是由天使、恶魔和神驱动的，而不是有可计算和可理解的物理定律，那将引导你走向不同的哲学观。

sentences.en: If you think that knowledge is something that is passed down from above and through generations versus something that is created on the fly and then tested against reality, that will lead you to a different philosophical outlook.
sentences.zh: 如果你认为知识是代代相传的，而不是在飞行中创造并根据现实进行测试的，那将引导你走向不同的哲学观。

sentences.en: If you think humans are created by God as opposed to humans evolved from some unicellular organism, yeah, it still doesn't solve the original problem.

sentences.en: Who created that? But at least it takes you further back.
sentences.zh: 谁创造了那个？但至少它把你带得更远了。

sentences.en: Even sim theory is an attempt at reformulating philosophy based on what we know about computers, even though it leads to a lot of the same conclusions as creator.

sentences.en: But it is at least philosophy that is informed by technology and by science.

sentences.en: So even philosophy can make progress.
