sentences.en: Religion solves coordination problems. ethnicity solves coordination problems historically.
sentences.zh: 宗教解决协调问题。种族在历史上解决协调问题。

sentences.en: And when you break down those coordination systems too fast and don't replace them with anything else, you get societal breakdown.
sentences.zh: 当你过快地打破这些协调系统而不替换它们时，你就会得到社会崩溃。

sentences.en: So you can have very malfunctioning societies, you know, go to Japan versus go to any Western city and you can see the difference between a culture that's working and a culture that's not.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以有非常功能失调的社会，你知道，去日本对比去任何西方城市，你可以看到一个运作良好的文化和一个不运作的文化之间的区别。

sentences.en: So I think that that's like a broader set of things that I've changed my mind on a fair bit.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这就像我改变主意的一系列更广泛的事情。

sentences.en: I used to be much more laissez-faire on that stuff.
sentences.zh: 我过去在那些事情上要自由放任得多。

sentences.en: Let's put it that way. What else? I mean, on child raising, I've gotten a lot looser.
sentences.zh: 我们就这么说吧。还有什么？我的意思是，在抚养孩子方面，我变得宽松多了。

sentences.en: You know, I'm still not like completely laissez-faire, but I'm much more realized like kids are going to be kids and you kind of let them do their thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我仍然不是完全自由放任，但我更多地意识到孩子就是孩子，你让他们做他们自己的事情。

sentences.en: You've gotten the... Debate with them. Is it Taleb that has the ascending levels of like anarchism versus conservatism?
sentences.zh: 你已经……和他们辩论。是Taleb有那种无政府主义与保守主义的上升水平吗？

sentences.en: Is that his insight? Like at the local level, I'm this.
sentences.zh: 那是他的洞察力吗？就像在地方层面，我是这个。

sentences.en: It seems like you've gone the other way.
sentences.zh: 看起来你走的是另一条路。

sentences.en: It's like at the child level, I'm an anarchist.
sentences.zh: 就像在孩子层面，我是无政府主义者。

sentences.en: At the societal level, I'm a conservative.
sentences.zh: 在社会层面，我是保守主义者。

sentences.en: Yeah, no, he was quoting somebody else, some brothers, I forget which ones, but he was making the point eloquently as he often does uh that uh at you know at the family local level he's a communist at the family level you're communist uh at maybe the the extended family level you're a socialist at the local level you know you're kind of a a democrat and so on until at the federal level you're libertarian right so you've done it the other way you know being a libertarian with the kids and you're being a religious conservative and societal no that's that's that's a that's a funny way of looking at it i don't know if the scale is that yeah yeah that's simple um what else have i changed my mind on i mean i think the modern ai is really cool i think it's but i think these are natural language computers um they're starting to show evidence of kind of uh reasoning at some levels but i don't think they do creativity.
sentences.zh: 是的，不，他是在引用别人的话，一些兄弟，我忘了是哪几个，但他像往常一样雄辩地指出了这一点，在家庭地方层面，他是共产主义者，在家庭层面你是共产主义者，在也许大家庭层面你是社会主义者，在地方层面你是民主党人，以此类推，直到联邦层面你是自由意志主义者，对吧？所以你反其道而行之，你知道，对孩子是自由意志主义者，而对社会是宗教保守主义者，不，那是一种有趣的看待方式，我不知道规模是否是那样。是的，那很简单。我还在什么事情上改变了主意？我的意思是，我认为现代人工智能真的很酷，我认为它是……但我认为这些是自然语言计算机，它们开始显示出某种层面的推理证据，但我不认为它们有创造力。

sentences.en: I think modern AI. So just on that, one of my favorite takes is from Dworkash Patel, and he says, if you gave any human on the planet 0.001% of the consumption that LLM has, any LLM, they would have come up with thousands of new ideas.
sentences.zh: 我认为现代人工智能。所以就这一点而言，我最喜欢的观点之一来自Dworkash Patel，他说，如果你给地球上的任何人类LLM所拥有的0.001%的消费，任何LLM，他们会想出成千上万的新想法。

sentences.en: Give me one new idea. One fundamental new idea.
sentences.zh: 给我一个新想法。一个根本性的新想法。

sentences.en: That's been generated. Yeah, like I'm big into poetry.
sentences.zh: 那是被生成的。是的，就像我非常喜欢诗歌。

sentences.en: Every poem ever written by an LM is garbage.
sentences.zh: LM写的每一首诗都是垃圾。

sentences.en: I think even their fiction writing is terrible.
sentences.zh: 我认为即使是他们的小说写作也很糟糕。

sentences.en: Even the new GPT-405, with all due respect to Sam and crew, I think they're terrible writers.
sentences.zh: 即使是新的GPT-405，对Sam和团队表示敬意，我认为他们是糟糕的作家。

sentences.en: I find them really bad at summarizing. They're really good at extrapolating paperwork.
sentences.zh: 我发现他们真的很不擅长总结。他们非常擅长推断文书工作。

sentences.en: They're very bad at actually distilling the essence of something and what's important.
sentences.zh: 他们非常不擅长真正提炼事物的本质和什么是重要的。

sentences.en: They don't have an opinions or a point of view, but they're still unbelievably powerful breakthroughs.
sentences.zh: 他们没有观点或视角，但它们仍然是令人难以置信的强大突破。

sentences.en: They solve search. They solve natural language computing.
sentences.zh: 它们解决了搜索。它们解决了自然语言计算。

sentences.en: They make English a programming language.
sentences.zh: 它们使英语成为一种编程语言。

sentences.en: They solve driving. They solve simple coding and backup coding.
sentences.zh: 它们解决了驾驶。它们解决了简单的编码和备份编码。

sentences.en: They solve translation. They solve transcription.
sentences.zh: 它们解决了翻译。它们解决了转录。

sentences.en: They are a fundamental breakthrough in computing.
sentences.zh: 它们是计算领域的一个根本性突破。

sentences.en: It is a different way to program a computer rather than you explicitly speak its language and write the code and then run the data through it.
sentences.zh: 这是一种编程计算机的不同方式，而不是你明确地说它的语言并编写代码，然后让数据通过它。

sentences.en: You just run enough data through it until it figures out how to write the program.
sentences.zh: 你只是让足够多的数据通过它，直到它弄清楚如何编写程序。

sentences.en: That's huge. But are they AGI? Not yet. And I don't see a direct path from here to there.
sentences.zh: 这太大了。但它们是AGI吗？还没有。我没有看到从这里到那里的直接路径。

sentences.en: Maybe we'll have to solve a few more problems before that happens.
sentences.zh: 也许在发生这种情况之前，我们必须解决更多问题。

sentences.en: And I think ASI is a fantasy. I don't think there's any such thing.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为ASI是一个幻想。我不认为有这样的东西。

sentences.en: Artificial super intelligence, where it has some kind of intelligence that humans can't fathom.
sentences.zh: 人工智能超级智能，它拥有某种人类无法理解的智能。

sentences.en: Okay. Yeah, it seems like, I don't know, if you're from the Bostrom camp or whatever.
sentences.zh: 好的。是的，看起来，我不知道，如果你来自Bostrom阵营或什么的。

sentences.en: No, I'm not an AI doomer. I think that's such a flawed line of reasoning.
sentences.zh: 不，我不是AI末日论者。我认为那是一个如此有缺陷的推理路线。

sentences.en: But let's say that, you know, you came out of the lesswrong.com, like Slate Star Codec world, and there was this sort of lineage from computers and AI gets more powerful, more powerful, more powerful and then you end up AGI, ASI.
sentences.zh: 但假设，你知道，你来自lesswrong.com，像Slate Star Codec世界，并且有一种从计算机和AI变得更强大、更强大、更强大，然后你最终得到AGI、ASI的血统。

sentences.en: And it seems like LLMs have been this sort of orthogonal move from that, which are you saying you don't believe they are a step on that?
sentences.zh: 而且看起来LLM是那种正交的举动，你是说你不相信它们是那一步吗？

sentences.en: It's kind of a little bit of an additional branch.
sentences.zh: 这有点像一个额外的分支。

sentences.en: I think Stephen Wolfram puts it better. It's a different form of intelligence.
sentences.zh: 我认为Stephen Wolfram说得更好。这是一种不同形式的智能。

sentences.en: It's like if you see a jaguar in the jungle, it has a different form of intelligence and you're like a plant has a form of intelligence, how it can like photosynthesize and grow.
sentences.zh: 就像如果你在丛林中看到一只美洲虎，它有一种不同形式的智能，就像植物有一种智能，它如何进行光合作用和生长。

sentences.en: It's a different form of intelligence. It's not an intelligence again, And like love or like happiness is overloaded word that means many things to many people.
sentences.zh: 这是一种不同形式的智能。它不是智能，再次，就像爱或幸福是过载的词，对许多人来说意味着许多事情。

sentences.en: But by my definition, where, you know, the true test is you get what you want out of life.
sentences.zh: 但根据我的定义，你知道，真正的测试是你从生活中得到你想要的。

sentences.en: It doesn't even have a life. It doesn't even want anything.
sentences.zh: 它甚至没有生命。它甚至不想要任何东西。

sentences.en: It's a different thing. I do think it's unbelievably useful.
sentences.zh: 这是另一回事。我确实认为它非常有用。

sentences.en: I'm glad that it exists. You don't see it much yet in large scale production systems replacing humans because this tendency to hallucinate.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴它存在。你还没有在大规模生产系统中看到它取代人类，因为这种幻觉倾向。

sentences.en: So you can't put it into anything mission critical.
sentences.zh: 所以你不能把它放入任何任务关键型的东西中。

sentences.en: Confidently wrong one time out of 10. Correct.
sentences.zh: 十分之一的时候自信地错了。正确。

sentences.en: And it doesn't even know when it's wrong. and maybe they'll get that one out of 10 down to one out of 100 but you'll kind of always want human oversight for critical critical things i i always feel so bitter yeah it's i'm petty sometimes my less equanimous version of me is petty and i always want to like teach it a lesson if it gets something wrong like how the fuck like no you were so confident i'm treating it but i'm anthropomorphizing it doesn't have a point of view and they are going to get a lot better and they might get to the point where the error rates are so low that you can put them into certain bounded problems like self-driving i think will be solved completely because it's a bounded problem.
sentences.zh: 而且它甚至不知道自己什么时候错了。也许他们会把十分之一的错误率降到百分之一，但你总是希望有人类监督关键的关键事情。我总是感到如此痛苦，是的，我有时很小气，我不那么平静的版本很小气，如果它弄错了，我总是想教训它，就像‘该死，不，你太自信了’，我正在对待它，但我正在拟人化它，它没有观点，而且它们会变得好得多，它们可能会达到错误率如此之低的地步，以至于你可以将它们放入某些有界问题中，比如自动驾驶，我认为会被完全解决，因为它是一个有界问题。

sentences.en: Cars don't go off-road and drive through houses and stuff like that, right?
sentences.zh: 汽车不会越野并穿过房子之类的，对吧？

sentences.en: And same way, certain kinds of coding. The creative side of coding, I think, doesn't go away.
sentences.zh: 同样，某些类型的编码。编码的创造性方面，我认为不会消失。

sentences.en: I think, if anything, programmers get even more leveraged and more powerful, and rather than computing and replacing programmers, programmers use AI to replace everybody else.
sentences.zh: 我认为，如果有的话，程序员会变得更加杠杆化和强大，而不是计算和取代程序员，程序员使用AI来取代其他人。

sentences.en: On Tesla versus Waymo, would you bet on software or hardware for self-driving?
sentences.zh: 关于Tesla对比Waymo，你会押注软件还是硬件进行自动驾驶？

sentences.en: Yeah, so I think Tesla's in the stronger, longer-term position, but it's hard to argue with what's working right now.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以我认为Tesla处于更强、更长期的位置，但很难反驳现在正在工作的东西。

sentences.en: And Waymo is working right now. So I would not underestimate them because there's a learning curve that you go through when you actually deploy something.
sentences.zh: 而Waymo现在正在工作。所以我不会低估他们，因为当你真正部署某事时，你会经历一个学习曲线。

sentences.en: And Waymo is way ahead in that regard. But Tesla's camera only approach, if it works, is a superior.
sentences.zh: 而Waymo在这方面遥遥领先。但Tesla的纯摄像头方法，如果它有效，是更优越的。

sentences.en: It's much more scalable. And Tesla knows how to print cars, right?
sentences.zh: 它更具可扩展性。而且Tesla知道如何打印汽车，对吧？

sentences.en: They can just mass manufacture cars. But I think they'll both be around.
sentences.zh: 他们可以大规模制造汽车。但我认为它们都会存在。

sentences.en: They'll both be fine. It's everybody else who doesn't have a self-driving vehicle that's screwed.
sentences.zh: 它们都会没事的。是其他没有自动驾驶汽车的人倒霉了。

sentences.en: You mentioned kids there and you had a tweet that said, I'm not convinced that declining fertility needs to be proactively fought.
sentences.zh: 你提到了孩子，你有一条推文说，我不相信人口下降需要被主动对抗。

sentences.en: I forgot that one. You're going to have to, I dug deep.
sentences.zh: 我忘了那条了。你必须……我挖得很深。

sentences.en: Why? Well, I mean, think back, like, what was it, 30 years ago, 20 years ago, everybody was saying overpopulation of the earth is going to be a problem, Malthusian ending, we're going to have too many people, and all of a sudden we're going to have too few people.
sentences.zh: 为什么？好吧，我的意思是，回想一下，就像，30年前，20年前，每个人都在说地球人口过剩将是一个问题，马尔萨斯终结，我们将有太多人，突然之间我们将有太少人。

sentences.en: So part of it is just the doomerism meme is always alive and well, right?
sentences.zh: 所以部分原因只是末日论模因总是活着并且很好，对吧？

sentences.en: It just gets repackaged. Yeah, we're running out of oil, we have too much oil, right?
sentences.zh: 它只是被重新包装了。是的，我们的石油快用完了，我们有太多的石油，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, it's like the world is cooling, the world is warming.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像世界在变冷，世界在变暖。

sentences.en: Like there's always something to scream about the world is ending.
sentences.zh: 就像总有什么东西可以尖叫世界末日。

sentences.en: There's no progress in technology. AI is going to blow up the world, right?
sentences.zh: 技术没有进步。AI要炸毁世界，对吧？

sentences.en: So people tend to overdo in both directions.
sentences.zh: 所以人们倾向于在两个方向上做得过火。

sentences.en: Now, what is the actual fertility problem, right?
sentences.zh: 现在，实际的生育问题是什么，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, people are having less kids. Are they having less kids because there's a disease?
sentences.zh: 好吧，人们生的孩子少了。他们生的孩子少了是因为有疾病吗？

sentences.en: Was there a virus? Did they lose their fertility?
sentences.zh: 有病毒吗？他们失去了生育能力吗？

sentences.en: Is it microplastics in the testicles, right?
sentences.zh: 是睾丸里的微塑料吗，对吧？

sentences.en: No, it's people are having less kids because they're choosing to have less kids, right?
sentences.zh: 不，人们生的孩子少了是因为他们选择少生孩子，对吧？

sentences.en: Women have gotten emancipation, independence in the workforce and they're making more money.
sentences.zh: 女性获得了解放，在劳动力市场中获得了独立，她们赚了更多的钱。

sentences.en: People don't need kids as an insurance policy.
sentences.zh: 人们不需要孩子作为保险单。

sentences.en: So they have less kids. Maybe they're living hedonistic lives.
sentences.zh: 所以他们生的孩子少了。也许他们过着享乐主义的生活。

sentences.en: God bless them, right? They want to have more fun.
sentences.zh: 上帝保佑他们，对吧？他们想玩得更开心。

sentences.en: They want to have less kids. I don't see the act of choosing to have less kids as a problem.
sentences.zh: 他们想少生孩子。我不认为选择少生孩子是一个问题。

sentences.en: Okay. So let's move one level up. It's because of the retirees.
sentences.zh: 好的。所以让我们向上移动一个层次。这是因为退休人员。

sentences.en: It's because a large percentage of the population is essentially retiring at the guaranteed age of 65 or 70, thanks to social security.
sentences.zh: 这是因为很大一部分人口基本上在社会保障的保证年龄65或70岁退休。

sentences.en: And so they need other people to pay for it.
sentences.zh: 所以他们需要其他人来支付它。

sentences.en: They need more workers in the workforce.
sentences.zh: 他们需要劳动力中有更多的工人。

sentences.en: And if the workforce is shrinking, then you have a small number of people exactly who are supporting a large number of retirees.
sentences.zh: 如果劳动力在萎缩，那么你就有一小部分人正好在支持大量退休人员。

sentences.en: And in democracies, you can't take pensions away if the voters vote you out.
sentences.zh: 而在民主国家，如果选民把你选下去，你就不能取消养老金。

sentences.en: So this slowly strangled the economy. So what do you do?
sentences.zh: 所以这慢慢扼杀了经济。那你该怎么办？

sentences.en: Then you have a bunch of immigration and then the whole culture changes.
sentences.zh: 然后你会有大量的移民，然后整个文化就变了。

sentences.en: You end up in a low trust society and people start fighting over limited resources and how do you control which immigrants come in and how do you make sure that they're good taxpayers after they're in and so on.
sentences.zh: 你最终会进入一个低信任社会，人们开始为有限的资源而战，你如何控制哪些移民进来，你如何确保他们在进来后是好的纳税人，等等。

sentences.en: So you end up in kind of this trap where the low fertility rate is upstream of the downstream problems that are cultural and societal.
sentences.zh: 所以你最终陷入了这种陷阱，低生育率是文化和社会下游问题的上游。

sentences.en: But I'm not sure that you're going to solve that by making people have more kids.
sentences.zh: 但我并不确定你会通过让人们多生孩子来解决这个问题。

sentences.en: How are you going to meme them into having more kids?
sentences.zh: 你打算怎么让他们多生孩子？

sentences.en: And I'm not even sure it's necessarily a problem because keep in mind, you have more resources now.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不确定这一定是个问题，因为记住，你现在有更多的资源。

sentences.en: You have less of a burden. Now there's a flip side where every kid is a lottery ticket, not an invention.
sentences.zh: 你的负担更小了。现在每个孩子都是一张彩票，而不是发明。

sentences.en: So there's some benefit to having more kids, but you can't force it.
sentences.zh: 所以多生孩子有一些好处，但你不能强迫它。

sentences.en: I think it'll work itself out, right? The Scott Adams has this great law which calls the Adams law of slow-moving disasters.
sentences.zh: 我认为它会自行解决，对吧？Scott Adams有这个伟大的定律，称之为Adams缓慢移动灾难定律。

sentences.en: When disasters are very slow-moving, like peak oil or global warming or population collapse, and everyone can kind of see them coming, economics and society is a force to solve them because enough individual people has incentives to go solve them.
sentences.zh: 当灾难移动非常缓慢时，比如石油峰值或全球变暖或人口崩溃，每个人都能看到它们到来，经济和社会是一种解决它们的力量，因为足够多的个人有动力去解决它们。

sentences.en: So I don't know exactly how it gets solved, but I think it could get solved in various ways. one example could be you know maybe people retire later maybe AI and automation and robots take care of the older people Maybe we figure out how to have immigrants while still keeping a high-trust society.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道它究竟是如何解决的，但我认为它可以通过各种方式解决。一个例子可能是，你知道，也许人们退休得更晚，也许AI和自动化和机器人照顾老年人，也许我们弄清楚了如何在保持高信任社会的同时拥有移民。

sentences.en: We kind of put more rules around immigration that protects some of the high-trust benefits.
sentences.zh: 我们对移民施加更多规则，保护一些高信任利益。

sentences.en: Maybe we outsource more things. Maybe we just, you know, have more land and housing to go around.
sentences.zh: 也许我们外包更多事情。也许我们只是，你知道，有更多的土地和住房。

sentences.en: Believe me, if we were having too many kids, everybody would be complaining about how there's no housing and there's no land, right?
sentences.zh: 相信我，如果我们生了太多的孩子，每个人都会抱怨没有住房，没有土地，对吧？

sentences.en: So they'll always find something to care about.
sentences.zh: 所以他们总会找到关心的事情。

sentences.en: So I just don't view this as like a thing that any individual or government action is going to solve.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是不认为这是一个任何个人或政府行动都能解决的事情。

sentences.en: I think economics and incentives over time will solve it. and I'm not even convinced it's like that big of a problem.
sentences.zh: 我认为经济和激励机制随着时间的推移会解决它。我甚至不相信这是一个那么大的问题。

sentences.en: Is there anything that you do think is a sufficient?
sentences.zh: 有没有什么你确实认为是一个足够的？

sentences.en: It may be self-correcting too, which is that if there are too few kids in society and the returns to having kids literally might just go up.

sentences.en: You must brush your teeth, you know, cover your mouth when you cough, you know, clean up after yourself.
sentences.zh: 你必须刷牙，咳嗽时要遮住嘴，用完东西要收拾干净。

sentences.en: Don't touch that. Wash your hands after you do this. don't eat food off the floor, right?
sentences.zh: 别碰那个。做完这件事要洗手。别吃掉在地上的食物，对吧？

sentences.en: But all of these are subsumed under the germ theory of disease, right?
sentences.zh: 但所有这些规则其实都归纳在疾病细菌理论之下，对吧？

sentences.en: So if you instead go on YouTube and show them videos of germs, or if you have them look under a microscope at anything, they're like, ah.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你转而在 YouTube 上给他们看细菌的视频，或者让他们用显微镜观察任何东西，他们就会恍然大悟。

sentences.en: They can infer what's going on. Yeah, there's creepy crawlies everywhere and I got to watch out for them.
sentences.zh: 他们能推断出发生了什么。没错，到处都是肉眼看不见的小东西，我得小心提防它们。

sentences.en: And then, you know, you can talk about how, if you look at humans, like our real enemy are pathogens.
sentences.zh: 然后，你可以谈谈如果你观察人类，我们真正的敌人其实是病原体。

sentences.en: I think a lot of aging and disease are actually downstream of our competition with pathogens over time. to a point that people still don't fully appreciate.
sentences.zh: 我认为很多衰老和疾病实际上是我们长期与病原体竞争的后续结果，这一点人们至今仍未充分认识到。

sentences.en: There's a red queen hypothesis, which is that we undergo sexual selection to mix up our genes.
sentences.zh: 有一个“红皇后假说”，即我们通过有性生殖来打乱基因组合。

sentences.en: And so every 20 years, every generation mix up your genes.
sentences.zh: 所以每隔 20 年，每一代人都要重新混合基因。

sentences.en: But if you look at how bacteria and viruses mutate through just random mutations, their mix-up rate on their genes and evolution rate is roughly the same as ours, even though they go through thousands of generations those 20 years because they're not doing sexual selection.
sentences.zh: 但如果你观察细菌和病毒如何通过随机突变进行变异，它们的基因混合率和进化速度与我们大致相同，尽管它们在 20 年里经历了数千代，因为它们不进行有性生殖。

sentences.en: They're doing asexual replication mutation. their evolutionary rate is roughly equivalent to ours.
sentences.zh: 它们进行的是无性复制突变。它们的进化速度与我们大致相当。

sentences.en: So we're in a red queen race where we're both running at roughly the same speed using very different strategies.
sentences.zh: 所以我们处于一场“红皇后”竞赛中，双方都在以截然不同的策略以大致相同的速度奔跑。

sentences.en: But a lot of how we're involved is around pathogens.
sentences.zh: 但我们很多进化过程都是围绕病原体展开的。

sentences.en: Like our immune system is one of the most expensive things to run in the body.
sentences.zh: 比如我们的免疫系统是人体内运行成本最高的系统之一。

sentences.en: So much is about immune system optimization.
sentences.zh: 很多事情都与免疫系统优化有关。

sentences.en: That's about pathogens. Junk DNA in bacteria and CRISPR was discovered because in bacteria, their DNA is evolved to fight viruses.
sentences.zh: 这都是关于病原体的问题。细菌中的垃圾 DNA 和 CRISPR 的发现，是因为细菌的 DNA 进化出了对抗病毒的能力。

sentences.en: And the way it does that is by taking viral DNA and snipping it up every time there's a viral attack and storing it in their own DNA so they have a copy so they can recognize it next time it attacks and so on.
sentences.zh: 它的做法是：每次受到病毒攻击时，就截取病毒的 DNA 片段，并将其存储在自己的 DNA 中，这样它们就有了备份，下次病毒再攻击时就能识别出来，以此类推。

sentences.en: A lot of the population structure of species determines how long their lifespans are.
sentences.zh: 一个物种的种群结构在很大程度上决定了它们的寿命长短。

sentences.en: So if in a given species, there's a very high rate of infection, then you'll have these older members of the population are carrying diseases that will then infect the young.
sentences.zh: 如果某个物种的感染率很高，那么种群中那些年长的成员就会携带疾病，进而传染给幼体。

sentences.en: So it's important for that species to get rid of the old faster.
sentences.zh: 因此，对该物种而言，更快地淘汰年长者很重要。

sentences.en: So the higher the disease rate in a given population, the less long-lived the entire population.
sentences.zh: 所以，一个种群的疾病率越高，整个种群的寿命就越短。

sentences.en: So the older ones don't infect the younger ones.
sentences.zh: 这样年长的个体就不会传染给年轻的个体了。

sentences.en: That's a hypothesis. It's an interesting hypothesis. homeostasis within the human body how we're always returning to a given level of things like that's a that's a fundamental part of our makeup our temperature ph blood pressure and so on under homeostasis but if you if you engage in any kind of signaling like you take a peptide for example that's a signaling molecule you take a hormone externally the body will counteract it you take testosterone the body will counteract it will downregulate its own production very fast and the body releases its own hormones in pulses rather than steady state why is that well that's because bacteria and viruses can infect your body and trick your body they can take it over like toxoplasmosis does this rabies does this they take over macroscopic structure structural bodies and small bacteria and viruses would hack our bodies and literally take them over if we didn't have defense mechanisms and one of those defense mechanisms is homeostasis anytime you see something getting out of whack you immediately push back really hard on because like did i just get infected is something trying to take me over it's also why hormones get released in pulses at night rather than in steady state low levels because enemy bacteria can release toxins or the same signaling molecules in small quantities, but they can't pulse.
sentences.zh: 这只是一个假说。这是一个有趣的假说。人体内的稳态，即我们如何始终回归到某种基准水平，这是我们构成的一个基本部分，比如我们的体温、pH 值、血压等等，这些都处于稳态之下。但如果你进行任何形式的信号干预，比如你服用肽类，那是一种信号分子，或者你从外部摄入激素，身体就会进行抵消。你摄入睾酮，身体就会抵消它，并迅速下调自身的产量。而且身体是以脉冲方式而非稳态方式释放自身激素的，为什么呢？因为细菌和病毒会感染你的身体并欺骗它，它们可以接管你的身体，比如弓形虫病会这样做，狂犬病也会这样做。它们接管宏观结构，而微小的细菌和病毒会入侵我们的身体，如果我们没有防御机制，它们甚至会直接接管我们。其中一种防御机制就是稳态：每当你看到某项指标失控，你就会立即进行强力回击，因为你会想：“我是不是被感染了？有什么东西想接管我吗？”这也是为什么激素是在夜间以脉冲形式释放，而不是以稳定的低水平释放的原因，因为敌对细菌可以释放毒素或少量的相同信号分子，但它们无法同步脉冲。

sentences.en: They can't coordinate to pulse. So your body can coordinate to pulse as a macroscopic object, but microscopic objects can't coordinate to create the same pulses.
sentences.zh: 它们无法协调产生脉冲。所以你的身体作为一个宏观物体可以协调产生脉冲，但微观物体无法协调产生同样的脉冲。

sentences.en: Oh, that's cool. Yeah, so there's all, I mean, so you know that it's coming from you.
sentences.zh: 哦，那太酷了。没错，所以这一切，我的意思是，你知道这是源自你自身。

sentences.en: Is that why? Correct. You know it's endogenous rather than exogenous.
sentences.zh: 是因为这个吗？没错。你知道这是内源性的，而不是外源性的。

sentences.en: I never knew that. That's fascinating. And that's why we resist a lot of exogenous treatments and a lot of our medical treatments don't work.
sentences.zh: 我以前从不知道这一点。太迷人了。这就是为什么我们对许多外源性治疗产生抗性，而且我们很多医疗手段往往无效的原因。

sentences.en: Um, anyway, so this, these are, there's, there's a bunch more I could go on, but I think that a lot of, uh, you know, you, you see this in cancers where, uh, a lot of, uh, bacteria show up at the Epstein-Barr virus shows up in a lot of cancers.
sentences.zh: 嗯，总之，这些例子还有很多，我可以继续说下去，但我认为，你知道，你在癌症中也能看到这一点，很多细菌会出现，EB 病毒也会出现在许多癌症中。

sentences.en: And, um, you know, now it seems like the gut microbiome influences so many things.
sentences.zh: 而且，现在看来肠道微生物群影响着许多事情。

sentences.en: Basically, uh, bacteria and viruses are at the top of the food chain compared to us.
sentences.zh: 基本上，细菌和病毒在食物链顶端，远高于我们。

sentences.en: Like we are top of the well-known food chain, but bacteria viruses eat us.
sentences.zh: 我们虽然是已知食物链的顶端，但细菌和病毒会吃掉我们。

sentences.en: Fungus eats us. So these microscopic predators are our natural predators.
sentences.zh: 真菌也会吃掉我们。所以这些微观捕食者才是我们真正的天敌。

sentences.en: And so a lot of aging, societal structure, hygiene, religious strictures against pork, circumcision, all of these things, these are all designed to resist bacteria and viruses.
sentences.zh: 因此，许多关于衰老、社会结构、卫生习惯、宗教对猪肉的禁忌、割礼等等，所有这些设计都是为了抵御细菌和病毒。

sentences.en: So if you can teach children this philosophy at an early age, you shortcut all the debates.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你能从小教给孩子这种哲学，就能省去所有的争论。

sentences.en: How effective have you been at teaching that philosophy to children?
sentences.zh: 你在向孩子们传授这种哲学方面有多成功？

sentences.en: That one, I think I've been pretty effective.
sentences.zh: 那一点，我觉得我做得相当成功。

sentences.en: I've drilled that one at home. The one I haven't quite gotten around to yet as evolution.
sentences.zh: 我在家里反复灌输过这一点。我还没来得及讲的是进化论。

sentences.en: Like I'm starting to do little bits of that.
sentences.zh: 我开始做一点点这方面的引导了。

sentences.en: You know, like we came from monkeys. What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 比如我们是从猴子进化来的。那意味着什么？

sentences.en: I already got them thinking about some of the deeper questions.
sentences.zh: 我已经让他们开始思考一些更深层的问题了。

sentences.en: I did ask my, you know, young son, like, you know, can nothing exist?
sentences.zh: 我确实问过我年幼的儿子：“虚无可能存在吗？”

sentences.en: I thought that was a fun question. So I had to throw a fun question.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那是一个有趣的问题。所以我得抛出一个有趣的问题。

sentences.en: How old is he now? Like three? No, no, he's eight.
sentences.zh: 他现在多大了？三岁？不，不，他八岁了。

sentences.en: Oh, right. An eight-year-old and a six-year-old.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。一个八岁，一个六岁。

sentences.en: So I asked them both, like, can nothing exist?
sentences.zh: 所以我问了他们两个：“虚无可能存在吗？”

sentences.en: And they had pretty good answers, right?
sentences.zh: 他们给出的答案相当不错，对吧？

sentences.en: Another one we played with the other day was like, what is the matrix?
sentences.zh: 我们前几天玩的另一个游戏是：“什么是矩阵？”

sentences.en: Okay. You know, what is this? What is all this?
sentences.zh: 好吧。你知道，这是什么？这一切到底是什么？

sentences.en: And it's entertaining. It's just fun to talk about, right?
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。谈论这些问题本身就很有意思，对吧？

sentences.en: To talk about these questions with your kids.
sentences.zh: 和你的孩子们谈论这些问题。

sentences.en: I'm not saying that one is a good way of child raising.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说这是一种好的育儿方式。

sentences.en: It's not leading to any deeper learning.
sentences.zh: 这并不会带来什么更深层的学习。

sentences.en: Other than maybe just have them start or continue to question the basic structure of reality and not move past it so quickly.
sentences.zh: 除了可能让他们开始或继续质疑现实的基本结构，而不是那么快地跳过它。

sentences.en: Also to take joy. What's the meta lesson that's being taught there?
sentences.zh: 还有就是享受过程。这里传授的元课程是什么？

sentences.en: Dad spends time asking questions to which there are not necessarily an answer because there is something enjoyable in the process of learning and trying to decipher what's happening?
sentences.zh: 父亲花时间问一些未必有答案的问题，因为在学习和试图解读正在发生的事情的过程中，本身就有一种乐趣？

sentences.en: Possibly. Also, dad tries not too hard to teach people things.
sentences.zh: 有可能。还有，父亲尽量不去刻意教导人们什么。

sentences.en: I don't want to be didactic. He helps them to arrive at it.
sentences.zh: 我不想显得好为人师。他帮助他们自己得出结论。

sentences.en: He helps, yeah, correct. Dad is here to help you solve problems when you have problems and you constantly have problems.
sentences.zh: 他提供帮助，是的，没错。父亲在这里是为了在你遇到问题时帮你解决问题，而你总是在不断遇到问题。

sentences.en: So if you come to dad, dad can help explain to you how he would solve the problem.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你来找父亲，父亲可以帮你解释他会如何解决这个问题。

sentences.en: But most of the time, they don't want that.
sentences.zh: 但大多数时候，他们并不想要那个。

sentences.en: Agency, agency, agency. Most of the time, they just want me to solve the problem, right?
sentences.zh: 自主权，自主权，自主权。大多数时候，他们只是想让我直接把问题解决掉，对吧？

sentences.en: Right, okay, yeah. So sometimes it's have to play dumb.
sentences.zh: 没错，好吧，是的。所以有时候必须装傻。

sentences.en: It's like, why is my Wi-Fi not working on my computer?
sentences.zh: 就像，“为什么我的电脑连不上 Wi-Fi？”

sentences.en: I'm like, I don't know. Did you click on that thing?
sentences.zh: 我说：“我不知道。你点那个东西了吗？”

sentences.en: You've got like a rebellious sovereign child.
sentences.zh: 你有一个叛逆且独立的后代。

sentences.en: Sovereign as they may be, but sometimes they still need the...
sentences.zh: 尽管他们很独立，但有时他们仍然需要……

sentences.en: Yeah. So in addition to feeling loved and having high self-esteem, I think the most important trait that would be nice to not rob them of is agency.
sentences.zh: 是的。所以除了感受到爱和拥有高自尊之外，我认为最重要且不该剥夺他们的特质就是自主权。

sentences.en: I want them to preserve their agency. They're born naturally agentic and willful, but a lot of child raising can beat that out of them by essentially domesticating them.
sentences.zh: 我想让他们保持自主权。他们天生就有自主意识和意志力，但很多育儿方式会通过本质上的“驯化”把这些磨灭掉。

sentences.en: That's right. And I would rather have wild animals and wolves than have well-trained dogs because I'm not going to be around to take care of them.
sentences.zh: 没错。我宁愿要野兽和狼，也不要训练有素的狗，因为我不可能一直陪着照顾他们。

sentences.en: Yeah. So they're going to have to be able to look after themselves.
sentences.zh: 是的。所以他们必须能够照顾好自己。

sentences.en: Yeah, a friend of mine, Parsa on AirChat, he had a great saying.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的一个朋友，AirChat 上的 Parsa，他说过一句很棒的话。

sentences.en: He said he wants his children to be quick to learn and hard to kill.
sentences.zh: 他说他希望他的孩子们学得快，且不容易被干掉。

sentences.en: I thought that was pretty good. Yeah, that was cool.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那话说得真好。是的，那很酷。

sentences.en: I remember you saying, just thinking about sort of future and culture and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 我记得你说过，在思考未来、文化之类的事情时，

sentences.en: I remember you saying that the left had won the culture war and now they're just driving around shooting the survivors.
sentences.zh: 我记得你说过左派已经赢得了文化战争，现在他们只是在四处游荡，射杀幸存者。

sentences.en: After the last six months of change that we've seen and sort of where we're at at the moment, And what do you think the future of the culture wall looks like?
sentences.zh: 经历了过去六个月的种种变迁，以及我们目前所处的境地，你认为文化战争的未来会是什么样？

sentences.en: It's not over yet. They definitely won earlier rounds.
sentences.zh: 它还没有结束。他们确实赢得了早期的几轮较量。

sentences.en: They took over institutions. I think now it's much more of a fair fight where you have people like Elon, you know, kind of supporting.
sentences.zh: 他们接管了各种机构。我认为现在是一场更公平的博弈，因为有像Elon这样的人在提供支持。

sentences.en: So there's these different forces through history, right?
sentences.zh: 所以历史上一直存在着这些不同的力量，对吧？

sentences.en: Historians will argue about this. but there's a theory of the great man of history thing where it's like oh you have the einsteins you have the teslas you have the um the genghese khan's and the caesars right they determine the flow of history and then there's the other uh point of view that no there are these massive forces at play you know demographics and geography and so on and then the particular great man doesn't matter they just come and go napoleon doesn't matter they would have been somebody else uh the specific names are not important and because of kind of the leftist turn that our institutions took in the last few decades, they now only subscribe to the great forces theory of history, not the great man theory of history.
sentences.zh: 历史学家们会对此争论不休。但有一种“伟人史观”理论，认为像Einstein、Tesla、成吉思汗和凯撒大帝这样的人决定了历史的走向；而另一种观点则认为，不，是人口、地理等巨大的力量在起作用，特定的伟人并不重要，他们只是来来去去，Napoleon并不重要，换成别人也一样，具体的名字并不重要。由于过去几十年里我们的机构向左转，他们现在只认同“大力量史观”，而不认同“伟人史观”。

sentences.en: But I think now we're seeing the two play out where you're seeing Trump and Elon and other individuals rising up and saying, no, we resist.
sentences.zh: 但我认为现在我们看到了两者的博弈，你看到Trump、Elon和其他个人站出来说，不，我们要反抗。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's interesting. And I think that unfortunately, and so the battle between these collectivists and great forces versus individuals, it's as old as humanity itself.
sentences.zh: 是的，这很有趣。而且我认为不幸的是，这种集体主义、大力量与个人之间的斗争，和人类本身一样古老。

sentences.en: And it is fundamental to the species. We are not a completely individualistic species.
sentences.zh: 这是人类物种的根本属性。我们并不是一个完全个人主义的物种。

sentences.en: You know, no man is an island. A single person can't do anything by themselves.
sentences.zh: 你知道，没有人是一座孤岛。单凭个人是无法成就任何事情的。

sentences.en: But we're also not a Borg. We're not a beehive.
sentences.zh: 但我们也不是博格人（Borg）。我们不是蜂巢。

sentences.en: We're not an ant colony. We're not all just drones marching along.
sentences.zh: 我们不是蚁群。我们不是只会排队行进的工蜂。

sentences.en: So which is it? We're somewhere in the middle.
sentences.zh: 那么到底是哪一种呢？我们处于两者之间。

sentences.en: And the human race is always kind of bouncing between the two.
sentences.zh: 人类社会总是在这两者之间摇摆。

sentences.en: We like strong leaders. We like to be led.
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢强大的领导者。我们喜欢被领导。

sentences.en: We like to coordinate our forces and mass and do things.
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢协调我们的力量，集结起来做大事。

sentences.en: But at the same time, we're also all individuals and willing to break away. and willing to do our own thing.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，我们也是独立的个体，愿意脱离群体，愿意做自己的事情。

sentences.en: And everyone's always fighting to be a leader and there's always status games going on.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在争当领导者，地位之争永远存在。

sentences.en: So there's a pendulum that's always swinging back and forth.
sentences.zh: 所以总有一个钟摆在来回摆动。

sentences.en: And in modern economics, the way that manifests is between sort of Marxism and capitalism, right?
sentences.zh: 在现代经济学中，这种表现就是马克思主义与资本主义之间的博弈，对吧？

sentences.en: Marxism is like from each according to his ability to each according to his needs.
sentences.zh: 马克思主义主张“各尽所能，按需分配”。

sentences.en: We're all equal. There's a millennial project.
sentences.zh: 我们都是平等的。这是一个千禧年的愿景。

sentences.en: We're all going to be equal in the end. And don't try and stand out, but do what's good for everybody.
sentences.zh: 最终我们都会平等。不要试图脱颖而出，要为所有人谋福利。

sentences.en: And there's a religious aspect to it. And then the capitalist individualist is like, libertarian every man for himself you just each do what you want and it'll work out for the greater good that's adam smith you know the invisible hand of the market will feed you the baker should bake and the butcher should butcher and the candlestick maker should make candlesticks and it'll all work out each person does their best and they trade and so which is it which which which which theory is correct and i think there's always going to be a battle between the two and i think the interesting thing is what's going on there's a modern flavor to it which changes it the modern flavor is that the individual is getting more powerful because they're becoming more leverage.
sentences.zh: 这其中有一种宗教色彩。而资本主义个人主义者则主张自由意志，每个人为自己负责，各取所需，只要每个人都做自己想做的事，最终会实现更大的利益。这就是Adam Smith所说的，市场的“看不见的手”会供养你，面包师应该烤面包，屠夫应该卖肉，烛台制作者应该做烛台，一切都会顺其自然，每个人尽其所能进行交易。那么到底是哪一种理论正确呢？我认为这两者之间永远会有博弈。有趣的是，现代社会出现了一种新的风味，改变了这种博弈。这种现代风味在于，个人因为拥有了更多的杠杆，变得越来越强大。

sentences.en: So someone like an Elon Musk can have the leverage of tens of thousands of brilliant engineers and producers working for him.
sentences.zh: 所以像Elon Musk这样的人，可以拥有数以万计的杰出工程师和生产人员为他工作所带来的杠杆。

sentences.en: He can have factories of robots manufacturing things.
sentences.zh: 他可以拥有制造产品的机器人工厂。

sentences.en: He can have hundreds of billions of dollars of capital behind him, and he can project himself through media to hundreds of millions of people.
sentences.zh: 他身后可以有数千亿美元的资本，他可以通过媒体将自己的影响力投射到数亿人身上。

sentences.en: That is more power than any individual could have had historically.
sentences.zh: 这比历史上任何个人所能拥有的权力都要大。

sentences.en: So the great men of history are becoming greater.
sentences.zh: 所以历史上的“伟人”变得越来越伟大了。

sentences.en: That said, that same leverage is increasing the gap between the haves and have-nots.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，同样的杠杆作用也在扩大贫富差距。

sentences.en: So in the wealth game, more people are winning overall and the average is going up.
sentences.zh: 所以在财富游戏中，总体上有更多人赢了，平均水平在提高。

sentences.en: But in the status game, there are essentially more losers.
sentences.zh: 但在地位游戏中，本质上输家更多了。

sentences.en: There are more invisible men and women who are getting nothing out of life and have no leverage, relatively speaking.
sentences.zh: 有更多隐形的人，他们从生活中一无所获，相对而言没有任何杠杆。

sentences.en: Objectively speaking, they might be better off.
sentences.zh: 客观地说，他们的生活可能比以前更好。

sentences.en: They still have phones and they still have TVs.
sentences.zh: 他们依然有手机，依然有电视。

sentences.en: They're not absolutist creatures, they're relative creatures.
sentences.zh: 他们不是绝对主义的生物，而是相对主义的生物。

sentences.en: Correct. And so to the extent that we're relative creatures, there are more losers than winners.
sentences.zh: 没错。就我们是相对主义生物而言，输家确实比赢家多。

sentences.en: And in a democracy, those people will outnumber the winners and they will vote the winners down.
sentences.zh: 在民主制度下，这些人的人数会超过赢家，他们会投票否决赢家。

sentences.en: And so that's the battle that kind of goes on.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是正在进行的博弈。

sentences.en: And the democracy has gotten very broad.
sentences.zh: 而且民主的范围已经变得非常广泛。

sentences.en: And so one of my other quips is that it's not the right to vote that gives you power.
sentences.zh: 所以我另一个俏皮话是：并不是投票权赋予了你权力。

sentences.en: It's power that gives you the right to vote.
sentences.zh: 而是权力赋予了你投票权。

sentences.en: So we've confused the two. So what happened was, you know, voting started as a way for people who had power to divide up the power and not fight amongst themselves.
sentences.zh: 我们混淆了这两者。事情是这样的，投票最初是那些拥有权力的人为了分配权力、避免内部争斗而采取的一种方式。

sentences.en: The winners of the revolution, the winners of the war, the people in the House of Lords and the House of Commons, they divide up power amongst themselves. to say, hey, we have all the money, we have the power, we are the knights, we have the swords, we have the warriors, we could kill everybody, but we don't want to just fight each other all day long.
sentences.zh: 革命的胜利者、战争的胜利者、上议院和下议院的人，他们在自己之间分配权力，意思是：嘿，我们拥有所有的钱，我们拥有权力，我们是骑士，我们有剑，我们有战士，我们可以杀掉任何人，但我们不想整天互相残杀。

sentences.en: We don't have to be Game of Thrones forever.
sentences.zh: 我们不需要永远上演《权力的游戏》。

sentences.en: So we're going to divide up power by voting among ourselves.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要通过在我们之间投票来分配权力。

sentences.en: But then as society goes on and becomes more and more peaceful, that franchise for voting gets spread.
sentences.zh: 但随着社会的发展，变得越来越和平，投票的特权开始普及。

sentences.en: It gets spread to people who don't have land, who don't have power, who may not be able to inflict physical violence.
sentences.zh: 它普及到了那些没有土地、没有权力、可能无法施加物理暴力的人身上。

sentences.en: And then eventually you get to the point where everybody's voting.
sentences.zh: 最终你达到了每个人都在投票的地步。

sentences.en: Everybody's voting. And everybody's voting for candy and fairies and you know all the free things in life and then eventually people start voting to oppress each other the 51 percent in every in any domain vote to suppress the 49s the tyranny the majority but not all of them are willing to back that up with physical power and so you can end up in a situation where people who don't have physical power are using the institutions of the state to control the people who do have physical power as a simple example taking the united states to people who don't have guns voting to disarm the people that do have guns, right?
sentences.zh: 每个人都在投票。每个人都在投票要求糖果、仙女和生活中所有免费的东西，然后人们开始投票压迫彼此。在任何领域，51%的人投票压制49%的人，这就是多数人的暴政。但并非所有人都愿意用物理力量来支持这一点，所以你最终可能会陷入这样一种境地：没有物理力量的人利用国家机器来控制那些拥有物理力量的人。举个简单的例子，在美国，没有枪的人投票解除那些有枪的人的武装，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, if the people who do have guns get coordinated and care enough, you can't do that, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果那些有枪的人协调一致并且足够在意，你是做不到的，对吧？

sentences.en: So I think eventually these societal structures are unstable.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这些社会结构最终是不稳定的。

sentences.en: They break down. And they break down because eventually the people who have the power and say, no, wait a minute, you don't get to vote.
sentences.zh: 它们会崩溃。崩溃的原因是，最终那些拥有权力的人会说，等等，你不能投票。

sentences.en: You only got to vote because you had power and now you don't have power and you're somehow trying to vote.
sentences.zh: 你之所以能投票是因为你曾经拥有权力，而现在你没有权力了，却还想通过投票来行事。

sentences.en: All of nature, all of society, all of capitalism, all of human endeavors are underpinned by physical violence.
sentences.zh: 大自然的一切、社会的一切、资本主义的一切、人类的一切努力，都是以物理暴力为基础的。

sentences.en: And that is very hard truth to swallow and hard to get away from.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很难接受的残酷真相，也很难摆脱。

sentences.en: Nature is red in tooth and claw. If you don't fight, you don't survive, you don't live, you die.
sentences.zh: 大自然是血腥残酷的。如果你不战斗，你就无法生存，你就活不下去，你就会死。

sentences.en: And that's true of everything alive today.
sentences.zh: 这对当今所有活着的东西都是如此。

sentences.en: And humans are no different. So giving up physical power and then thinking you can exercise political power fails, which is why every communist revolution, which is all about equality and Kumbaya and brothers and sisters end up being run by a bunch of thugs.
sentences.zh: 人类也不例外。所以放弃物理力量，然后认为你可以行使政治权力是行不通的，这就是为什么每一场共产主义革命，尽管口号是平等、大同和兄弟姐妹，最终都由一群暴徒来统治。

sentences.en: Because if you don't have a way to divide up the wealth based on merit, then it's always going to be based on power and influence.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你没有一种基于功绩来分配财富的方法，那么它最终总是基于权力和影响力。

sentences.en: The thugs with the guns always win in the end.
sentences.zh: 拿着枪的暴徒最终总是赢家。

sentences.en: So the question is just, can you keep the thugs with the guns paid and happy and successful society where you're allocating based on merit?
sentences.zh: 所以问题仅仅在于，你能不能让拿着枪的暴徒得到报酬、感到满意，并建立一个基于功绩分配的成功社会？

sentences.en: Because if you can't, then you're going to do it based on power.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你做不到，那么你就会基于权力来分配。

sentences.en: So I do think that this battle is not over, but that's because it never stopped.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实认为这场战斗还没有结束，但那是因为它从未停止过。

sentences.en: It's always been there from day one. It will continue.
sentences.zh: 它从第一天起就一直存在，并将持续下去。

sentences.en: Is it a battle to not care about the news in an age of news saturation?
sentences.zh: 在新闻饱和的时代，不去关心新闻是一场战斗吗？

sentences.en: All of this stuff, headlines, 24 hours a day stream directly into your consciousness through a device in your pocket.
sentences.zh: 所有这些东西，头条新闻，每天24小时通过你口袋里的设备直接流向你的意识。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of what we've spoken about today is freedom, freedom from having to think about things or care about things that you do not have control over or that you shouldn't or that you don't want to.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们今天谈论的很多内容都是关于自由，即从那些你无法控制、或者你不应该关心、或者你不想关心的事物中解脱出来。

sentences.en: And yet people are just... like submerged up to the bottom of their nostrils, basically drowning in worry.
sentences.zh: 然而人们却……就像被淹没到了鼻孔处，基本上沉浸在焦虑之中。

sentences.en: So how, yeah, is it, is it a battle to sort of stay out of the news when you're saturated in it?
sentences.zh: 那么，当你被新闻包围时，不去关注新闻是一场战斗吗？

sentences.en: Yeah. I mean, as you're saying, the human brain is not evolved to handle all the world's emergencies breaking in real time and you can't care about everything and you'll go insane if you try.
sentences.zh: 是的。我的意思是，正如你所说，人类大脑的进化并不是为了处理世界上所有实时发生的紧急事件，你不可能关心所有事情，如果你试图这样做，你会疯掉的。

sentences.en: Um, does it mean you shouldn't care at all?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是否意味着你根本不应该关心？

sentences.en: There's no should. I mean, if you want to care, go ahead and care.
sentences.zh: 没有所谓的“应该”。我的意思是，如果你想关心，那就去关心吧。

sentences.en: I would just say that you're probably better off only caring about things that are local or things that you can affect.
sentences.zh: 我只是认为，你最好只关心那些本地的或者你能产生影响的事情。

sentences.en: So if you really care about something that's in the news, then by all means care about it, but make a difference.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你真的关心新闻里的某件事，那就一定要去关心，但要做出改变。

sentences.en: Go do something about it and make sure that it's your overwhelming desire and you don't have five other desires at the same time.
sentences.zh: 去为此做点什么，并确保这是你压倒性的渴望，而且你同时没有其他五个渴望。

sentences.en: Also just realize the consequences of it.
sentences.zh: 也要意识到后果。

sentences.en: You're going to be unhappy until that thing gets fixed and that thing will often be out of your control.
sentences.zh: 在那件事解决之前，你都会不快乐，而那件事往往是你无法控制的。

sentences.en: Desire is a contract to be unhappy until you get what you want, but for the most part, that's something that is in your life.
sentences.zh: 欲望是一份合同，让你在得到想要的东西之前一直处于不快乐的状态，但大多数情况下，那只是你生活中的一部分。

sentences.en: It's like till I lose the weight, until I get the job.
sentences.zh: 就像“直到我减肥成功”、“直到我找到工作”。

sentences.en: You can be outside too. Yeah, if it's until the carbon dioxide parts per million are below this particular number, it's like, that's a...
sentences.zh: 你也可以在外面。是的，如果是“直到二氧化碳浓度低于这个特定数值”，那就像是……

sentences.en: That's a tough one. Or all the people with Trump derangement syndrome, right?
sentences.zh: 这确实是个难题。或者看看那些患有“特朗普错乱综合征”的人，对吧？

sentences.en: He's living rent-free in their heads and driving them insane.
sentences.zh: 特朗普在他们的脑子里免费住着，把他们逼得发疯。

sentences.en: And I get it. I mean, there are politicians who have definitely driven me insane as well.
sentences.zh: 我理解。我的意思是，确实也有政客让我感到抓狂。

sentences.en: But it comes at a very high cost. And it's something that is out of your control that you cannot really influence.
sentences.zh: 但这代价非常高昂。而且这是你无法控制、也无法真正施加影响的事情。

sentences.en: So it's probably good to at least be conscious of it.
sentences.zh: 所以，至少能意识到这一点大概是件好事。

sentences.en: You mentioned historians before. One of my friends has a question.
sentences.zh: 你之前提到了历史学家。我的一位朋友有个问题。

sentences.en: His equivalent of Peter Thiel's question of what is it that you believe that most people would disagree with.
sentences.zh: 他把Peter Thiel那个“你相信什么大多数人不同意的事情”的问题，转化为了自己的版本。

sentences.en: His is, what do you think is currently ignored by the media but will be studied by historians?
sentences.zh: 他问的是：你认为目前被媒体忽视，但未来会被历史学家研究的事情是什么？

sentences.en: You're asking me that question right now?
sentences.zh: 你现在就要问我这个问题吗？

sentences.en: What do I think is ignored by the media but will be studied by historians? well i mean the media is only focused on very timely things right so it depends if you want to talk about timely or timeless right but as a simple example if i just look at things that maybe the next five or ten years that are going to make a massive difference that people are not focused enough on um and i think within two years this will be obvious so like the then i make a prediction and predictions are tough but you're gonna have to eat it in a few yeah i'm gonna have to eat this in a few years so i'm probably wrong but uh two things that i pay attention to um that i don't think uh a lot of people do pay attention to well there's a couple one is i think just how bad modern medicine is i think people just put a lot more faith in modern medicine than is warranted like our best ideas for a lot of things are surgery just cutting things out right uh treating things that are extraneous like oh you don't really need a gallbladder you You don't really need an appendix.
sentences.zh: 你问我什么事被媒体忽视但会被历史学家研究？嗯，媒体只关注非常时效性的事情，所以这取决于你是想谈论时效性的还是永恒的话题。举个简单的例子，如果我只看未来五到十年内会产生巨大影响，但人们关注度不够的事情……嗯，我觉得两年内这就会变得显而易见。所以，如果我要做一个预测——预测很难，而且几年后我可能得为自己的话负责——所以我很可能是错的。但我关注的两件事，我觉得没多少人关注。其中之一是现代医学有多糟糕。我觉得人们对现代医学的信任远超其应有的程度。我们处理很多问题的最佳方案就是手术，就是把东西切掉，处理那些所谓多余的部分，比如‘哦，你其实不需要胆囊，你不需要阑尾’。

sentences.en: So you don't really need tonsils. Oh, that's false.
sentences.zh: ‘你不需要扁桃体’。哦，那是错的。

sentences.en: Suplist requirement. Human body is very, very efficient.
sentences.zh: 这是人体必需的。人体是非常、非常高效的。

sentences.en: All those things are needed. You know, so I think the state of modern medicine is still pretty bad.
sentences.zh: 所有这些器官都是有用的。所以我觉得现代医学的现状依然很糟糕。

sentences.en: We don't have many good explanatory theories in biology.
sentences.zh: 我们在生物学领域没有太多好的解释性理论。

sentences.en: We have germ theory of disease. We have evolution.
sentences.zh: 我们有疾病细菌学说，有进化论。

sentences.en: We have cell theory. We have DNA genetics, morphogenesis, embryogenesis, and not much else.
sentences.zh: 我们有细胞学说，有DNA遗传学、形态发生、胚胎发生，除此之外就没别的了。

sentences.en: You know, there's not much else. Everything else is rules of thumb, memorization, A affects B because it affects C, affects D, but we don't understand the underlying explanation.
sentences.zh: 真的没别的了。其他一切都只是经验法则、死记硬背，A影响B是因为它影响了C，进而影响了D，但我们并不理解背后的根本解释。

sentences.en: It's all just words pointing to words pointing to words.
sentences.zh: 这全都是词汇指向词汇，再指向词汇。

sentences.en: So biology is still in a very sorry state.
sentences.zh: 所以生物学依然处于非常可悲的状态。

sentences.en: And because we are not allowed to take risk that might kill people, we just don't experiment enough in biology.
sentences.zh: 而且因为我们不允许承担可能导致死亡的风险，我们在生物学上实验得不够。

sentences.en: So a lot of treatments are just outright banned by large regulatory bodies.
sentences.zh: 所以很多疗法直接被大型监管机构禁止了。

sentences.en: So we just don't have the innovation. So I think we're still in the stone age when it comes to biology and we've got a long ways to go. and I think people will look back aghast at this and I think this is Brian Johnson's point he's like you know let's be more extreme let's try to live forever let's be more experimental and I'll start as end of one and start experimenting on myself But even there, I disagree with Brian on many things, like, you know, taking huge amounts of supplements.
sentences.zh: 所以我们缺乏创新。我觉得在生物学方面我们还处于石器时代，还有很长的路要走。我觉得人们回头看时会感到震惊。这也是Brian Johnson的观点，他说‘我们要更极端一点，尝试永生，要更具实验性’，他从自己开始，作为一个个体进行实验。但即便如此，我在很多事情上也不同意Brian的看法，比如摄入大量的补剂。

sentences.en: I think we just don't know it's supplements outside of the international context, like just eat liver, man.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在国际背景之外，我们根本不知道补剂的作用，还是吃点肝脏吧，伙计。

sentences.en: Right. But it's fine. And I wouldn't be vegan either.
sentences.zh: 没错。但这没关系。我也不会去当纯素食者。

sentences.en: But, you know, I really appreciate that he's experimenting.
sentences.zh: 不过，我真的很欣赏他在进行实验。

sentences.en: He's good-natured about it. Me too. He shares everything.
sentences.zh: 他对此心态很好。我也是。他分享了一切。

sentences.en: So we need more people like that. So I think the state of biology, people will look back and say, wow, that was in the dark ages. um i think uh another uh another thing that we'll look back on is i think we we still continue to underestimate how important drones are going to be in warfare the future of all warfare is drones there will be nothing else on the battlefield um because i think of the end state of drones as autonomous bullets not even guided autonomous like they're self-directed uh and so if that's the future we're headed towards and that's a it is just why would you have an armed force that's there's gonna be no there's gonna be no aircraft carriers there's gonna be no tanks there's gonna to be no infantrymen.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要更多像他这样的人。所以我认为生物学的现状，人们回头看时会说，哇，那简直是黑暗时代。嗯，我觉得另一件我们回头看时会感叹的事情是，我们依然低估了无人机在战争中的重要性。未来所有的战争都是无人机战争，战场上将不会有其他东西。因为我认为无人机的终极形态就是自主子弹，甚至不是制导的，是自主的，也就是自我导向。如果这是我们前进的未来，那么为什么还要有武装部队？未来将不会有航空母舰，不会有坦克，不会有步兵。

sentences.en: There's just going to be autonomous bullets.
sentences.zh: 只会剩下自主子弹。

sentences.en: Buy autonomous bullets against your autonomous bullets.
sentences.zh: 用你的自主子弹去对抗对方的自主子弹。

sentences.en: Whichever ones win, the other side just surrenders because it's over.
sentences.zh: 哪一方赢了，另一方就投降，因为一切都结束了。

sentences.en: I think that's the second piece of it. I think a third piece that is going to be kind of unexpected is the GLP-1s, which I know you and I have privately discussed before.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是第二点。我觉得第三点可能有点出人意料，那就是GLP-1类药物，我知道你和我私下讨论过。

sentences.en: I think these are the most breakthrough drugs since antibiotics.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是自抗生素以来最具突破性的药物。

sentences.en: They're probably more important than statins.
sentences.zh: 它们可能比他汀类药物更重要。

sentences.en: They're sort of miracle drugs. There are downsides, but the downsides and side effects are so minor compared to the upsides beyond just weight loss.
sentences.zh: 它们算是奇迹药物。虽然有缺点，但相比于除了减肥之外的益处，这些缺点和副作用微不足道。

sentences.en: They also seem to be addiction breakers.
sentences.zh: 它们似乎还能戒除成瘾。

sentences.en: They seem to lower many kinds of cancer.
sentences.zh: 它们似乎能降低多种癌症的风险。

sentences.en: They almost metabolically reverse aging up to a certain point.
sentences.zh: 它们在一定程度上几乎能从代谢层面逆转衰老。

sentences.en: And I think they're going to bend the curve on healthcare costs.
sentences.zh: 我认为它们将改变医疗成本的曲线。

sentences.en: And the big question people are going to be asking over the next five years is why are Americans paying thousands of dollars a month for this when people overseas are getting them for free, or I can order them from China for free or whatever.
sentences.zh: 未来五年人们会问的一个大问题是：为什么美国人每个月要为此支付数千美元，而海外的人却能免费获得，或者我可以从中国免费订购之类的。

sentences.en: And maybe if I were Bernie Sanders, the platform I would be running on is I would say, okay, we're going to pay hundreds of billions of dollars to Novo and Eli Lilly, and we're just going to make these free.
sentences.zh: 如果我是Bernie Sanders，我的竞选纲领就是：好吧，我们要向Novo和Eli Lilly支付数千亿美元，然后让这些药免费。

sentences.en: Or there's hundreds of analogs of these things that work.
sentences.zh: 或者说，市面上还有数百种类似的药物有效。

sentences.en: These are not going to be limited to just the few that are being used today.
sentences.zh: 这些药物不会仅限于今天使用的那几种。

sentences.en: Just take one of them or two of them and make them free.
sentences.zh: 随便拿出一两种让它们免费就行。

sentences.en: And I think it'll make a big difference.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这会产生巨大的影响。

sentences.en: And as you and I were discussing earlier, this does bend a lot of people out of shape who got there the old-fashioned way and they want to see obesity as a moral failing on people's parts and it lowers their status if they are suddenly the signal is less of a signal yeah absolutely yeah so so they're incented to say oh well you don't know the downsides you know it's irresponsible to suggest it's going to cause cancer have fun losing bone and muscle mass by the way none of that stuff is really true the cancer stuff is actually beneficial on i know people who are now taking these things for anti-aging reasons They're already fit, but they just want to age better and have a stronger insulin metabolism.
sentences.zh: 正如我们之前讨论的，这让很多通过老派方式减肥的人感到不舒服，他们想把肥胖看作是个人的道德缺失，如果别人轻易瘦下来，他们的优越感就降低了，信号意义也减弱了。没错，绝对是这样。所以他们有动机说‘哦，你不知道副作用，建议使用是不负责任的，它会导致癌症，祝你骨骼和肌肉流失愉快’。顺便说一句，这些说法都不是真的，癌症方面的研究其实显示它是有益的。我知道有些人现在为了抗衰老而服用这些药物。他们本来就很健康，但他们想老得更好，拥有更强的胰岛素代谢能力。

sentences.en: And there's evidence now that these things are, you know, they put off dementia, Alzheimer's, colon cancer.
sentences.zh: 现在有证据表明这些药物可以推迟痴呆症、阿尔茨海默病、结肠癌。

sentences.en: It's insane, cardiovascular disease. Like the list of benefits is insane.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了，还有心血管疾病。益处清单简直疯狂。

sentences.en: There's no free lunch. But this is a class of drugs that prevents you from taking other drugs into your body.
sentences.zh: 天下没有免费的午餐。但这是一类能防止你摄入其他有害物质的药物。

sentences.en: It prevents you from taking too much sugar, too many calories in an era of abundance, prevents you from smoking, prevents you from even there's an organization called Casper that is now doing a study on heroin addictions.
sentences.zh: 它能防止你在物质过剩的时代摄入过多的糖分和热量，防止你吸烟，甚至还有个叫Casper的组织正在研究它对海洛因成瘾的作用。

sentences.en: And they're showing that it's going to lower opioid overdoses and heroin addictions.
sentences.zh: 他们显示这能降低阿片类药物过量和海洛因成瘾。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of overwhelming medical evidence coming out.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多压倒性的医学证据正在涌现。

sentences.en: And I think, I don't know the exact number, but I think something like 10% of the population might not have tried these things.
sentences.zh: 我想，虽然我不确定确切数字，但大概有10%的人口可能已经尝试过这些药物了。

sentences.en: I think that's the number that I'd seen as well.
sentences.zh: 我想我也看到过这个数字。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's massive. I think it's about 50% of the population say that they would like to try it.
sentences.zh: 是的，规模很大。我觉得大约有50%的人口表示他们想尝试一下。

sentences.en: Exactly. So I think the body positivity movement is dead.
sentences.zh: 没错。所以我认为‘身体积极性’运动已经死了。

sentences.en: And we always kind of knew it was a scam.
sentences.zh: 我们一直都知道那是个骗局。

sentences.en: I mean, it's dying very, very quickly. Yeah, I quipped like you can never be too rich, too thin or too clean.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它正在非常、非常快地消亡。是的，我曾打趣说，人永远不会嫌钱多、嫌瘦或嫌干净。

sentences.en: Right. And immediately, like a whole bunch of people went. nonlinear my mentions, like, what do you mean too thin?
sentences.zh: 没错。然后立刻就有一堆人跳出来。我的评论区炸了，说‘你什么意思，太瘦？’

sentences.en: And what about the hygiene hypothesis? And, you know, obviously there's always exceptions, but people want to be thin and fit and people want to be clean back to the pathogen discussion that we had.
sentences.zh: 还有‘卫生假说’之类的？显然总有例外，但人们就是想变瘦、变健康，人们就是想保持干净，回到我们之前讨论的病原体话题。

sentences.en: Um, so I think overall that there's going to be huge demand for these things.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为总体而言，对这些药物的需求将是巨大的。

sentences.en: And our modern medical system is not built to supply these well.
sentences.zh: 而我们的现代医疗体系并没有为此做好供应准备。

sentences.en: I'm not, I'm not, uh, I don't hold it against the farmers.
sentences.zh: 我并不是在责怪制药公司。

sentences.en: I think the farmers did their job by creating the thing, but I think next we need to step up and figure out how to make it broadly and cheaply available, as opposed to just milk it only for people on obesity who can get Medicare to sign off for it, or people paying out of pocket at very, very high prices.
sentences.zh: 我认为制药公司通过创造这些药物完成了他们的工作，但接下来我们需要站出来，弄清楚如何广泛且廉价地提供这些药物，而不是仅仅为了那些能让医疗保险买单的肥胖患者，或者那些自掏腰包支付高昂价格的人而榨取利润。

sentences.en: The benefits of societal distribution of the safer GLP-1s is so large that whichever politicians tackles that is going to be richly rewarded.
sentences.zh: 社会化分发更安全的GLP-1类药物所带来的益处是巨大的，任何解决这个问题的政客都将获得丰厚的回报。

sentences.en: Well, obesity is the number one source of malnutrition worldwide.
sentences.zh: 嗯，肥胖是全球营养不良的首要来源。

sentences.en: There's twice as many people that are obese than are starving.
sentences.zh: 肥胖人口是饥饿人口的两倍。

sentences.en: So about half a billion people are starving, and a billion people are obese.
sentences.zh: 大约有五亿人在挨饿，而有十亿人肥胖。

sentences.en: And so many problems are downstream of that.
sentences.zh: 很多问题都是由此引发的。

sentences.en: Like, you know, look at how much of the federal budget goes into dialysis because of kidney failure.
sentences.zh: 比如，看看联邦预算中有多少钱花在肾衰竭的透析上。

sentences.en: And why is that? It's because of diabetes, right?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？是因为糖尿病，对吧？

sentences.en: So, so many of the problems that we have in modern society are downstream of obesity.
sentences.zh: 所以，现代社会中许多问题都是肥胖的下游产物。

sentences.en: And you know this, like fitness is so important.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，健身非常重要。

sentences.en: And yes, there's, in some people, these things cause muscle and bone loss, but not in the people who are eating high protein and working out hard.
sentences.zh: 是的，对某些人来说，这些药物会导致肌肉和骨骼流失，但对于那些摄入高蛋白并努力锻炼的人来说则不会。

sentences.en: So they can be taken in a way that's safer.
sentences.zh: 所以只要使用得当，它们是安全的。

sentences.en: And some versions of these, like liraglutide, the original one, they've been around for decades. and the others have been around for about a decade.
sentences.zh: 其中一些版本，比如利拉鲁肽（liraglutide），最初的版本已经存在几十年了，其他的也已经存在了大约十年。

sentences.en: And we already have, as you said, 10% of the population taking them, so they're already quite widely distributed.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，我们已经有10%的人口在使用它们，所以它们已经相当普及了。

sentences.en: It's a good sample size. Yeah, it's a great sample size.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的样本量。是的，这是一个很棒的样本量。

sentences.en: What more do you need? Like if you have a bacterial infection that's eating you, I don't say, oh, I have this antibiotic, but it's going to raise your blood pressure.
sentences.zh: 你还需要什么？如果你有细菌感染正在吞噬你，我不会说‘哦，我有这种抗生素，但它会升高你的血压’。

sentences.en: It's like, no, take the antibiotic. If you're going to kill yourself, I say take this antipsychotic and stay alive a little longer and solve it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不，吃抗生素吧。如果你要自杀，我会说吃这种抗精神病药，多活一会儿，然后再解决问题。

sentences.en: I don't say, oh, it's going to cause your heart rate to go up by three beats a minute.
sentences.zh: 我不会说‘哦，它会让你的心率每分钟增加三次’。

sentences.en: I don't worry about that. So similarly, if you're poisoning yourself with toxins and overuse of substances that you shouldn't be using, either heroin, alcohol, cigarettes, sugar, or just sheer calories, take this GLP-1.
sentences.zh: 我对此并不担心。同样地，如果你正因毒素或滥用不该使用的物质——无论是海洛因、酒精、香烟、糖，还是单纯的热量过剩——而毒害自己，那就服用这种GLP-1药物吧。

sentences.en: They also improve digestion. You just have less food matter going through your stomach.
sentences.zh: 它们还能改善消化。你胃里通过的食物残渣会变少。

sentences.en: They lower cancer risks across the board.
sentences.zh: 它们能全面降低患癌风险。

sentences.en: There's quite a few cancers that are lower.
sentences.zh: 确实有相当多的癌症风险会降低。

sentences.en: Cardiovascular, I mean, I don't know what else to tell you.
sentences.zh: 心血管方面，我的意思是，我不知道还能告诉你什么。

sentences.en: I've been very surprised by the negative reception. whenever you have a conversation about glp1s and i think a lot of it may be people who well think about how many sacred cows are being gored right all the people who are basically saying uh you should work harder you should be fit like i did right it's lowering their status think about all the nutritionists and doctors and trainers who are now being you know it's too easy they're being put out of business in a way right uh it's kind of like why does the american military keep buying aircraft carriers, right?
sentences.zh: 我对负面评价感到非常惊讶。每当你谈论GLP-1时，我想其中很大一部分原因可能是人们——嗯，想想有多少“神圣不可侵犯的观念”正在被打破吧，对吧？那些基本上在说“你应该更努力工作，你应该像我一样保持健康”的人，这降低了他们的地位。想想那些营养学家、医生和教练，他们现在被认为——你知道，这太容易了——他们某种程度上正在失业，对吧？这有点像为什么美国军方还在不断购买航空母舰，对吧？

sentences.en: In the age of drones, there's an incentive bias.
sentences.zh: 在无人机时代，这存在一种激励偏差。

sentences.en: There's a very strong motivated reasoning, but it doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 这背后有非常强烈的动机性推理，但这并不重要。

sentences.en: 10% people are on it. Everybody wants to be fit.
sentences.zh: 10%的人正在使用它。每个人都想保持健康。

sentences.en: It's going to spread like wildfire. I was just thinking as you were talking that, you know, when we think about health and a lot of people kind of get captured by the way that they were brought up, the habits that they had from their childhood or what mom and dad did or genetic predisposition and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 它会像野火一样蔓延。你刚才说话的时候我正在想，你知道，当我们思考健康时，很多人会被他们的成长方式、童年养成的习惯、父母的做法或遗传倾向等因素所束缚。

sentences.en: I think you have as many reasons as many people to sort of feel hard done by challenges that you had earlier on in your life.
sentences.zh: 我认为你和许多人一样，有足够的理由对早年生活中遇到的挑战感到委屈。

sentences.en: Is getting past your past a skill, sort of not being owned today by your history, sort of not having that victimhood mentality?
sentences.zh: 摆脱过去是一种技能吗？比如不被历史所左右，不持有那种受害者心态？

sentences.en: Yeah, I did have a tough childhood, but I don't think about it.
sentences.zh: 是的，我确实有一个艰难的童年，但我不会去想它。

sentences.en: I think there are a couple of things going on there.
sentences.zh: 我认为这其中有几件事在起作用。

sentences.en: One is, I did process it quite a bit. I thought about it, but I thought about it to get rid of it.
sentences.zh: 一是，我确实处理过它。我思考过它，但我思考它是为了摆脱它。

sentences.en: I didn't think about it to dwell on it or to...
sentences.zh: 我思考它不是为了沉溺其中，或者……

sentences.en: Yeah, I wanted to be successful. I wanted more than anything else to rise past that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想成功。我比任何事情都更想超越过去。

sentences.en: And so I couldn't have that as a burden on me.
sentences.zh: 所以我不能让它成为我的负担。

sentences.en: So I had to get rid of it. So to the extent that I dealt with it, it was for the express purpose of getting rid of it, not to create an identity or story or to reflect upon it, or to say, look at me, look at what I've accomplished and look how great I am and what I've done.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须摆脱它。因此，我处理它的程度，完全是为了摆脱它，而不是为了创造一个身份、故事，或者反思它，又或者说“看看我，看看我取得了什么成就，看看我有多棒，我做了什么”。

sentences.en: So I got rid of it. And I think at some point you wrestle with that thing and then you just realize like you're never going to untangle the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 所以我摆脱了它。我认为在某个时刻，你与那件事搏斗，然后你就会意识到，你永远无法理清整件事。

sentences.en: It's a Gordian knot problem. Like Alexander, you know, found that tangled knot in India and it said, oh, the famous conqueror will come and will untie this knot.
sentences.zh: 这是一个“戈耳狄俄斯之结”的问题。就像亚历山大在印度发现了那个纠缠的结，传说伟大的征服者会来解开这个结。

sentences.en: Nobody else can untie the knot. And he took one look at it, pulled out a sword and just cut it.
sentences.zh: 没人能解开那个结。他看了一眼，拔出剑直接砍断了它。

sentences.en: So at some point you just have to cut your past.
sentences.zh: 所以在某个时刻，你必须砍断你的过去。

sentences.en: If your past is bothering you, you will eventually get tired of trying to untangle that knot and you will just drop it because you will realize life is short.
sentences.zh: 如果你的过去困扰着你，你最终会厌倦试图解开那个结，你会直接放弃它，因为你会意识到生命是短暂的。

sentences.en: And the more you want to accomplish in this life, actually, the less time you have to unravel that thing.
sentences.zh: 而且，你在这辈子想完成的事情越多，实际上你解开那件事的时间就越少。

sentences.en: So I just wanted to actually get things done.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是想把事情做完。

sentences.en: So I had no time to deal with it. So I just cut it.
sentences.zh: 所以我没时间去处理它。所以我直接砍断了它。

sentences.en: It's like a really bad relationship. But in this case, it's a bad relationship with your own history.
sentences.zh: 这就像一段非常糟糕的关系。但在这种情况下，这是与你自己历史的一段糟糕关系。

sentences.en: So you just drop it. Yeah, I think so much of what we've spoken about today is on the shortness of life and the fact that every moment is precious. you had to take about the most fundamental resource in your life is not time, it's attention.
sentences.zh: 所以你直接放弃它。是的，我想我们今天谈论的很多内容都是关于生命的短暂，以及每一刻都很珍贵的事实。你曾提到生命中最基本的资源不是时间，而是注意力。

sentences.en: That's right. I used to think, you know, the currency of life, right?
sentences.zh: 没错。我曾经认为，你知道，这是生命的货币，对吧？

sentences.en: People think it's money. And yes, money is important.
sentences.zh: 人们认为那是金钱。是的，金钱很重要。

sentences.en: And it does let you trade certain things for time, but it doesn't really buy your time.
sentences.zh: 它确实让你能用某些东西交换时间，但它并不能真正买到你的时间。

sentences.en: Ask Warren Buffett how much time money can buy you or Michael Bloomberg.
sentences.zh: 问问Warren Buffett或Michael Bloomberg，金钱能为他们买到多少时间。

sentences.en: They're, you know, Rich is Scrooge and Chris's, but they can't buy more time, right?
sentences.zh: 他们是富有的守财奴，但他们买不到更多时间，对吧？

sentences.en: Brian Johnson, notwithstanding. So you can't trade money for time.
sentences.zh: Brian Johnson的情况除外。所以你不能用金钱交换时间。

sentences.en: Money is not the real currency of life.
sentences.zh: 金钱不是生命的真正货币。

sentences.en: And time itself doesn't even mean that much because as we talked about before, a lot of time can be wasted because you're not really present for it.
sentences.zh: 而且时间本身甚至没有那么重要，因为正如我们之前谈到的，很多时间会被浪费掉，因为你并没有真正活在当下。

sentences.en: You're not paying attention. So the real currency of life is attention.
sentences.zh: 你没有集中注意力。所以生命的真正货币是注意力。

sentences.en: It's what you choose to pay attention to and what you do about it.
sentences.zh: 是你选择关注什么，以及你对此做了什么。

sentences.en: And so back to the point about the news media, you can put your attention on the news but that's how you're spending the real currency of life so just be aware of that if you want to that's fine there's no there's no right or wrong here like maybe it is your destiny to pick something in the news learn about that problem adopt that problem and solve it but just be careful because your attention is the only thing that you have and that can also be captured by your own past yes you can fritter it away on anything you like is there an advantage to starting out as a loser absolutely yeah yeah because if you're because if you're a loser then you'll want to be a winner and then you'll develop all the characteristics that'll help you be a you know quote-unquote winner in life that said i wouldn't sentence my kids to it like i don't think you can artificially do that you know it's sort of like imagine that you were you know 300 years ago you're born a surf and then somehow you managed to escape off the farm and you become a landowner and then eventually you become minor nobility an aristocrat.
sentences.zh: 所以回到新闻媒体的话题，你可以把注意力放在新闻上，但那就是你在消耗生命真正货币的方式，所以如果你想这样做，请意识到这一点。这没问题，没有所谓的对错，也许你的命运就是去关注新闻中的某件事，了解那个问题，接纳那个问题并解决它，但要小心，因为你的注意力是你拥有的唯一东西，它也可能被你自己的过去所俘获。是的，你可以把它浪费在任何你喜欢的事情上。从失败者开始有优势吗？绝对有。因为如果你是一个失败者，你就会想成为赢家，然后你就会培养出所有能帮助你成为——你知道，所谓的——人生赢家特质。话虽如此，我不会让我的孩子们经历这些，我不认为你可以人为地做到这一点。你知道，这就像想象一下，300年前你出生为一个农奴，然后你以某种方式设法逃离了农场，成为了地主，最终成为了小贵族。

sentences.en: Are you going to put your kids back on the farm and say you're going to be a surf again?
sentences.zh: 你会把你的孩子送回农场，说你要再次成为农奴吗？

sentences.en: I know they all like those stories. The kids themselves like those stories because it says, I came from the school of hard knocks.
sentences.zh: 我知道他们都喜欢那些故事。孩子们自己喜欢那些故事，因为它说，“我来自艰苦的环境”。

sentences.en: My dad made me go shovel hay for a summer.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸让我去铲了一个夏天的干草。

sentences.en: It's not real. I mean, you're not going to trick them.
sentences.zh: 那不是真的。我的意思是，你骗不了他们。

sentences.en: I think all you can do is kind of cultivate an appreciation and gratitude for what you have.
sentences.zh: 我认为你所能做的就是培养对你所拥有的东西的欣赏和感激。

sentences.en: And the only way to do that is just evidence it yourself, right?
sentences.zh: 而做到这一点的唯一方法就是你自己去践行，对吧？

sentences.en: Just show yourself how you spend money, how you respect it, what you do with it, how you take care of people, who you're responsible for.
sentences.zh: 展示你自己是如何花钱的，如何尊重它，你用它做什么，你如何照顾他人，你对谁负责。

sentences.en: And the more resources you have, the greater the tribe you can take care of, the more of the tribe you can take care of.
sentences.zh: 你拥有的资源越多，你能照顾的部落就越大，你能照顾的部落成员就越多。

sentences.en: So when you have no resources, you're struggling to take care of yourself.
sentences.zh: 所以当你没有资源时，你在努力照顾自己。

sentences.en: And at that point, it's good to be selfish because you can't save somebody else if you can't even save yourself.
sentences.zh: 在那一点上，自私一点是好的，因为如果你连自己都救不了，你就救不了别人。

sentences.en: Yes. So you take care of yourself and you become the best version of yourself.
sentences.zh: 是的。所以你照顾好自己，成为最好的自己。

sentences.en: But there are too many men who are able, fit. and have some money who are doing nothing with their lives.
sentences.zh: 但有太多有能力、健康且有钱的男人，他们的生活却一事无成。

sentences.en: They're just sitting at home doing nothing, just indulging in themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们只是坐在家里什么也不做，沉溺于自我。

sentences.en: Maybe they go on dates and they get DoorDash.
sentences.zh: 也许他们去约会，然后点外卖。

sentences.en: Like I have no respect for that. I think there's nothing worse in society than a lazy man because he's sort of leaving it all on the table.
sentences.zh: 我对那种行为毫无尊重。我认为社会上没有比懒汉更糟糕的事情了，因为他基本上放弃了一切。

sentences.en: He's leaving his potential on the table.
sentences.zh: 他放弃了自己的潜力。

sentences.en: It's bad for him. So the next thing you do is you go and you have a family and you take care of your family, you take care of that tribe.
sentences.zh: 这对他是坏事。所以你接下来要做的是组建家庭，照顾你的家人，照顾那个部落。

sentences.en: Then you take care of your extended family, you take care of your cousins, brothers, uncles, grandmothers, aunts, sisters, everybody that you can. and then if you have more resources beyond that then you go take care of your local tribe you take care of your people you start trying to do some good for the world and if you have more resources than that you go take care of an even bigger tribe and that's how you earn both respect and self-confidence and you live up to your potential so the the more you have the more is rightfully expected of you and i think it's a good compact with society when highly capable people express and flex that capability by giving more and more and by doing more and more and society rewards them with the one thing they can't get otherwise, which is status.
sentences.zh: 然后你照顾你的大家庭，照顾你的堂表亲、兄弟、叔叔、祖母、阿姨、姐妹，所有你能照顾的人。如果在此之外你还有更多资源，那么你就去照顾你的当地部落，照顾你的人民，开始尝试为世界做点好事。如果你拥有的资源比那还多，你就去照顾一个更大的部落，这就是你赢得尊重和自信的方式，你才能发挥出你的潜力。所以你拥有的越多，人们理所当然对你的期望就越高。我认为当高能力的人通过给予更多、做更多来表达和展示这种能力时，这与社会达成了一种良好的契约，而社会则用他们无法通过其他方式获得的东西来奖励他们，那就是地位。

sentences.en: So society should give you status in exchange for it.
sentences.zh: 所以社会应该以此为交换给予你地位。

sentences.en: They should say, okay, you did a good job.
sentences.zh: 他们应该说，好吧，你做得很好。

sentences.en: You took care of more people than just yourself and just the people immediately around you.
sentences.zh: 你照顾的人不仅仅是你自己和你身边的人。

sentences.en: And that's what an alpha male to me is. An alpha male is not the one who gets to eat first.
sentences.zh: 这就是我心目中的Alpha男性。Alpha男性不是那个先吃饭的人。

sentences.en: The alpha male eats last. The alpha male feeds everybody else first and then gets to eat last.
sentences.zh: Alpha男性最后吃饭。Alpha男性先喂饱所有人，然后自己最后吃。

sentences.en: And they do that out of their own self-respect and pride.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做是出于自尊和骄傲。

sentences.en: And the society rewards them by calling them an alpha and giving them status.
sentences.zh: 社会通过称他们为Alpha并给予他们地位来奖励他们。

sentences.en: I wonder whether some of the pushback that we've got against rich, wealthy, powerful people is disincentivizing.
sentences.zh: 我想知道我们对富有、有权势的人的一些抵制是否起到了反作用。

sentences.en: It is. Who was it? Zuck who donated money to Zuckerberg General's Hospital and they wanted to pull his name off of it.
sentences.zh: 确实是。是谁来着？Zuckerberg向Zuckerberg综合医院捐了钱，然后他们想把他的名字从上面撤下来。

sentences.en: I didn't see that, but that's ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 我没看到那个，但这太荒谬了。

sentences.en: Yeah, that kind of stuff backfires, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，那种事情会适得其反，对吧？

sentences.en: You should reward people for doing- What were you saying before?
sentences.zh: 你应该奖励人们做——你刚才说什么？

sentences.en: You don't just need to, in fact, actually actively avoid castigating people if you want their behavior to change when they get something wrong, look at reinforcing it when they get something right.
sentences.zh: 你不仅需要，事实上，如果你想改变人们做错事时的行为，你应该积极避免指责他们，而是在他们做对时给予强化。

sentences.en: It's happening at a societal level as well.
sentences.zh: 这在社会层面也在发生。

sentences.en: Correct. I mean, like the guys who make a lot of money and go out and buy sports teams, I wouldn't do that, right?
sentences.zh: 没错。我的意思是，那些赚了很多钱然后去买运动队的人，我不会那样做，对吧？

sentences.en: But the one who goes out and builds a hospital or builds a rocket to take people to the moon, you know, rescue some astronauts, you should be rewarding him for that.
sentences.zh: 但那个去建造医院或制造火箭把人们送上月球，你知道，营救宇航员的人，你应该为此奖励他。

sentences.en: Naval, I really appreciate you. I hope that this has lived up to whatever weird daydreams you've been having.
sentences.zh: Naval，我真的很感激你。我希望这达到了你一直以来的那些奇怪白日梦的要求。

sentences.en: What have you got coming up? what can people expect from you over the next however long expect nothing that's the most naval way that we could have finished this dude it's uh it's been a long time coming and i really do appreciate you for being here today but i do hope to deliver something oh i think you have so thank you thanks for having me thank you too thanks for getting in my mind and hopefully now you're out we'll see i might be even worse now you've got the real memories to stick i don't know the reason to win the game is to be free of it the reason the reason to do the podcast Just to be done with it.
sentences.zh: 你接下来有什么计划？人们在接下来的这段时间里可以期待你做些什么？什么都不要期待。这是我们结束这次谈话最“Naval”的方式了。伙计，这真是期待已久，我真的很感谢你今天能来。但我确实希望能交付一些东西。哦，我想你已经做到了，所以谢谢你。谢谢你的邀请。也谢谢你。感谢你进入我的思想，希望现在你已经出来了。我们会看到的，你现在可能更糟了。你有了真正的记忆，我不知道。赢得游戏的理由是摆脱它。做播客的理由，只是为了把它做完。

sentences.en: All right. Wow, you made it to the end. Congratulations.
sentences.zh: 好了。哇，你坚持到了最后。恭喜。

sentences.en: Well, if you enjoyed that, you're going to love my full-length conversation with the one and only Alain de Botton from the School of Life right here.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果你喜欢这个，你会喜欢我与来自School of Life的Alain de Botton进行的完整对话，就在这里。

sentences.en: Go on. Press it.
sentences.zh: 去吧。点击它。
